akhfash:1-1.t: He said: ﴿غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي ٱلصَّيْدِ﴾ — ﴿أَوْفُواْ بِٱلْعُقُودِ﴾ ﴿غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي ٱلصَّيْدِ﴾: (غيرَ) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

akhfash:2-2.t:
[And] He said ﴿لاَ تُحِلُّواْ شَعَآئِرَ ٱللَّهِ﴾; its singular is "شعيرة" (rite).
 [And] He said ﴿وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ﴾: "الشَنَئانُ" (hatred) is vowelled [in its second letter], like "الدَرَجان" and "المَيَلان"; it is from "شَنِئْتُه" (I hated him), so "أنا أشنَؤه" "شَنَئاناً". And He said ﴿لاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ﴾, i.e. let it not make it right (lawful) for you; because His saying ﴿لاَ جَرَمَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلْنَّارَ﴾ is only "it is true (ḥaqq) that theirs is the Fire". The poet said [in the kāmil metre; this is the one hundred and eightieth shāhid]:
وَلَقَدْ طَعَنْتُ أَبّا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً * جَرَمَتْ فَزارَةُ بَعْدَها أَنْ يَغْضَبُوا
(I struck Abū ʿUyayna a thrust after which it became right for Fazāra to be angry.)
i.e. it was made right for them.
And His saying ﴿أَن صَدُّوكُمْ﴾ means "because they barred you". It has also been read ﴿إِنْ صَدُّوكُم﴾ in the sense of "if they bar you", i.e. "if they do [it]", i.e. if they intend* [it] and have not yet done it. You may also say that when they have already done it, as though you were relating what had not happened; as in the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿قَالُوۤاْ إِن يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾, when in their view the theft had already taken place.
And He said ﴿أَن تَعْتَدُواْ﴾, i.e. let not hatred of a people make it right for you to transgress, i.e. let that not drive you to aggression. Then He said ﴿وَتَعَاوَنُواْ عَلَى ٱلْبرِّ وَٱلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾.

akhfash:3-3.t:
And He said ﴿وَٱلْمَوْقُوذَةُ﴾, from (وُقِذَتْ) (it was beaten to death), so "هِيَ مَوْقُوذَةٌ".
﴿وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ﴾ has the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] because it has been made like a noun, like "أَكِيلَةِ الأَسَدِ" (the lion's prey). [Otherwise] you would say "هِيَ أَكِيلٌ" and "هِيَ نَطِيحٌ", because whatever has [the sense of] "مَفْعُولَة", its "فَعِيل" is without the hāʾ, e.g. "القَتيِل" (slain) and "الصَريع" (felled) when you mean a woman, and "هِيَ جَريحٌ" (she is wounded), because you say "مَجْرُوحَةٌ".
And He said ﴿وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ﴾; in one dialect they lighten it to "السَبْع".
﴿وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ﴾: its plural is "الأنْصاب".
﴿وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُواْ بِٱلأَزْلاَمِ﴾ means: "and that is forbidden"; its singular is "زُلَم" and "زَلَمَ" (divining arrow).
And He said ﴿مَخْمَصَةٍ﴾: you say "خَمَصَهُ الجُوع" (hunger emptied his belly); [مَخْمَصة] is like "المَغْضَبَة", because He meant the maṣdar (verbal noun).
[And He said] ﴿يَئِسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾ with hamza on the second yāʾ; it is of [the pattern] "فَعِل", "يَفْعِل". Giving kasra to the first yāʾ is a dialect usage, as with "لِعْبَ": some of them give kasra to the lām and the ʿayn, and they also make the ʿayn unvowelled while giving the lām fatḥa or kasra; and likewise "يئس". That is because when "فعل" has as its second letter one of the six [guttural] letters, they give its first letter kasra and leave it with kasra, as they do in "فعيل", e.g. "شِعير" and "صِهيل". Some of them make [the second] unvowelled and give the first kasra, as in "رِحْمَهُ اللهُ"; therefore you say "يِئْسَ", giving the yāʾ kasra and making the hamza unvowelled. [Translator's note: the text has «تسكر الياء», evidently for «تكسر الياء» "you give the yāʾ kasra".] This verse has been read ﴿نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ﴾ according to that dialect in which they say "لِعِبَ". And some people say "نَعِمَ الرَّجُلُ زَيْدٌ"; it is permissible to give kasra to this nūn in "نَعِمَ", because what follows it is one of the six letters, just as "لِعِب" was given kasra. As for their saying that the ʿayn of "نِعِمّا" is unvowelled when assimilated, it is a mistake, because two unvowelled letters do not meet. But if you wish, you may make it covert (ikhfāʾ), putting it between assimilation and full pronunciation, so that it has the weight of a vowelled letter, just as ﴿إِنِّي لَيَحْزُنُنِيۤ﴾ was read with the first nūn given a trace (ishmām) of the ḍamma.
And He said ﴿ٱلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ﴾, because Islam [still] had some obligations [to come]; when Allah had completed what He willed of it, He said ﴿ٱلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ﴾ ﴿وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلأِسْلاَمَ دِيناً﴾ — not in any sense other than this.
And He said ﴿فَمَنِ ٱضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٍ لإِثْمٍ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾, as if He said: "then Allah is Forgiving, Merciful to him", as you say "عبدُ اللهِ ضَرَبْتُ" (ʿAbdullāh, I struck) meaning: I struck him. The poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-first shāhid]:
ثَلاثٌ كُلُّهُنَّ قتلتُ عَمْداً * فَأَخْزَى اللهُ رابعَةً تَعُود
(Three — all of them I killed deliberately; may Allah disgrace a fourth that returns.)
And another said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-second shāhid]:
قدْ أَصْبَحَتْ أُمُ الخِيارِ تَدَّعي * عَلَيَّ ذَنْباً كُلَّهُ لَمْ أَصْنعِ
(Umm al-Khiyār has come to accuse me of a sin, all of which I did not commit.)

akhfash:4-4.t:
And He said ﴿مَاذَآ أُحِلَّ﴾: if you wish, you take "ذا" as having the status of "الذي" (that which), and if you wish, you take it as zāʾida (redundant), as the poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-third shāhid]: 
يا خُزْرَ تَغْلِبَ ماذا بالُ نِسْوَتِكُم * لا يَسْتَفِقنَ الى الدَيْرَيْنَ تَحْنانا
(O squint-eyed ones of Taghlib, what is the matter with your women, who never cease yearning for the two monasteries?)
"ذا" can only be zāʾida here, [since] if you said "ما الذي بال نسوتكم" it would not be [proper] speech. 
[And] He said ﴿ٱلْجَوَارِحِ﴾: these are the earners (hunting animals), as you say "فُلانٌ جارِحَةُ أَهْلِهِ" (so-and-so is the earner of his family) and "مالَهُمْ جارِحَةٌ", i.e. they have no slaves "ولا حافِرَةْ" (nor beasts of burden).
[And] He said ﴿كُلُواْ مِمَّآ أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: [so] He put in ﴿مِنْ﴾, as He put it in [one's] saying "كانَ مِنْ حَديث" (there was some talk) and "قَدْ كانَ مِنْ مَطَرٍ" (there has been some rain); and His saying ﴿وَيُكَفِّرُ عَنكُم مِّن سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ﴾ and ﴿يُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن جِبَالٍ فِيهَا مِن بَرَدٍ﴾, which according to one explanation is "He sends down from the sky mountains in which there is hail". Some said ﴿وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن جِبَالٍ فِيهَا مِن بَرَدٍ﴾ [means]: in the sky are mountains of hail, i.e. He makes the mountains of hail in the sky, and makes the sending down from them.

akhfash:5-5.t:
And He said ﴿مُحْصِنِينَ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحِينَ وَلاَ مُتَّخِذِيۤ أَخْدَانٍ﴾: by it He means the men. 
And He said ﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَاتُ﴾ (and) there are made lawful ﴿لَكُمْ المُحْصنات﴾ of the women ﴿مُحْصِنِينَ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحِينَ﴾, i.e. they are made lawful for you in this state.

akhfash:6-6.t:
And He said ﴿وَٱمْسَحُواْ بِرُؤُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾: in the reading of some, He referred it back to "washing", because He had said ﴿فٱغْسِلُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾. And some read ﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾ as [referring to] wiping, i.e. and wipe your feet; this, people do not recognise. [Translator's note: the second reading is evidently meant to be the genitive «وَأَرْجُلِكُمْ», as the explanation shows; the text repeats the accusative form.] Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Wiping the two feet suffices." The genitive is permissible by proximity-agreement (itbāʿ) while in meaning it is "washing", as in "هذا جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ" (this is the ruined hole of a lizard, with "ruined" in the genitive next to "lizard"). The accusative is safer and better than this forced usage. Like it is the Arabs' saying "أَكَلْتُ خبزا ولبنا" (I ate bread and milk), though milk is not eaten; and they say "ماسَمِعْتُ برائحةٍ اطيبَ من هذهِ ولا رأيتُ رائحةً أطيبَ من هذِه" (I have not heard of a scent better than this, nor seen a scent better than this), and "ما رأيتُ كلاماً أصوبَ من هذا" (I have not seen speech more correct than this). The poet said [in the majzūʾ al-kāmil metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-fourth shāhid]: 
يا لَيْتَ زَوجَكِ قَدْ غَدا * مُتَقَلِّداً سَيْفاً وَرُمْحاً 
(Would that your husband had gone out in the morning girded with a sword and a spear.) [i.e. a spear is not "girded", but carried.]
And like it is ﴿لاَ تُحِلُّواْ شَعَآئِرَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ [2] ﴿وَلاۤ آمِّينَ ٱلْبَيْتَ ٱلْحَرَامَ﴾ [2].
And He said ﴿مَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْ حَرَجٍ﴾, i.e. Allah does not will to place upon you hardship.

akhfash:9-9.t: And He said: ﴿وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾: it is as if He explained the promise in order to make clear what He promised them, i.e. thus He promised them, and He said ﴿لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾.

akhfash:12-12.t: [And He said] ﴿وَقَالَ ٱللَّهُ إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ لَئِنْ أَقَمْتُمُ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَآتَيْتُمْ ٱلزَّكَاةَ وَآمَنتُمْ بِرُسُلِي﴾ ﴿لأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ﴾: the first lām is in the sense of an oath, and the second is for another oath.

akhfash:14-14.t: And He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ إِنَّا نَصَارَىٰ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَهُمْ﴾, as you say "مِنْ عبدِ اللهِ أخَذْتُ دِرْهَمَه" (from ʿAbdullāh I took his dirham).

akhfash:22-22.t: [And] He said ﴿إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوْماً جَبَّارِينَ﴾: He made ﴿إِنَّ﴾ govern "القوم" and made "جَبْارِينَ" its qualifier, because ﴿فِيها﴾ is not a noun.

akhfash:26-26.t: [And] He said ﴿فَلاَ تَأْسَ عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْفَاسِقِينَ﴾: it is from "أَسَي", "يَأْسىَ", "أَسَىَ شَدِيداً", which is grief. And "يَئِسَ" is from "اليَأس" (despair), which is the cutting off of hope, from "يَئِسوا"; and His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَيْأَسُواْ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is from the cutting off of hope; it is from "يئست", and is like "إِيٍس" in its conjugation, or if you wish, like "خَشِيْتُ" in its conjugation. As for "أسَوْتَ", "تَأْسُوا", "أَسْواً", it is treating a wound. And "أُسْتُ", "أَؤُوسُ", "أَوْساً" is in the sense of: I gave. "أُسْتُ" is on the analogy of "قُلْتُ", and "أَسَوْتُ" [is on the analogy of] "غَزَوْتُ".

akhfash:27-27.t: [And] He said ﴿وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ٱبْنَيْ آدَمَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾: the hamza belongs to "نَبَأ", because it is from "أَنْبَاتُهُ" (I informed him). The alif of "ابْنَيْ" goes [in pronunciation] because it is a connecting alif (alif waṣl) in the diminutive. [Translator's note: «في التصغير» "in the diminutive" is as written; it may be a corruption, perhaps of «في الدَّرْج» "in continuous speech".] When you pause, [you say] "نبأ" short, and you do not say "نبا", because it is the first term of an iḍāfa, so the alif is not retained in it*.

akhfash:30-30.t: And He said ﴿فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ﴾, like "فَطَوَّعَتْ", meaning: "it made [it] seem permissible (rakhkhaṣat)". And you say "طَوَّقْتُهُ إمْريِ", i.e. I bound him with it. [Translator's note: the text compares «فطوّعت» with itself, and «طوّقته إمري» appears corrupt; translated as written.]

akhfash:31-31.t: And He said ﴿أَعَجَزْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْغُرَابِ فَأُوَارِيَ﴾: ﴿فَأُوَارِيَ﴾ is accusative because you have conjoined it with fāʾ to [the verb after] ﴿أَنْ﴾. It does not have hamza, because it is from "وَارَيْتُ" (I concealed). And it is ﴿عَجَزْتُ﴾ [with fatḥa on the jīm] only because it is from "عَجَزَ", "يَعْجِزُ"; some say "عَجَزَ", "يَعْجُزُ", and "عَجِزَ", "يَعْجَزُ".

akhfash:32-32.t:
[And] He said ﴿مِنْ أَجْلِ ذٰلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾. If you wish, you drop the hamza of ﴿أَجْلِ﴾ and give the nūn its vowel, in the dialect of those who lighten the hamza. "الأَجْلُ" is wrongdoing (jināya), from "أَجَلَ", "يَأْجِلُ"; you say "قَدْ أَجَلْتَ عَلَيْنٰا شَرْاً" (you have brought evil upon us). Some Arabs say ﴿مِنْ جَرّا﴾, from "الجَريرة" (crime), putting it on [the pattern] "فَعْلَى".
And He said ﴿أَنَّهُ مَن قَتَلَ نَفْساً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾, meaning: "or without corruption in the land".

akhfash:36-36.t: And He said ﴿لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَّا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لِيَفْتَدُواْ بِهِ مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ مَا تُقُبِّلَ مِنْهُمْ﴾, meaning: "if they had this with them for ransom, it would not be accepted from them".

akhfash:41-41.t:
And He said ﴿لاَ يَحْزُنكَ﴾, light, with fatḥa on the yāʾ; the people of Medina read ﴿يُحْزِنْكَ﴾, taking it from "أحْزَنَ". The Arabs say "أَحْزَنْتُه" and "حَزَنْتُهُ" (I grieved him).
And He said ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي ٱلْكُفْرِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوۤاْ آمَنَّا بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾, i.e. "from these and from these"; then He said, as a new start, ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ﴾, i.e. they are listeners. And if you wish, you take it with ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هِادُواْ﴾ ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ﴾ and then cut it off from the first speech. Then He said ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ﴾, according to that nominative of the first. As for His saying ﴿لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾, here the speech is cut off, and the meaning is: "and among those who are Jews are listeners to falsehood — they listen to the speech of the Prophet ﷺ in order to lie about him — listeners for another people who have not yet come to you", meaning: "they listen on their behalf and inform them, while they have not come to you".

akhfash:45-45.t: And He said ﴿وَٱلْجُرُوحَ قِصَاصٌ﴾: if it is conjoined to what follows "أَنَّ", it is accusative, and the nominative is as a mubtadaʾ (subject), as you say "إنَّ زَيْداً منْطَلِقٌ وعَمْرٌ ذاهبٌ" (Zayd is leaving and ʿAmr is going); and if you wish, you say "وَعَمْراً ذاهبٌ" — accusative and nominative.

akhfash:46-46.t: [And] He said ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ ٱلإِنجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدًى وَنُورٌ﴾ [with a masculine pronoun], because some say "هِيَ الإِنْجيل" (it [fem.] is the Gospel) and some say "هُوَ الإِنجيل" (it [masc.] is the Gospel). It may also be because "the Gospel" is a book, so it is masculine in meaning, and they made it masculine on that basis — as He said ﴿وَإِذَا حَضَرَ ٱلْقِسْمَةَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾ and then said ﴿فَٱرْزُقُوهُمْ مِّنْهُ﴾, using the masculine, while "القِسْمَةُ" (the division) is feminine, because in meaning it is "the inheritance" and "the wealth", so He used the masculine on that basis.

akhfash:48-48.t:
And He said ﴿وَمُهَيْمِناً عَلَيْهِ﴾, meaning: "and as a witness over it" — accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). 
And He said ﴿شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهَاجاً﴾: "الشِّرْعَةُ" is religion (law), from "شَرَعَ", "يَشْرَعُ"; and "المِنْهٰاجُ" is the road, from "نَهَجَ", "يَنْهَجُ".

akhfash:51-51.t: And He said ﴿لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلْيَهُودَ وَٱلنَّصَارَىٰ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾, then He said ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ﴾ as a mubtadaʾ (subject) [i.e. a new sentence].

akhfash:53-53.t:
[And] He said ﴿وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾ — accusative, because it is conjoined to His saying ﴿فَعَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأْتِيَ بِٱلْفَتْحِ﴾; and it has been read in the nominative as a new start (ibtidāʾ). Abū ʿAmr said the accusative is impossible, because "and perhaps Allah that those who believe say" is not permissible; this is only [possible as] "perhaps that they say", making ﴿أَنْ يَقُولَ﴾ conjoined to what follows "عَسَى", or it is a following [by association], as in their saying "أَكَلْتُ خُبْزاً وَلَبَنَاً" (I ate bread and milk) and: 
....................... * مُتَقَلِّداً سَيْفاً وَرُمْحاً
(… girded with a sword and a spear.)

akhfash:60-60.t:
And He said ﴿بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذٰلِكَ مَثُوبَةً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, as He said ﴿بِخَيْرٍ مِنْ ذلِك﴾*.
And He said ﴿وَعَبَدَ ٱلطَّاغُوتَ﴾, i.e. ﴿مَن لَّعَنَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ ﴿وَعَبَدَ ٱلطَّاغُوتَ﴾ (and [who] worshipped the ṭāghūt).

akhfash:63-63.t: And He said ﴿وَأَكْلِهِمُ ٱلسُّحْتَ﴾ and He said ﴿عَن قَوْلِهِمُ ٱلإِثْمَ﴾: He put both in the accusative because the verb [the verbal noun] falls upon them.

akhfash:64-64.t: And He said ﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ يَدُ ٱللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ غُلَّتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾. They mentioned that it [the hand] is "the gift" and "the favour"; and likewise ﴿بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ﴾ — as you say "إنَّ لِفُلانٍ عِنْدِي يَداً" (so-and-so has a hand with me), i.e. a favour. And He said ﴿أُوْلِي ٱلأَيْدِي وَٱلأَبْصَارِ﴾, i.e. possessors of favours. "اليَد" (hand) may occur in [various] senses: you say "بَيْنَ يَدَي الدارِ" (between the two hands of the house), meaning: in front of it, though the house has no hands. [Translator's note: this is the author's interpretation, translated as written.]

akhfash:67-67.t: And He said ﴿فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ﴾, and some read ﴿رِسالاتِهِ﴾. Both are correct, because "الرِّسالَة" (the message) may comprise "الرَّسائِل" (messages), as you say "هَلَكَ البَعِيرُ والشَّاةُ" (the camel and the sheep perished) and "أَهْلَكَ الناسَ الدينارُ والدِرْهَمُ" (the dinar and the dirham have destroyed people), meaning the collective.

akhfash:69-69.t: And He said: ﴿وَٱلصَّابِئُونَ وَٱلنَّصَارَىٰ﴾, and He said in another place ﴿والصّابِئِينَ﴾. The accusative is the regular analogy, by conjunction to what follows ﴿إِنّ﴾. As for this one, its nominative is on two lines. [First,] it is as if His saying ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾ is in the position of the nominative in meaning, because it is a sentence that is a new start: one's saying "إنَّ زَيْداً مُنْطَلِقٌ" and "زَيْدٌ مُنْطَلِقٌ" without "إنّ" are the same in meaning; so if you wish, when you conjoin something to it, you make it follow the meaning, as you said "إنَّ زيداً مُنْطَلِقٌ وعمرٌو". But when it is put after the khabar (predicate) it is better and more frequent. [Second,] some said: since before it there is a verb, it was likened in form to what follows what precedes it — though its meaning is not within the verb before it, which is ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ﴾ — so he made it follow it and put it in the nominative by it, even though it is not so in meaning. That is because things occur in the wording that are not so in the meanings; among them their saying "هذا جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ" (this is the ruined hole of a lizard), and their saying "كَذَبَ عَلَيْكُمْ الحَجُّ", putting "الحَجّ" in the nominative by "كَذَبَ", whereas its meaning is only "عَلَيْكُم الحَجَّ" (upon you is the pilgrimage), accusative by their command. And you say "هذا حَبُّ رُمّانِي" (these are the seeds of my pomegranate), attaching "the pomegranate" to yourself, though only "the seeds" are yours, not "the pomegranate". So the likes of this are permissible while the meaning is otherwise.

akhfash:71-71.t:
[And] He said ﴿ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ﴾ and did not say "ثُمَّ عَمِيَ وَصَمَّ" although it is a verb placed first, because He informed about a people that they became blind and deaf, then explained how many of them did that, as you say "رأيتُ قَوْمَك ثُلُثَيْهِم" (I saw your people — two thirds of them). Like that is ﴿وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّجْوَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ﴾. And if you wish, you assign the verb to the latter [noun], putting it in the dialect of those who say "أَكَلُوني البَراغِيثُ" (the fleas ate me, with a plural verb), as he said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-fifth shāhid]: 
ولكِنْ دِيافِيٌّ أَبُوهُ وأُمُّهُ * بِحَوْراَنَ يَعْصُرْنَ السَّلِيطُ أَقارِبُه
(But [he is] one from Diyāf, his father and his mother; in Ḥawrān his kinsfolk press oil.)

akhfash:73-73.t:
[And] He said ﴿لَّقَدْ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ثَالِثُ ثَلاَثَةٍ﴾. That is because they put "Jesus" and "Mary" with Him. So it is in speech: when one is with two, one says "ثالِثُ ثلاثَةٍ" (the third of three), as He said ﴿ثَانِيَ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾ when there was only one with him. Whoever says "ثالثَ اثْنَيْنِ" (making two into three) is obliged to say "ثَانِيَ واحِدٍ" (making one into two). This is permissible in poetry, and in analogy it is sound. The poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-sixth shāhid]: 
وَلكِنْ لا أَخُونُ الجارَ حَتّىَ * يُزيلُ اللهُ ثالِثَةَ الأَثافِي
(But I do not betray the neighbour, until Allah removes the third of the hearthstones [i.e. never].)
Whoever says "ثانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ" and "ثالثُ ثَلاثَةٍ" says "حاديَ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ" (the eleventh of eleven) when a man is with ten. Whoever says "ثالثُ اثْنَيْنِ" says "حاديَ عَشْرَةَ" (the one making ten into eleven). As for the Arabs' saying "حاديَ عَشَرَ" and "ثانيَ عَشَر", this is in counting, when you say "second", "third", "fourth", "tenth" without saying "the tenth of such-and-such". When it passed ten and he wanted to say "حادي" and "ثاني", its meaning would not be known except by mentioning the ten, so he joined to it something of the letters of "ten".

akhfash:94-94.t: And He said ﴿لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنَ ٱلصَّيْدِ﴾ as an oath, i.e. by Allah, He will surely test you. Likewise this lām followed by the nūn occurs * only after an oath.

akhfash:95-95.t:
And He said: ﴿فَجَزَآءٌ مِّثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ ٱلنَّعَمِ﴾, i.e. then upon him is a compensation like what he killed, of livestock. 
[And] He said ﴿يَحْكُمُ بِهِ ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِّنْكُمْ هَدْياً﴾: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and ﴿بَالِغَ ٱلْكَعْبَةِ﴾ is its qualifier. Your saying ﴿بَالِغَ ٱلْكَعْبَةِ﴾ is not definite, because it has the sense of tanwīn: when one says "هذا ضاربُ زَيْدٍ" in the dialect of those who drop the nūn, and he has not yet done it, it is indefinite. Like that is ﴿هَـٰذَا عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا﴾: in it is some [sense of] tanwīn, except that it cannot be reached because of the implied noun [the pronoun]. 
Then He said ﴿أَوْ كَفَّارَةٌ طَعَامُ مَسَاكِينَ﴾, i.e. or upon him is an expiation — nominative with tanwīn — then He explained, saying "it is the feeding of poor people". Some read ﴿كَفّارَةُ طَعَامِ مَساكِينَ﴾, putting "expiation" in iḍāfa (genitive construct) with it. 
[And] He said ﴿أَو عَدْلُ ذٰلِكَ صِيَاماً﴾, meaning: or upon him is the equivalent of that in fasting — as you say "عَليْها مثلُها زُبْداً" (on it is its like in butter). Some read ﴿أَوْ عِدلُ ذلك صياما﴾ with kasra, and that is the [proper] way, because "العِدْل" is the equivalent. As for "العَدْل", it is the maṣdar (verbal noun): you say "عَدَلْتُ هذا بهذا عَدْلاً حَسَنا" (I balanced this with this well); and "العَدْل" is also the equivalent. He said ﴿وَلاَ يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ﴾, i.e. an equivalent. So they distinguished between this and "عدل المتاع" (the pack-load of goods), as you say "امرأَةٌ رَزانٌ" (a sedate woman) and "حَجَرٌ رَزِينٌ" (a heavy stone).

akhfash:97-97.t: And He said ﴿جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْكَعْبَةَ ٱلْبَيْتَ ٱلْحَرَامَ قِيَاماً لِّلنَّاسِ﴾, and He said ﴿وَٱلْهَدْيَ وَٱلْقَلاَئِدَ﴾, i.e. and He made for you the sacrificial animals and the garlands.

akhfash:105-105.t: And He said ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ لاَ يَضِرْكُمْ﴾, light, in the jussive because the answer to a command is jussive, taking it from "ضَارَ", "يَضِير". Some read ﴿يُضِرَّكُمْ﴾ and ﴿يَضُرُّكْمْ﴾, making the position jussive in both, except that he vowelled it because the rāʾ is doubled: its first [rāʾ] is unvowelled, so making its last unvowelled is not sound, since two unvowelled letters would meet. The best of these is ﴿لا يَضُرُّكُمْ﴾, nominative as a new start, because it is not a consequence of His saying ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾; He only informed [them] that it will not harm them.

akhfash:106-106.t: And He said ﴿شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ﴾, then He said ﴿ٱثْنَانِ ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِّنْكُمْ﴾, i.e. the testimony between you is the testimony of two. When "the testimony" was dropped, "the two" took its place and became nominative by its nominative, as He said ﴿وَسْئَلِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ﴾, meaning: the people of the town; (القريةَ) became accusative by the accusative of "الأَهْل" and took its place. Then He conjoined ﴿أَوْآخَرَانِ﴾ to "the two".

akhfash:107-107.t:
And He said: ﴿مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلأَوْلَيَانِ﴾, i.e. of the first ones (الأَوَّلَيْنِ) against whom [the claim] was established*. And some read ﴿ٱلأَوْلَيَانِ﴾, and that is how we read it. [Translator's note: the quotation in the first sentence was evidently meant to give the other reading «ٱلأَوَّلِينَ», as the gloss shows; the text has ﴿ٱلأَوْلَيَانِ﴾ both times.] Because when He said ﴿يَقُومَانِ مَقَامَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ﴾, it was as if He had defined the two of them until they became like a definite noun in meaning; so He said ﴿ٱلأَوْلَيَانِ﴾, making the definite noun follow them as a badal (substitute). The like of this, which follows the meaning, is frequent. The rajaz poet said [this is the one hundred and eighty-seventh shāhid]:
عَلَيَّ يومَ تَملكُ الأُمُورَا * صَوْمُ شُهورٍ وَجَبَتْ نُذُورا
* وَبَدَناً مُقَلَّداً مَنْحُورا *
(Incumbent on me, on the day you take charge of affairs, is a fast of months that became binding as vows, and a garlanded sacrificial camel slaughtered.)
He made it [بَدَناً, accusative] depend on "أَوْجَبَ" (he made binding), because it has the meaning of "قَدْ أَوْجَبَ".

akhfash:114-114.t:
[And He said] ﴿قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ ٱللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَآ أَنزِلْ عَلَيْنَا مَآئِدَةً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيداً لأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا﴾: He made ﴿تكونُ﴾ a qualifier of "the table", as He said ﴿هَبْ لِي مِن لَّدُنْكَ وَلِيّاً يَرِثُنِي﴾ — nominative if he makes it a qualifier, and jussive if he makes it an answer — as you say "أَعْطِني ثَوْباً يَسَعُني" (give me a garment that fits me) when you mean a roomy one, and "يَسَعْني" [jussive] when you make it an answer, as if you were stipulating that it fit you.
[And] He said ﴿وَآيَةً مِّنْكَ﴾, conjoined to "عيد" (festival), as if He said: "it will be a festival and a sign". It is mentioned that the reading of Ibn Masʿūd is ﴿تَكُنْ لَنَا عِيداً﴾.
Their saying ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ﴾ is not because they thought he was unable. Rather it is like the Arabs' saying: "أَتَسْتَطيعُ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ في هذهِ الحاجَةِ وتدَعَنا من كَلامِكَ" (can you go off on this errand and spare us your talk?), and you say "أَتَسْتَطيعُ أَنْ تَكُفَّ عَنّي فإِنِّي مَغْمُوم" (can you leave me alone, for I am distressed?). This is not because he is unable; rather he means "leave me alone", and he mentions ability to him in order to argue against him, i.e. you are able; when he reminds him of it, he knows that it is an argument against him. ﴿هَلْ تَسْتَطيعُ رَبَّكَ﴾ was read, as far as I know, only because of the obscurity of this other meaning — and Allah knows best. It is permissible, as if the verb were implied, meaning "can you call upon your Lord?" or "can you [ask] your Lord that you call upon Him?" — all of this is permissible.
"المائِدَةُ" is food, and the "فَعَلْتُ" form from it is "مِدْتُ", "أَمِيدُ". The poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-eighth shāhid]:
نُهْدِى رُؤوسَ المُجْرِمينَ الأَندادْ * إلى أمِيرِ المؤمِنِينَ المُمْتاد
(We send the heads of the rival criminals as gifts to the Commander of the Faithful, the one from whom bounty is sought.)
[And "المُمْتاد"] is "مُفْتَعِلٌ" from "مِدْتُ".

daas-irab:54-54.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ يا: vocative particle; أي: the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; the relative noun is a badal (substitute); and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ﴾ من: a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); يرتد: imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) with the sukūn, given a fatḥa because of the doubling (taḍʿīf); منكم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent); ﴿عَنْ دِينِهِ﴾ attached to يرتد; the clause of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ من; and the nominal clause من يرتد is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); يأتي: imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; الله: its fāʿil; and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. ﴿يُحِبُّهُمْ﴾ imperfect verb, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم; and the clause يحبونه is conjoined. ﴿أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ أذلة: a second adjective, to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; and likewise ﴿أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ﴾. ﴿يُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the wāw is its fāʿil; الله, the Name of Majesty, is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause is a fourth adjective. ﴿لا يَخافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لائِمٍ﴾ the clause is conjoined to يجاهدون. ﴿ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ﴾ the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ and فضل its khabar; الله, the Name of Majesty, is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ the hāʾ is the first object of يؤتي and the relative noun its second object; the clause is resumptive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); and the clause يشاء is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ واسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ الله, the Name of Majesty, is the mubtadaʾ; واسع its first khabar and عليم its second khabar; and the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:55-55.t:
﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa), having no governing effect. ﴿وَلِيُّكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject), or a fronted khabar (predicate) on the implied order: الله وليكم.
﴿وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ conjoined to الله, the Name of Majesty; and likewise the relative noun ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾, and the clause آمنوا after it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ﴾ the relative noun is a badal (substitute) from the relative noun before it, and the clause يقيمون الصلاة is a ṣila with no grammatical position; and likewise the clause ﴿يُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ﴾ which is conjoined to it. ﴿وَهُمْ راكِعُونَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or conjunctive; هم: mubtadaʾ, and راكعون its khabar; and the clause is circumstantial or conjoined.

daas-irab:56-56.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and the jussive conditional noun ﴿مَنْ﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿يَتَوَلَّ اللَّهَ﴾ is the khabar (predicate); ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined; ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun is conjoined; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَإِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْغالِبُونَ﴾ إنّ, its noun and its khabar; هم is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position; it is also permissible for هم to be a mubtadaʾ and الغالبون its khabar, the clause هم الغالبون being the khabar of أنّ [Translator's note: so written in the source, «أن», for إنّ]; the clause فإن حزب الله is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the conditional من; and the clause ومن يتول is resumptive.

daas-irab:57-57.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿لا تَتَّخِذُوا الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَكُمْ هُزُواً﴾ تتخذوا: imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and the relative noun its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause اتخذوا after it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; دينكم: first direct object, and هزوا: second object. ﴿وَلَعِباً﴾ conjoined to it. ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in the verb اتخذوا. ﴿أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ﴾ أوتوا: past verb, passive; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and it is the first object; الكتاب its second object; and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ attached to أوتوا. And ﴿الْكُفَّارَ﴾ a conjoined noun. ﴿أَوْلِياءَ﴾ second direct object of the verb تتخذوا. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil; الله, the Name of Majesty, its object. ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ إن is conditional; the tāʾ is the noun of كان and مؤمنين its khabar (predicate); the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) clause is omitted, the implied form being: إن كنتم مؤمنين فاتقوا الله; the clause إن كنتم مؤمنين is initial, with no grammatical position; and the clause واتقوا الله is conjoined.

daas-irab:58-58.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); إذا: an adverbial, conditional, non-jussive particle. ﴿نادَيْتُمْ﴾ past verb, and the tāʾ is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلَى الصَّلاةِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) ناديتم. ﴿اتَّخَذُوها هُزُواً﴾ past verb; the wāw is its fāʿil, the hāʾ its first object and هزوا its second object. ﴿وَلَعِباً﴾ conjoined to هزوا. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ﴾ أنّ, its noun and its khabar (predicate), which are interpretable as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The nominal clause ﴿ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

daas-irab:59-59.t:
﴿قُلْ﴾ imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is «you». ﴿يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative; الكتاب is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿هَلْ تَنْقِمُونَ مِنَّا﴾ imperfect verb; the wāw is its fāʿil; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) this verb; هل is an interrogative particle; and the clause is the speech reported by «say» (maqūl al-qawl), a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ﴾ آمنا: past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because of its connection with نا of the agents, and it is in the position of accusative by the maṣdar-forming أن before it; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of accusative as a direct object: «Do you resent anything in us except our believing?». بالله:
attached to the verb آمنا. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is conjunctive; ما: a relative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, the implied form being: «and you resent nothing in us except our believing in Allah and in what was sent down». ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty and the preposition are attached to آمنا. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; the relative noun is conjoined. ﴿أُنْزِلَ﴾ past verb, passive. ﴿إِلَيْنا﴾ attached to the passive verb أنزل. ﴿وَما أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ the clause is conjoined. And قبل: an adverb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive; [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to أنزل. ﴿وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فاسِقُونَ﴾ أنّ, its noun and its khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined, the implied form being: وبأن أكثركم فاسقون. Or the interpreted maṣdar is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being: وفسقكم ثابت عندكم («and your iniquity is established in you»).

daas-irab:60-60.t:
﴿قُلْ﴾ imperative verb; the fāʿil (agent) is «you»; and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿هَلْ﴾ interrogative particle. ﴿أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ﴾ imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the kāf is its object, and the fāʿil is «I»; the clause is the speech reported by «say» (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿مِنْ ذلِكَ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the elative noun (ism al-tafḍīl) شر. ﴿مَثُوبَةً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ attached to an adjective of مثوبة. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مَنْ لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of genitive as a badal (substitute) from شر, or in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause لعنه is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَجَعَلَ مِنْهُمُ الْقِرَدَةَ﴾ past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); and القردة is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْخَنازِيرَ﴾ conjoined; and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿أُولئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكاناً﴾ أولئك: a demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and شر its khabar.
And مكانا is a tamyīz. ﴿وَأَضَلُّ﴾ conjoined to شر. ﴿عَنْ سَواءِ﴾ attached to أضل. ﴿السَّبِيلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. And the nominal clause:
أولئك شر is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:61-61.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); إذا: an adverbial, conditional, non-jussive particle; the clause جاؤوكم is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). The verbs ﴿جاؤا- قالوا- دخلوا- خرجوا﴾ are past verbs, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). The clause ﴿قالُوا﴾ has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the clause ﴿آمَنَّا﴾ is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) after the verb of saying; the clause ﴿قَدْ دَخَلُوا﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw of قالوا; and ﴿بِالْكُفْرِ﴾ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb دخلوا. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is also circumstantial (ḥāliyya); هم is a detached nominative pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause is likewise in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the wāw of قالوا. The clause ﴿خَرَجُوا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of هم. ﴿بِهِ﴾ attached to the verb before them. The nominal clause الله أعلم is resumptive after the resumptive wāw, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾ ما is relative (mawṣūliyya), in the position of genitive, i.e. «of that which they used to conceal»; the clause كانوا is the ṣila (relative clause) and the clause يكتمون is the khabar [of كان]; it is also permissible to parse ما as maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), the implied form being: والله أعلم بكتمانهم («and Allah knows best their concealing»).

daas-irab:62-62.t: ﴿وَتَرى كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); ترى: imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as «you»; كثيرا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; and the clause is resumptive. ﴿يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ﴾ imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a direct object, i.e. «hastening into enmity». ﴿وَأَكْلِهِمُ﴾ conjoined to الإثم. ﴿السُّحْتَ﴾ direct object of the maṣdar (verbal noun) أكل. ﴿لَبِئْسَ ما كانُوا﴾ the lām is of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); بئس: an invariable (jāmid) past verb of blame; ما, the relative, is its fāʿil; and the clause كانوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ imperfect verb, nominative; and the clause يعملون is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كانوا before it.

daas-irab:63-63.t: ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a particle of urging (ḥaḍḍ) meaning «why not» (هلا). ﴿يَنْهاهُمُ الرَّبَّانِيُّونَ﴾ imperfect verb; the hāʾ is its object and الربانيون its fāʿil (agent). ﴿وَالْأَحْبارُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَنْ قَوْلِهِمُ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) ينهاهم. ﴿الْإِثْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) قول; and similar to it: ﴿السُّحْتَ﴾ direct object of the maṣdar أكل, which is conjoined to قول before it. ﴿لَبِئْسَ ما كانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ﴾ like the previous verse.

daas-irab:64-64.t: ﴿وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ﴾ past verb and fāʿil (agent); the feminine tāʾ is given a kasra to prevent the meeting of two quiescent letters; and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿يَدُ اللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the nominal clause is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) after the verb of saying. ﴿غُلَّتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ past verb, passive, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلُعِنُوا﴾ past verb, passive, and likewise its deputy agent; and the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِما قالُوا﴾ ما is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of genitive by the preposition, the implied form being: «and they were cursed because of their saying». And the clause قالوا is in the position of genitive as an adjective of ما. [Translator's note: so in the source, although ما has just been parsed as maṣdariyya; on that parsing the clause would be its ṣila.] ﴿بَلْ يَداهُ مَبْسُوطَتانِ﴾ بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); يداه: mubtadaʾ, nominative with the alif because it is a dual; likewise مبسوطتان is a khabar, nominative with the alif; and the clause is resumptive. ﴿يُنْفِقُ﴾ imperfect verb whose fāʿil is «he». ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ وليزيدن: the wāw is resumptive, and the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath; يزيدن: imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its connection with the heavy nūn of emphasis; كثيرا: its first object, to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached (mutaʿalliq); the relative noun ما is its fāʿil; أنزل: past verb, passive, to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it, إليك, are attached, and the nāʾib fāʿil is «it»; من ربك: attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿طُغْياناً﴾ second direct object. ﴿وَكُفْراً﴾ conjoined; the clause ليزيدن has no grammatical position because it is the response to the oath, and the clause of the oath and its response is resumptive. ﴿وَأَلْقَيْنا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَداوَةَ﴾ past verb to which the adverb after it is attached; نا is its fāʿil and العداوة its object. ﴿وَالْبَغْضاءَ﴾ conjoined. ﴿إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl: «persisting until the Day of Resurrection»; and القيامة is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كُلَّما﴾ conditional, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as an adverb of time. ﴿أَوْقَدُوا﴾ past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun للحرب are attached; the wāw is its fāʿil, and ﴿ناراً﴾ its object; and the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿أَطْفَأَهَا اللَّهُ﴾ past verb; the hāʾ is a fronted direct object and الله, the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil; and the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَساداً﴾ imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the wāw is its fāʿil; فسادا is a ḥāl in the sense of «causing corruption», or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); and the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is the mubtadaʾ; the clause لا يحب المفسدين is the khabar; and the clause والله is resumptive.

daas-irab:65-65.t: ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿أَنَّ أَهْلَ﴾ أنّ and its noun, and the clause آمنوا is its khabar (predicate); أنّ with its noun and its khabar are interpretable as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, its implied form being: «had their faith and their piety come about, We would have expiated their misdeeds from them». ﴿اتَّقَوْا﴾ past verb and fāʿil; and the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَكَفَّرْنا عَنْهُمْ﴾ past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached (mutaʿalliq); نا is its fāʿil and ﴿سَيِّئاتِهِمْ﴾ its object; and the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. And similarly ﴿وَلَأَدْخَلْناهُمْ جَنَّاتِ﴾ past verb and its fāʿil; the hāʾ is its first object and جنات its second object; and ﴿النَّعِيمِ﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:66-66.t:
The clause ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ﴾ and the clause ﴿لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾: their i'rab is like that of the previous verse. ﴿وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ ما: a relative noun conjoined to التوراة; the clause أنزل is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and إليهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ أكلوا: past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَمِنْ تَحْتِ﴾ conjoined to من فوقهم. ﴿أَرْجُلِهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿مِنْهُمْ أُمَّةٌ مُقْتَصِدَةٌ﴾ منهم is attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) أمة, and مقتصدة is an adjective; and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
﴿وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ the wāw is conjunctive; كثير is a mubtadaʾ and منهم is attached to كثير; the clause ﴿ساءَ ما..﴾ is the khabar of كثير, and the clause ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ is the ṣila of ما.

daas-irab:67-67.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ﴾ its i'rab has preceded at the beginning of the surah. ﴿بَلِّغْ﴾ imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) is «you»; and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ ما: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause after it is its ṣila (relative clause); إليك is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزل. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ﴾ إن is conditional; [تفعل] an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil is «you»; and the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَما بَلَّغْتَ رِسالَتَهُ﴾ بلغت: past verb; the tāʾ is its fāʿil and رسالته its object; and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), after the connective fāʾ. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ يعصمك: imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir) and the kāf is its object; and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكافِرِينَ﴾ إنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the verbal clause لا يهدي is its khabar; and the clause إن الله is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:68-68.t: For the detailed i'rab of this verse, see the previous verses. ﴿لَسْتُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ﴾ لستم: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the tāʾ is its noun; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) its khabar (predicate). ﴿حَتَّى تُقِيمُوا﴾ imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and ﴿التَّوْراةَ﴾ its object. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the verb, together with the preposition حتى, are attached to لستم. ﴿وَالْإِنْجِيلَ﴾ conjoined. ﴿وَما﴾ the relative is conjoined to التوراة.. and the clause ﴿لَيَزِيدَنَّ﴾ has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath.. and its like has preceded. ﴿فَلا تَأْسَ﴾ تأس: imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿عَلَى الْقَوْمِ﴾ attached to تأس. ﴿الْكافِرِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the yāʾ. [Translator's note: so in the source; الكافرين here is an adjective (naʿt) of القوم, not a muḍāf ilayhi.]

daas-irab:69-69.t: This verse has passed in Surat al-Baqara with a slight difference, namely the saying of Allah the Exalted: فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ﴿no. 62﴾. The accusative of الصابئين [there] is on the basis that it is conjoined to what precedes it; as for the nominative [here], it is on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, the implied form being: «Those who believed and those who are Jews.. all of them are thus, and the Sabians likewise ...»; and the nominal clause is conjoined to the resumptive clause إن الذين آمنوا. ﴿مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ﴾ من: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) from الذين; and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), because the relative noun carries a scent of condition, the implied form being: «whoever of the Jews and the Christians believes, no fear shall be upon them»; لا is negating; خوف: mubtadaʾ; عليهم its khabar. ﴿وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ the clause يحزنون is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم; and the nominal clause ولا هم is conjoined.

daas-irab:70-70.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿أَخَذْنا مِيثاقَ﴾ past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object. ﴿بَنِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the fatḥa, a diptote because of being a proper name and foreign. ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنا إِلَيْهِمْ رُسُلًا﴾ past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); نا is its fāʿil and رسلا its object; and the clause is conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath. ﴿كُلَّما﴾ a non-jussive conditional noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to the apodosis. ﴿جاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ﴾ past verb; the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and رسول the fāʿil; and the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿بِما لا تَهْوى أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ ما: a relative noun in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جاءهم; and the clause after it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿فَرِيقاً كَذَّبُوا﴾ كذبوا: past verb; the wāw is its fāʿil and فريقا its fronted object; and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ): «whenever a messenger came to them, they disobeyed him..»; and the clause ﴿وَفَرِيقاً يَقْتُلُونَ﴾ is conjoined.

daas-irab:71-71.t: ﴿وَحَسِبُوا﴾ past verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and the clause is conjoined by the wāw. ﴿أَلَّا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾ [تكون] a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (in the sense of: no trial would befall them as a result of their deed mentioned in the previous verse); it is accusative with the fatḥa, and لا is redundant (zāʾida) [Translator's note: so in the source; in the usual parsing this lā is negating]. أن and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of حسبوا, which means «they supposed». ﴿فَعَمُوا وَصَمُّوا﴾ two conjoined clauses. ﴿ثُمَّ تابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ تاب الله: past verb and its fāʿil; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them; and the clause is conjoined; likewise the two clauses ﴿ثُمَّ عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا﴾ are conjoined. ﴿كَثِيرٌ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the wāw in عموا or صموا. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ attached to كثير. ﴿وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject) and بصير khabar (predicate); and the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِما يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ بما: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to بصير, and the clause يعملون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; it is also possible for ما to be maṣdar-forming, i.e. «and Allah sees their deeds», so the clause is an adjective of ما. [Translator's note: so in the source; on the maṣdariyya parsing the clause would be the ṣila of the maṣdar-forming ما.]

daas-irab:72-72.t: ﴿لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا﴾ the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and the clause كفر.. is initial, with no grammatical position; or the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and the clause has no grammatical position as the response to the oath. The clause قالوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, likewise with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ إنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿هُوَ الْمَسِيحُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); and the clause is the khabar of إنّ. ﴿ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ﴾ ابن is an adjective of, or a badal (substitute) from, المسيح. مريم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the fatḥa, a diptote because of being a proper name and feminine. ﴿وَقالَ الْمَسِيحُ﴾ the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), i.e. they said that Allah is the Messiah.. while the Messiah was saying to them.. ﴿يا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), accusative with the yāʾ, treated like the sound masculine plural, the nūn being dropped for the annexation; إسرائيل: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the fatḥa in place of the kasra, a diptote because of being a proper name and foreign. ﴿اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ﴾ imperative and fāʿil (agent); the Name of Majesty is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is the speech reported by the verb of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿رَبِّي﴾ a badal, accusative with the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, and the yāʾ is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿وَرَبَّكُمْ﴾ a conjoined noun. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ إنّ, and the hāʾ is its noun; and the clause ﴿مَنْ يُشْرِكْ﴾ is its khabar; من: a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the clause يشرك is its khabar. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, genitive by the bāʾ; [together] attached to (mutaʿalliq) يشرك. ﴿فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْجَنَّةَ﴾ فقد: the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); حرم: past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil and الجنة its object; and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿وَمَأْواهُ﴾ mubtadaʾ, nominative with the ḍamma implied on the alif because of impossibility (taʿadhdhur), and the hāʾ is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿النَّارُ﴾ its khabar; and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَما لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصارٍ﴾ من: a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; أنصار: a noun genitive in form, nominative in position, as mubtadaʾ; للظالمين: attached to its khabar; and ما is negating, with no governing effect; it is also permissible for it to be the Ḥijāzī ما that governs like ليس, with أنصار as its noun. And the clause is resumptive on both views.

daas-irab:73-73.t:
﴿لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا﴾ its i'rab is like the preceding one. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ ثالِثُ ثَلاثَةٍ﴾ إنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; ثالث its khabar (predicate); and ثلاثة muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). And the clause is the speech reported by the verb of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ إِلَّا إِلهٌ واحِدٌ﴾ i.e. no god exists except One God, and it is not as they claim. ﴿وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya): they say that while there is no god but One. ما is negating. من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition.
﴿اللَّهَ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the word meant is إله] a noun genitive in form, nominative in position, as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar is omitted, implied as «existing». إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); إله is a badal (substitute) from the first إله. ﴿واحِدٌ﴾ an adjective; and the clause is circumstantial, or resumptive if the wāw is resumptive. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle and إن is conditional. ﴿لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا﴾ imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ﴾ عما is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ينتهوا, and the clause يقولون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; or the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ما and the verb [with the preposition] is attached to ينتهوا, i.e. «desist from their saying». The clause ينتهوا is initial, on the assumption that the wāw is resumptive, or the wāw of the oath. ﴿لَيَمَسَّنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ يمسن: imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its connection with the heavy nūn of emphasis; the relative noun after it is its object and ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ its fāʿil. The clause كفروا is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw before them. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ an adjective. The clause ليمسن has no grammatical position, being the response to the implied oath. And the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath, because the oath preceded the condition and so has the better claim to the response.

daas-irab:74-74.t: ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; لا is negating, with no governing effect. ﴿يَتُوبُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَهُ﴾ imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object; and the clause is conjoined. The nominal clause ﴿اللَّهُ غَفُورٌ﴾ is resumptive, after the resumptive wāw; and رحيم is an adjective.

daas-irab:75-75.t:
﴿مَا الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ﴾ ما is negating, with no governing effect; المسيح: mubtadaʾ (subject), and رسول its khabar (predicate); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ابن is an adjective or a badal (substitute); مريم is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the fatḥa in place of the kasra because of being a proper name and feminine; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ﴾ خلت: past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); الرسل is its fāʿil (agent); and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; and the clause is conjoined by the wāw before it. ﴿كانا يَأْكُلانِ الطَّعامَ﴾ كانا: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the alif is its noun; the verbal clause يأكلان الطعام is its khabar; and the clause كانا is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ الْآياتِ﴾ كيف: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; and the clause نبين الآيات is in the position
of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb انظر. ﴿ثُمَّ، انْظُرْ أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ أنى: an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; يؤفكون: imperfect verb, passive, and the wāw is its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is a direct object of the verb انظر; and the clause انظر is conjoined to the first, resumptive clause انظر.

daas-irab:76-76.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) is «you»; and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿أَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation. تعبدون: imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached (mutaʿalliq); the wāw is its fāʿil; الله, the Name of Majesty, is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the relative noun ﴿ما﴾ is its object; ﴿لا﴾ is negating. ﴿يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا﴾ imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; ضرا is its object, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as «he»; and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; الله, the Name of Majesty, is mubtadaʾ (subject). هو: a detached nominative pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; السميع: khabar (predicate) of هو, nominative; العليم: second khabar, nominative. And the clause mubtadaʾ. هو: a detached nominative pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; السميع: khabar of هو, nominative; العليم: second khabar, nominative. [Translator's note: the preceding passage is repeated in the source as written.] And the clause ﴿هُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الله. And the clause ﴿اللَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:77-77.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿يا﴾ vocative particle. ﴿أَهْلَ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf; and الكتاب is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لا تَغْلُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ﴾ تغلوا: imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); في دينكم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تغلوا. ﴿غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ﴾ غير is an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object): «do not exceed bounds with an exceeding other than the truth»; الحق is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause is the speech reported by «say» (maqūl al-qawl), a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا﴾ like ﴿لا تَغْلُوا﴾. ﴿أَهْواءَ﴾ direct object. ﴿قَوْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَدْ ضَلُّوا﴾ the clause is an adjective of قوم. ﴿مِنْ﴾ preposition. ﴿قَبْلُ﴾ mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of time, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation, in the position of genitive by من. ﴿وَأَضَلُّوا كَثِيراً﴾ past verb, fāʿil and direct object; and the clause is conjoined; and likewise the clause ﴿وَضَلُّوا عَنْ سَواءِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ is conjoined.

daas-irab:78-78.t:
﴿لُعِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾ الذين: a relative noun in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive past verb لعن; and the clause ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ بَنِي﴾ a noun genitive with the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw of the plural. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the fatḥa in place of the kasra, a diptote because of being a proper name and foreign. ﴿عَلى لِسانِ﴾ attached to لعن. ﴿داوُدَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the fatḥa because it is a diptote. ﴿وَعِيسَى﴾ conjoined to داوود, genitive with the kasra implied (muqaddara) on the alif. ﴿ابْنِ﴾ an adjective or a badal (substitute). ﴿مَرْيَمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the fatḥa because of being a proper name and feminine. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. ﴿بِما عَصَوْا﴾ ما is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); عصوا: past verb and fāʿil (agent), which together with the maṣdar-forming ما before it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: «because of their disobedience and the evil of their deeds»; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ذلك; and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿وَكانُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the wāw is its noun and the clause ﴿يَعْتَدُونَ﴾ its khabar; and the clause كانوا is conjoined to the clause عصوا, which is likewise resumptive.

daas-irab:79-79.t: ﴿كانُوا لا يَتَناهَوْنَ﴾ its i'rab is like ﴿كانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ﴾, and لا is negating. ﴿عَنْ مُنكَرٍ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿فَعَلُوهُ﴾ past verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is in the position of genitive as an adjective of منكر. ﴿لَبِئْسَ ما﴾ the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); بئس: an invariable (jāmid) past verb of blame; ما, the relative, is its fāʿil; the clause ﴿كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; the clause يفعلون is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كانوا; and the clause لبئس is initial, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:80-80.t: ﴿تَرى كَثِيراً﴾ imperfect verb and its object, and the fāʿil (agent) is «you». ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) كثير; and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿يَتَوَلَّوْنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ يتولون: imperfect verb; the wāw is its fāʿil and the relative noun its object; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the clause ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَبِئْسَ ما﴾ its i'rab has preceded in the previous verse. ﴿قَدَّمَتْ لَهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ قدمت: past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; أنفسهم is its fāʿil; and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْ سَخِطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ سخط is likewise a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from this verb and the maṣdar-forming particle before it is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is the invariable verb بئس, the implied form being: «Allah's anger against them: evil is what their souls have sent forth for them». ﴿وَفِي الْعَذابِ هُمْ خالِدُونَ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun في العذاب are attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, خالدون; and the nominal clause هم خالدون is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:81-81.t: ﴿وَلَوْ كانُوا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالنَّبِيِّ﴾ the clause كانوا is initial, with no grammatical position; the clause يؤمنون is the khabar (predicate); and the clause ﴿وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ﴾ is conjoined to it. ﴿مَا اتَّخَذُوهُمْ أَوْلِياءَ﴾ اتخذوهم: past verb; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), the hāʾ its first object and أولياء its second object. ﴿وَلكِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ﴾ لكنّ, its noun and its khabar; منهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) its noun ﴿كَثِيراً﴾; and the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:82-82.t: ﴿لَتَجِدَنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath; تجدن: imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its connection with the heavy nūn of emphasis; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as «you»; and ﴿أَشَدَّ﴾ is its first object. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive. ﴿عَداوَةً﴾ tamyīz (specification), accusative. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) عداوة. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ past verb and fāʿil; and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿الْيَهُودَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا﴾ conjoined to اليهود. ﴿وَلَتَجِدَنَّ أَقْرَبَهُمْ مَوَدَّةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الَّذِينَ قالُوا ... ﴾ like the previous verse. ﴿إِنَّا نَصارى﴾ إنّ, its noun and its khabar (predicate); and the clause is the speech reported by the verb of saying (maqūl al-qawl), a direct object. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance and the kāf is a particle of address. ﴿بِأَنَّ مِنْهُمْ قِسِّيسِينَ﴾ أنّ: a particle resembling the verb; قسيسين its noun; and منهم is attached to its khabar. ﴿وَرُهْباناً﴾ conjoined to قسيسين; أنّ and what follows it are interpretable as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source, «بالياء»; the bāʾ is meant]; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of the demonstrative. ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ أنّ and its noun; لا is negating; [يستكبرون] an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; and the clause لا يستكبرون is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.

daas-irab:83-83.t:
﴿وَإِذا سَمِعُوا﴾ إذا: an adverbial, conditional, non-jussive particle; and the clause سمعوا is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause ﴿أُنْزِلَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿تَرى أَعْيُنَهُمْ﴾ has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿تَفِيضُ﴾ imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿مِنَ الدَّمْعِ﴾ are attached (mutaʿalliq); and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِمَّا﴾ من is a preposition and ما a relative noun in the position of genitive by من; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تفيض.
﴿مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl; and the clause ﴿عَرَفُوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and the clause is resumptive, or circumstantial. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿آمَنَّا﴾ past verb and its fāʿil; and the clause is the speech reported by the verb of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَاكْتُبْنا﴾ the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa [the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition], and [اكتب] is a verb of supplication; نا is a direct object and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), i.e. «if the matter is so, then record us». ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to اكتبنا. ﴿الشَّاهِدِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; and the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

daas-irab:84-84.t:
﴿وَما لَنا﴾ ما: an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); لنا is attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate); and the nominal clause is conjoined.
﴿لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾ imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; لا is negating; and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿وَما﴾ a relative noun conjoined to الله, in the position of genitive like it; and the clause ﴿جاءَنا﴾ after it is its ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَنَطْمَعُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; or it is conjoined, on the assumption that the wāw is conjunctive. ﴿أَنْ يُدْخِلَنا﴾ أن and the imperfect verb after it are interpretable as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, [the two] attached to نطمع: «and we hope for our Lord's admitting us with the righteous people». ﴿رَبُّنا﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to يدخلنا. ﴿الْقَوْمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive. ﴿الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ an adjective, genitive with the yāʾ.

daas-irab:85-85.t:
﴿فَأَثابَهُمُ اللَّهُ ... جَنَّاتٍ﴾ أثابهم: past verb; the hāʾ is its first object and جنات its second object; and الله, the Name of Majesty, is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِما قالُوا﴾ ما is relative or maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb أثابهم; the clause قالوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the clause أثابهم is conjoined; and the clause ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ﴾ is in the position of genitive as an adjective of جنات.
﴿خالِدِينَ فِيها﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached. ﴿وَذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿جَزاءُ﴾ its khabar (predicate); and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the yāʾ.

daas-irab:86-86.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). الذين: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); and the clause ﴿وَكَذَّبُوا﴾ is conjoined. ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb كذبوا. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; the kāf is for address. ﴿أَصْحابُ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the nominal clause أولئك أصحاب الجحيم is the khabar of the relative noun الذين. And the clause والذين is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:87-87.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿لا تُحَرِّمُوا﴾ imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿طَيِّباتِ﴾ its object; and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); and the clause ﴿أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position, i.e. «what Allah has made lawful for you». ﴿وَلا تَعْتَدُوا﴾ like لا تحرموا; and the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ﴾: إنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause لا يحب المعتدين is its khabar (predicate); and the clause إن الله is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:88-88.t: ﴿وَكُلُوا﴾ imperative verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِمَّا﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) كلوا. ﴿رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ past verb and mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil; and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿حَلالًا﴾ direct object. ﴿طَيِّباً﴾ an adjective. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ imperative verb and fāʿil, and the Name of Majesty is the direct object; and the clause is conjoined, and likewise the clause وكلوا. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun in the position of accusative as an adjective. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِهِ﴾ attached to the khabar (predicate) after it. ﴿مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ its khabar; and the nominal clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:89-89.t:
﴿لا يُؤاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ imperfect verb; the kāf is its object and الله, the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil (agent); لا is negating, with no governing effect; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِاللَّغْوِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فِي أَيْمانِكُمْ﴾ attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from اللغو. ﴿وَلكِنْ يُؤاخِذُكُمْ﴾ the wāw is conjunctive; لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿يُؤاخِذُكُمُ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِما عَقَّدْتُمُ الْأَيْمانَ﴾ عقدتم: past verb; the tāʾ is its fāʿil and الأيمان its object; ما is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), which is more likely than its being relative. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ما and the verb after it is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يؤاخذكم. ﴿فَكَفَّارَتُهُ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the response to an implied condition: «if you swear an oath and break it, then its expiation ...»; كفارته is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِطْعامُ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿عَشَرَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿مَساكِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the fatḥa in place of the kasra, [being] the form of the ultimate plural (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ) on the pattern مفاعيل. ﴿مِنْ أَوْسَطِ﴾ attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted qualified noun, the implied form being: «feeding ten needy persons a defined food from the average». ﴿ما تُطْعِمُونَ﴾ ما: a relative noun in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted: ما تطعمونه. ﴿أَهْلِيكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative with the yāʾ, treated like the sound masculine plural, its nūn dropped for the annexation; and the kāf is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ﴾ conjoined to طعام [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the verse is إطعام]. ﴿رَقَبَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive. من: a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. يجد: imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَصِيامُ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and [صيام] a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being «then upon him is a fast»; and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿ثَلاثَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَيَّامٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. And the clause لم يجد is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من. ﴿ذلِكَ كَفَّارَةُ﴾ the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ and كفارة its khabar. ﴿أَيْمانِكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِذا حَلَفْتُمْ﴾ إذا: an adverbial, conditional, non-jussive particle; the clause حلفتم is in the position of genitive by annexation; and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. «if you swear and break [your oaths], then that is the expiation of your oaths». And the first clause ﴿ذلِكَ كَفَّارَةُ﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاحْفَظُوا أَيْمانَكُمْ﴾ imperative verb, fāʿil and direct object; and the clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿ذلِكَ كَفَّارَةُ﴾. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative in the position of genitive by the kāf; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object): «Allah makes clear to you His signs with a making-clear like that making-clear». ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آياتِهِ﴾ imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil and آياته its object; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ لعلّ, and the kāf is its noun; the clause تشكرون is in the position of nominative as its khabar; and the clause لعلكم تشكرون is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:90-90.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ the restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿الْخَمْرُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنْصابُ وَالْأَزْلامُ﴾ conjoined. ﴿رِجْسٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ عَمَلِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of الرجس. ﴿الشَّيْطانِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ﴾: the fāʾ connects the apodosis of an implied condition: «if wine is of the work of Satan, then avoid it»; and the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾: like the saying of Allah the Exalted in the previous verse ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾.

daas-irab:91-91.t:
﴿إِنَّما يُرِيدُ الشَّيْطانُ أَنْ يُوقِعَ﴾ يريد: imperfect verb and fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb after it is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. «Satan wants the casting [of enmity]». إنما is the restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿بَيْنَكُمُ﴾ an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) يوقع.
﴿الْعَداوَةَ﴾ direct object. ﴿وَالْبَغْضاءَ﴾ conjoined. ﴿فِي الْخَمْرِ﴾ attached to يوقع. ﴿وَالْمَيْسِرِ﴾ a conjoined noun.
﴿وَيَصُدَّكُمْ﴾ imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; and it is conjoined to يوقع. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَعَنِ الصَّلاةِ﴾ conjoined to ذكر الله. ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive; هل is an interrogative particle. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مُنْتَهُونَ﴾ its khabar (predicate), nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; and the clause is resumptive. The interrogation here is meant as a command, i.e. «desist».

daas-irab:92-92.t:
﴿وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ، وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ، وَاحْذَرُوا﴾ imperative verbs, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent) in each of them; and they are conjoined clauses.
The clause أطيعوا is conjoined to the clause ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُنْتَهُونَ﴾, which means «desist». ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is a jussive conditional particle. ﴿تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn; the tāʾ is the fāʿil; it is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, the implied form being: «if you turn away, then know that you will be requited for your deeds». ﴿أَنَّما﴾ the restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿عَلى رَسُولِنَا﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿الْبَلاغُ﴾. ﴿الْمُبِينُ﴾ an adjective. The clause أنما is resumptive. And أنما with what follows it stand in place of the two objects of اعلموا.
