daas-irab:32-32.t: ﴿مِنْ أَجْلِ ذلِكَ كَتَبْنا﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun من أجل are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb كتب, and نا is its fāʿil (agent); the demonstrative ذلك is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿عَلى بَنِي﴾ a noun genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is treated like a sound masculine plural, the nūn being dropped for annexation; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to كتبنا. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the fatḥa. ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ anna, with the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) as its noun. ﴿مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْساً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ﴾ قتل is a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun بغير are attached; نفسا is its object and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the conditional noun من is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and نفس is a muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَوْ فَسادٍ﴾ conjoined. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the two are attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) فساد. ﴿فَكَأَنَّما قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً﴾ the fāʾ is linking; كأنما is the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa) particle; [قتل is] a past verb with its object, its fāʿil is latent, and جميعا is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَمَنْ أَحْياها فَكَأَنَّما أَحْيَا النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً﴾ its i'rab is like the i'rab of what precedes it. ﴿وَلَقَدْ جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنا بِالْبَيِّناتِ﴾ جاءتهم is a past verb with its object, and رسلنا is its fāʿil; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb; the clause is the response to the oath with no grammatical position, coming after the lām that occurs in the response to the oath. ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ فِي الْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ﴾ inna and its noun, and لمسرفون is its khabar (predicate), the lām being the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); منهم: the two are attached to كثيرا; the adverb بعد is attached to مسرفون, and likewise the preposition and its genitive noun في الأرض. The demonstrative ذلك is in the position of the genitive by annexation, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:33-34.t: ﴿إِنَّما جَزاءُ الَّذِينَ﴾ جزاء is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the relative noun is in the position of the genitive by annexation, and ﴿إِنَّما﴾ is the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa) particle; the clause ﴿يُحارِبُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined to the Name of Majesty الله. ﴿وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَساداً﴾ an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial), or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿أَنْ يُقَتَّلُوا﴾ the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the subjunctive أن and the imperfect verb is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ جزاء, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوا﴾ conjoined. ﴿أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, passive (mabnī li-l-majhūl), and أيديهم is its nāʾib fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness. ﴿وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ﴾ conjoined to أيديهم. ﴿مِنْ خِلافٍ﴾ the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl from أيديهم and أرجلهم, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَوْ يُنْفَوْا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ a passive imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and the wāw is its nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿ذلِكَ لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ فِي الدُّنْيا﴾ the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, خزي is a second mubtadaʾ, and لهم is its khabar; this nominal clause is the khabar of ذلك; في الدنيا: the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of خزي. ﴿وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ﴾ لهم: the two are attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ عذاب; في الآخرة: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾ a naʿt, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun is in the position of the accusative by exception, with إلا. ﴿تابُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَنْ تَقْدِرُوا﴾ the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to تقدروا. ﴿فَاعْلَمُوا﴾ an imperative verb, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ anna, with the Name of Majesty as its noun, and غفور and رحيم are its two khabars; the clause takes the place of the two objects of اعلموا.

daas-irab:35-36.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ أي is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda); the relative noun is a badal (substitute), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the Name of Majesty is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَابْتَغُوا إِلَيْهِ الْوَسِيلَةَ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them or to الوسيلة after them, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَجاهِدُوا فِي سَبِيلِهِ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ laʿalla and its noun, and the clause تفلحون is its khabar (predicate); the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya). ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ inna, with the relative noun as its noun, and the clause is its khabar. ﴿لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ ما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ لهم: the two are attached to the omitted khabar of anna; في الأرض: the two are attached to an omitted ṣila; the relative noun ما is in the position of the accusative as the noun of anna [Translator's note: the source writes إن]; لو is a conditional particle. ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَمِثْلَهُ﴾ conjoined to ما. ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl of مثله. ﴿لِيَفْتَدُوا بِهِ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar of anna [Translator's note: so in the source]. ﴿مِنْ عَذابِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿يَوْمِ﴾ a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ also a muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ما تُقُبِّلَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ a past verb, passive (mabnī li-l-majhūl), to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivizing condition. ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) عذاب. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:113-113.t: ﴿قالُوا﴾ the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position. ﴿نُرِيدُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ مِنْها﴾ the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb نريد; منها is attached to (mutaʿalliq) نأكل; and the clause is the speech reported by the verb of saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clauses after it are conjoined to it. ﴿وَنَعْلَمَ أَنْ قَدْ صَدَقْتَنا﴾ أن is lightened from the heavy [أنّ], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn): «that you have spoken truly to us»; [صدقتنا] past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn; the tāʾ is its fāʿil (agent) and نا its object; and the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أن; and أن with what follows it is interpretable as a maṣdar which stands in place of the two objects of نعلم. ﴿وَنَكُونَ عَلَيْها مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb whose noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as «we»; من الشاهدين is attached to its omitted khabar; and عليها is attached to الشاهدين after it.

daas-irab:114-114.t: ﴿قالَ عِيسَى﴾ it is approximately like the previous verse. ﴿اللَّهُمَّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper name, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative; the vocative yā has been dropped and compensated for by a mīm at the end of the noun. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed, a muḍāf, accusative, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَنْزِلْ﴾ a verb of supplication, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb of supplication. ﴿مائِدَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ attached to an adjective of مائدة. ﴿تَكُونُ لَنا عِيداً﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb whose noun is a latent pronoun implied as «it», and عيدا is its khabar (predicate); لنا is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from عيدا, which was an adjective of it before being placed ahead of it. ﴿لِأَوَّلِنا﴾ attached to an omitted badal (substitute) from لنا. ﴿وَآخِرِنا﴾ conjoined to أولنا. ﴿وَآيَةً﴾ conjoined to عيدا. ﴿مِنْكَ﴾ attached to an omitted adjective of آية. ﴿وَارْزُقْنا﴾ the clause is conjoined to أنزل. ﴿وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ﴾ أنت: a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); خير its khabar; ﴿الرَّازِقِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; and the clause is resumptive, or circumstantial if the wāw is for circumstance.

daas-irab:115-115.t: ﴿قالَ اللَّهُ﴾ the verbal clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿إِنِّي مُنَزِّلُها عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ إنّ; the yāʾ is its noun, and منزلها its khabar (predicate), to which the preposition and its genitive noun عليكم are attached (mutaʿalliq); and the clause is the speech reported by the verb of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar is the clause ﴿يَكْفُرْ﴾. ﴿بَعْدُ﴾ an adverb of time, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation, attached to the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) يكفر; and ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَإِنِّي أُعَذِّبُهُ﴾ the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); إنّ, and the yāʾ is its noun, and the clause أعذبه its khabar; the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as «I». ﴿عَذاباً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿لا أُعَذِّبُهُ﴾ لا is negating; أعذب: imperfect verb; the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as a substitute for the absolute object (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq), because it refers back to it; and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun implied as «I». ﴿أَحَداً﴾ direct object. ﴿مِنَ الْعالَمِينَ﴾ attached to an omitted adjective of أحدا; the clause لا أعذبه أحدا is in the position of accusative as an adjective of عذابا; and the clause فإني is in the position of jussive as the apodosis.

daas-irab:116-116.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قالَ اللَّهُ: يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ﴾ the i'rab of its like has preceded. ﴿أَأَنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation. أنت: a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿قُلْتَ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached (mutaʿalliq); the tāʾ is its fāʿil (agent); and the clause is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate). ﴿اتَّخِذُونِي﴾ imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya); the wāw is the fāʿil and the yāʾ the first direct object. ﴿وَأُمِّي﴾ a noun conjoined to the yāʾ, accusative with the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, and the yāʾ is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلهَيْنِ﴾ second direct object, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a dual. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ attached to the verb اتخذوني or to an omitted adjective of إلهين; and the clause اتخذوني is the speech reported by the verb of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿قالَ سُبْحانَكَ﴾ سبحانك is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿ما يَكُونُ لِي أَنْ أَقُولَ﴾ ما is negating, with no governing effect; يكون: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿لِي﴾ are attached to its omitted khabar, and its noun is the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb أقول after it; and the clause ما يكون is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿ما لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ﴾ ما: a relative noun in the position of accusative as the direct object of أقول; ليس: a defective past verb. ﴿بِحَقٍّ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; حق: a noun genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ليس; لي is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from حق — it was an adjective of it, and when placed ahead of it, it became a ḥāl; and the clause ليس is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُ قُلْتُهُ﴾ إن: a jussive conditional particle. كنت: a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its noun. قلته: past verb, fāʿil and direct object; and the clause is the khabar of كنت. ﴿فَقَدْ عَلِمْتَهُ﴾ the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); قد: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); علمته: past verb, fāʿil and direct object; and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; and the clause إن كنت has no grammatical position, being resumptive. ﴿تَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِي﴾ ما: a relative noun in the position of accusative as direct object; في نفسي is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun; تعلم: and the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the wording «تعلم والجملة» is so in the source.] ﴿وَلا أَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِكَ﴾ its i'rab is approximately like the preceding one, and it is conjoined to it. ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ﴾ أنت علام: mubtadaʾ and khabar; the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ, and the kāf is its noun; and the clause إنك is causal.

daas-irab:117-117.t: ﴿ما قُلْتُ لَهُمْ﴾ past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); the tāʾ is its fāʿil (agent); ما is negating, with no governing effect. ﴿إِلَّا ما أَمَرْتَنِي بِهِ﴾ إلا: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ما: a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). أمرتني: past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn; the tāʾ is its fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is a direct object; and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. به is attached to the verb أمرتني. ﴿أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ﴾ أن is explicative (mufassira); اعبدوا: imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and الله, the Name of Majesty, its object. ﴿رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ﴾ ربي: a badal (substitute), accusative with the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, and the yāʾ is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); and ربكم is conjoined. It is also permissible for ﴿أَنِ﴾ to be a maṣdar-forming, subjunctive-governing particle; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from it and the verb after it is then in the position of genitive as a badal from the hāʾ in به, or in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), implied as «it». ﴿وَكُنْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيداً﴾ شهيدا: khabar of كان, to which the preposition and its genitive noun before it are attached; the tāʾ is its noun; and the clause is conjoined. ﴿ما دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the tāʾ is its noun, and فيهم is attached to its omitted khabar. And ما «its noun» after it is interpretable as a maṣdar in the position of genitive by annexation: «the duration of my remaining among them». [Translator's note: so in the source, «وما اسمها بعدها»; presumably «ما and what follows it» is meant.] ﴿فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive. لما: an adverb of time (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya), or a non-jussive conditional particle; توفيتني: past verb, its fāʿil and its object, and the nūn is for protection; and the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ كان, and the tāʾ is its noun; الرقيب its khabar, to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ are attached. أنت: a detached pronoun, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative as a badal from the tāʾ, or a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position; and the clause كنت is the response to لما, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَأَنْتَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ﴾ أنت شهيد: mubtadaʾ and khabar, to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; and the clause is resumptive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya).

daas-irab:118-118.t: ﴿إِنْ تُعَذِّبْهُمْ﴾ إن is a jussive conditional particle, and تعذبهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa); and the clause ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبادُكَ﴾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and it has been said that it is causal (taʿlīliyya) and the apodosis is omitted. And similarly ﴿وَإِنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ، فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ إنّ, its noun and its two khabars (predicates); and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis.

daas-irab:119-119.t:
﴿قالَ اللَّهُ﴾ the verbal clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿هذا يَوْمُ﴾ ذا: a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject), and يوم its khabar (predicate); and the clause is the speech reported by the verb of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿يَنْفَعُ الصَّادِقِينَ صِدْقُهُمْ﴾ ينفع: imperfect verb, its object, and its postponed fāʿil (agent); and the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).
﴿لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ جنات; and the clause is resumptive. And the clause ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ﴾ is in the position of nominative as an adjective of جنات. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative with the yāʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾ attached to خالدين, and likewise the adverb ﴿أَبَداً﴾ is attached to خالدين. ﴿رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ﴾ past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; and the clause is resumptive; and the clause ﴿رَضُوا عَنْهُ﴾ is conjoined to it. ﴿ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar, and العظيم is an adjective; and the clause is also resumptive.

daas-irab:120-120.t: ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, genitive by the lām; [the two] are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿مُلْكُ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَما﴾ a relative noun conjoined to ملك, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative. ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ هو: mubtadaʾ, and قدير: khabar, to which the preposition and its genitive noun على كل are attached; and قدير is muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: so in the source; the muḍāf ilayhi is شيء]; and the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا﴾ an accusative (manṣūb) imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَ النَّارِ﴾ the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿وَما هُمْ بِخارِجِينَ﴾ ما is the Ḥijāzī ما, working like laysa; the detached pronoun is its noun and بخارجين its khabar (predicate), the bāʾ being a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿مِنْها﴾ the two are attached to the active participle خارجين; the clause ﴿وَما هُمْ..﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُقِيمٌ﴾ لهم: the two are attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) عذاب, and مقيم is its naʿt (adjective); the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:38-39.t: ﴿وَالسَّارِقُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; السارق is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "[is] in what is recited to you", on the basis of omission of the muḍāf with the muḍāf ilayhi retained, the implied form being: "the ruling on the male thief and the female thief is in what.." (حكم السارق والسارقة فيما..). ﴿وَالسَّارِقَةُ﴾ conjoined. ﴿فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُما﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent), and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with the fatḥa. ﴿جَزاءً﴾ a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿بِما كَسَبا﴾ a past verb, and the alif is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from maṣdariyya ما and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar ﴿جَزاءً﴾; it is also permissible for ما to be a relative. ﴿نَكالًا﴾ a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, or a badal (substitute) of جزاء. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive by من, the two being attached to نكالا. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ, with its two khabars, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَمَنْ تابَ مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them, which is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the conditional noun من is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿ظُلْمِهِ﴾ a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَأَصْلَحَ﴾ conjoined to تاب. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِ﴾ inna, with the Name of Majesty as its noun, and the clause is its khabar; the clause ﴿إِنَّ﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and this apodosis together with the protasis is the khabar of من. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ inna, with the Name of Majesty as its noun, and غفور and رحيم are its two khabars; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:40-40.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the hamza is for interrogation. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ له: the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) ملك; the nominal clause is the khabar of anna, and الله, the Name of Majesty, is its noun; السموات is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and الأرض is conjoined. ﴿يُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ the relative noun is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb يعذب; the clause is resumptive, and the clause ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ لمن: the two are attached to يغفر, and the clause is conjoined. Anna and what follows it take the place of the two objects of تعلم. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ الله, the Name of Majesty, is a mubtadaʾ, and قدير is the khabar, to which the preposition and its genitive noun before it are attached; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:41-41.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ يا is the vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere أيّ here is parsed as an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on the ḍamma]. ﴿الرَّسُولُ﴾ a badal (substitute). ﴿لا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; the kāf is its object and the relative noun its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), and the clause ﴿يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾ the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause ﴿قالُوا﴾ is the ṣila. ﴿آمَنَّا﴾ a past verb, and نا is its fāʿil; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿بِأَفْواهِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to قالوا. ﴿وَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ a jussive imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾ conjoined to الذين قالوا. ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "they are listeners" (هم سماعون). ﴿لِلْكَذِبِ﴾ the two are attached to سماعون. ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ﴾ a badal from the first سماعون, to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached, and آخرين is a naʿt (adjective). ﴿لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the kāf its object; the clause is a second naʿt of قوم. ﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَواضِعِهِ﴾ يحرفون is an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, with its fāʿil and its object; مواضعه is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "after its being placed in its places" (من بعد وضعه في مواضعه). ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive; the clause ﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ﴾ is a third naʿt. ﴿إِنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هذا﴾ أوتيتم is a past verb, passive (mabnī li-l-majhūl), in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the demonstrative is its second object, the nāʾib fāʿil being the first object. ﴿فَخُذُوهُ﴾ the fāʾ is linking; an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ فَاحْذَرُوا﴾ a passive imperfect verb, jussive by لم, and it is the protasis; the wāw is its nāʾib fāʿil and the hāʾ its second object; فاحذروا: the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿وَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ فِتْنَتَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object, and the conditional noun is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿فَلَنْ تَمْلِكَ لَهُ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً﴾ من الله: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl from the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) after them. ﴿أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ﴾ the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and the relative noun its khabar. ﴿لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُطَهِّرَ﴾ a jussive imperfect verb; the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) its object; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ the object of يطهر. ﴿لَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيا خِزْيٌ﴾ لهم: the two are attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ خزي. ﴿فِي الدُّنْيا﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl, and the clause is a second khabar of the demonstrative. ﴿وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ﴾ conjoined. ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾ a naʿt.

daas-irab:42-42.t:
﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ﴾ سماعون is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "they" (هم), and the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached (mutaʿalliq) to it.
And likewise ﴿أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ﴾. ﴿فَإِنْ جاؤُكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an imperative verb to which the adverb after it is attached. The clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because it is joined to the linking fāʾ. ﴿أَوْ أَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ an imperative verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَإِنْ تُعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ إن is conditional; تعرض is a jussive (majzūm) imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَإِنْ حَكَمْتَ﴾ إن is conditional, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ the fāʾ is linking; an imperative verb to which the adverb and the preposition with its genitive noun after it are attached; the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, with the Name of Majesty as its noun, and the clause ﴿يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾ is its khabar.

daas-irab:43-43.t: ﴿وَكَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the wāw is resumptive. ﴿يُحَكِّمُونَكَ﴾ an imperfect verb; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and the kāf its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْراةُ﴾ التوراة is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, the adverb عندهم being attached to it. ﴿فِيها حُكْمُ اللَّهِ﴾ حكم is a mubtadaʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun فيها are attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar; الله, the Name of Majesty, is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿وَما أُولئِكَ﴾ ما is Ḥijāzī, working like laysa, and the demonstrative is in the position of the nominative as its noun. ﴿بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ its khabar, accusative in position and genitive in form because of the redundant (zāʾida) bāʾ before it; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:44-44.t:
﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَنْزَلْنَا التَّوْراةَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿فِيها هُدىً وَنُورٌ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هدى. ﴿يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ﴾ يحكم is an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and النبيون is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا﴾ a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective), and the clause أسلموا is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يحكم, and the clause ﴿هادُوا﴾ is the ṣila. ﴿وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبارُ﴾ conjoined to النبيون. ﴿بِمَا اسْتُحْفِظُوا﴾ بما: the two are attached to يحكم; استحفظوا is a past verb, passive (mabnī li-l-majhūl), the wāw is its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ كِتابِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَكانُوا عَلَيْهِ شُهَداءَ﴾ kāna, its noun and its khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the khabar شهداء, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَلا تَخْشَوُا النَّاسَ﴾ تخشوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, with its fāʿil and its object; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), and لا is the jussivizing lā of prohibition.
﴿وَاخْشَوْنِ﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), the wāw is the fāʿil, and the omitted yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَلا تَشْتَرُوا بِآياتِي﴾ لا is the lā of prohibition; تشتروا is an imperfect verb, jussive by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. The preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached to it. ﴿ثَمَناً﴾ its object. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ a naʿt. ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussivizing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; يحكم is a jussive imperfect verb, and بما: the two are attached to يحكم. ﴿أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿أولئك﴾ a demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as a second mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْكافِرُونَ﴾ the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ, and the clause فأولئك is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. The protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من.

daas-irab:45-45.t: ﴿وَكَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and likewise ﴿فِيها﴾ is attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to the clause أنزلنا. ﴿أَنَّ النَّفْسَ بِالنَّفْسِ﴾ anna and its noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate), i.e. "killed (مقتولة) for the soul"; anna and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of كتبنا. Likewise what follows it, i.e.: ﴿وَالْعَيْنَ﴾ "gouged out" (مقلوعة) ﴿بِالْعَيْنِ﴾, ﴿وَالْأَنْفَ﴾ "cut off" (مجدوع) ﴿بِالْأَنْفِ﴾, ﴿وَالْأُذُنَ﴾ "cut off" (مصلومة) ﴿بِالْأُذُنِ﴾, ﴿وَالسِّنَّ﴾ "pulled out" (مقلوعة) ﴿بِالسِّنِّ﴾, ﴿وَالْجُرُوحَ﴾ "retaliated for in kind" (مقصوص بها قصاصا). ﴿فَمَنْ تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ﴾ تصدق is a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the conditional noun is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the fāʾ is resumptive. ﴿فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَهُ﴾ the fāʾ is linking, [followed by] a mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ the i'rab of something similar has preceded in the previous verse.

daas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿وَقَفَّيْنا عَلى آثارِهِمْ بِعِيسَى﴾ a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun على آثارهم are attached (mutaʿalliq), and likewise بعيسى; نا is its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is conjoined. ﴿ابْنِ﴾ a genitive (majrūr) naʿt (adjective) or badal (substitute). ﴿مَرْيَمَ﴾ a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the fatḥa because it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), being a proper name and feminine. ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لِما﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to مصدقا. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ the adverb is attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿يَدَيْهِ﴾ a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the yāʾ because it is dual. ﴿مِنَ التَّوْراةِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ الْإِنْجِيلَ﴾ a past verb and its two objects, and نا is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِيهِ هُدىً﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun فيه are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هدى. ﴿وَنُورٌ﴾ conjoined, and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿وَهُدىً وَمَوْعِظَةً﴾ conjoined to ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾. ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ the two are attached to موعظة.

daas-irab:47-47.t: ﴿وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, and أهل is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined. It was also read with a kasra on the lām, as the lām of reason (taʿlīl), with the imperfect verb in the accusative. ﴿الْإِنْجِيلِ﴾ a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يحكم. ﴿أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to أنزل, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ﴾ for its i'rab see verse 45 [Translator's note: so in the source; the parallel phrase is parsed in full under verse 44].

daas-irab:48-48.t: ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ﴾ a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); نا is its fāʿil (agent) and الكتاب its object. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from الكتاب. ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ a second ḥāl. ﴿لِما﴾ the two are attached to مصدقا. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿مِنَ الْكِتابِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَمُهَيْمِناً﴾ conjoined to ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to what precedes them. ﴿فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an imperative verb to which the adverb after it is attached; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), and the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition. ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to أنزل الله [Translator's note: so in the source; بما is attached to احكم, and أنزل الله is its ṣila]; the clause is the ṣila of ما. ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, with its object, and its fāʿil is "you" (أنت); the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَمَّا جاءَكَ﴾ عما: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl, its implied form being: "turning away from what has come to you" (مائلا عما جاءك); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) fāʿil of جاءك. ﴿لِكُلٍّ﴾ the two are attached to جعلنا after them, or are the first object of جعلنا. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of the omitted noun for which the compensatory tanwīn (tanwīn al-ʿiwaḍ) in كل stands, the implied form being: "for every community" (لكل أمة). ﴿شِرْعَةً﴾ the object of جعل. ﴿وَمِنْهاجاً﴾ conjoined, and the verbal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil; لو is conditional. ﴿لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً﴾ the kāf is the first object of جعل and أمة its second object; واحدة is a naʿt; and the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of conditional لو. ﴿وَلكِنْ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ﴾ لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk) with no governing effect because it is lightened. ليبلوكم: the lām is the lām of reason (taʿlīl); يبلوكم is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of reason, and the kāf is its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted verb "He willed" (أراد); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي ما آتاكُمْ﴾ فيما: the two are attached to يبلوكم, and the clause آتاكم is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْراتِ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you know this, then race"; استبقوا الخيرات: an imperative verb, the wāw is its fāʿil and الخيرات its object; the clause has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive by إلى, the two being attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) مرجعكم; the clause is resumptive. ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ a ḥāl. ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the kāf is its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِما كُنْتُمْ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. ﴿فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and فيه: the two are attached to the verb after it.

daas-irab:49-49.t: ﴿وَأَنِ احْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; subjunctive أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb: "and We enjoined upon you to judge" (ووصيناك بالحكم); the adverb is attached to the verb before it. ﴿بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ، وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَهُمْ﴾ its i'rab has preceded in the previous verse. ﴿وَاحْذَرْهُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنُوكَ﴾ the hāʾ is the object of the verb احذر; أن يفتنوك: the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition: "beware of the temptation" (احذر الفتنة). ﴿عَنْ بَعْضِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ﴾ أنزل is a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent); the relative noun is in the position of the genitive by annexation, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ a past verb in the position of the jussive by conditional إن, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, after the resumptive fāʾ. ﴿فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّما يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُصِيبَهُمْ بِبَعْضِ ذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ أن and the verb يصيب after it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb يريد, and الله, the Name of Majesty, is its fāʿil. أنما is the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa) particle with no governing effect, and it takes the place of the two objects of اعلم before it; the clause اعلم is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ببعض: the two are attached to يصيبهم, and ذنوبهم is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ لَفاسِقُونَ﴾ من الناس: the two are attached to the khabar (predicate) of inna, ﴿لَفاسِقُونَ﴾, or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of كثير; the lām is the shifted lām (muzaḥlaqa) on the khabar of inna, and كثيرا is its noun.

daas-irab:50-50.t: ﴿أَفَحُكْمَ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ يَبْغُونَ﴾ يبغون is an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); حكم is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and الجاهلية a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the hamza at the start of the clause is for interrogation, and the clause, after the resumptive fāʾ, is resumptive. ﴿وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حُكْماً﴾ من is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and أحسن is its khabar (predicate), to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached (mutaʿalliq); حكما is a tamyīz (specification). ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾ the two are attached to حكما or to أحسن, in which case the lām means "in the view of" (عند). ﴿يُوقِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

daas-irab:51-51.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿لا تَتَّخِذُوا الْيَهُودَ وَالنَّصارى أَوْلِياءَ﴾ تتخذوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn because it is preceded by the jussivizing lā of prohibition; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); اليهود is its first object and أولياء its second object; النصارى is conjoined to اليهود. ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ﴾ بعضهم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أولياء its khabar (predicate); بعض is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) with no grammatical position, and the clause لا تتخذوا before it is resumptive, likewise with no grammatical position. ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ مِنْكُمْ﴾ من is a jussivizing conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; يتولهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive by the dropping of the weak letter; منكم: the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَإِنَّهُ مِنْهُمْ﴾ inna, with the hāʾ as its noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun as its khabar; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because it is joined to the linking fāʾ; the clause of protasis and apodosis is the khabar of من. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is the noun of inna; لا is negative; يهدي is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ; القوم is its object, and its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو); الظالمين is an accusative naʿt (adjective), with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause لا يهدي is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna, and the clause إن الله is resumptive.

daas-irab:52-52.t: ﴿فَتَرَى الَّذِينَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the relative noun is its object; the clause is resumptive after the fāʾ. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) مرض, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿يُسارِعُونَ فِيهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun فيهم are attached, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿نَخْشى أَنْ تُصِيبَنا دائِرَةٌ﴾ تصيبنا is an accusative (manṣūb) imperfect verb; نا is its object and دائرة its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb نخشى; the clause نخشى is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech); and the clause يقولون is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿فَعَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِالْفَتْحِ﴾ عسى is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; الله, the Name of Majesty, is its noun; the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and the verb after it is its khabar; بالفتح: the two are attached to يأتي. ﴿أَوْ أَمْرٍ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ﴾ أمر is conjoined to الفتح, and من عنده: the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أمر; the clause عسى is resumptive. ﴿فَيُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما أَسَرُّوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ نادِمِينَ﴾ the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya); يصبحوا is an incomplete imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ; the wāw is its noun and نادمين its khabar, to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿عَلى ما﴾ are attached. أسروا is a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun في أنفسهم are attached, and the clause أسروا is the ṣila, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:53-53.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ الذين is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of يقول; آمنوا is a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; the clause يقول is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَهؤُلاءِ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle. ﴿هؤُلاءِ﴾ a demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the relative noun after it is its khabar (predicate); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿أَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ﴾ a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached (mutaʿalliq), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. ﴿جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ﴾ جهد is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and أيمانهم a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لَمَعَكُمْ﴾ inna, with the hāʾ as its noun; in لمعكم the lām is the shifted lām (muzaḥlaqa), and the adverb مع is attached to the omitted khabar of inna; the clause has no grammatical position, being the response to an oath. ﴿حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ﴾ حبط is a past verb and أعمالهم the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا خاسِرِينَ﴾ the clause of the incomplete (nāqiṣ) verb أصبح with its noun and its khabar after it is conjoined to the clause حبطت.

farraa:1-1.t:
Of His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿أَوْفُواْ بِٱلْعُقُود﴾ — He means: the covenants. [Al-ʿuqūd] and al-ʿuhūd are one and the same.
His saying: ﴿أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ ٱلأَنْعَامِ﴾ — these are wild cattle, gazelles and wild asses.
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ — it is in the position of the accusative by exception; the nominative is permissible, just as "qāma al-qawmu illā Zaydan" and "illā Zaydun" are permissible. The meaning in it is: except what We make clear to you of the prohibition of what is forbidden while you are in the state of iḥrām, or in the sacred precinct. That is His saying ﴿غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي ٱلصَّيْدِ﴾ — He is saying: these are made lawful for you, while you do not hold game to be lawful ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ﴾. Similar to it is ﴿إلَى طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ ناظِرِينَ إنَاهُ﴾. It is equivalent to your saying: "This thing is made lawful for you, neither being excessive in it nor transgressing."
When you put (غير) in place of (لا), the accusative that comes after «لا» passes to «غير». Had it been (محلِّين الصيد), you would have put it in the accusative, as Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿ولا آمِّين الْبَيْتَ الحَرَامَ﴾; and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (ولا آمِّى البيتِ الحرامِ).
﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ مَا يُرِيدُ﴾: He decrees what He wills.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ عَلَىٰ فَتْرَةٍ مَّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ أَن تَقُولُواْ﴾ — its meaning is: lest you say: ﴿مَا جَآءَنَا مِن بَشِيرٍ﴾; like what He said: ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلّوا﴾.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تُحِلُّواْ شَعَآئِرَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ — most of the Arabs did not consider al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa to be among the rites, and did not go between them. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: do not regard abandoning that as lawful.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ ٱلشَّهْرَ ٱلْحَرَامَ﴾: nor fighting in the sacred month.
﴿وَلاَ ٱلْهَدْيَ﴾ — this is the sacrificial animal of the polytheists: [do not] interfere with it, nor frighten anyone who has garlanded his camel. When one of the Arabs wanted to travel outside the sacred months, he would garland his camel and thereby be safe. So He said: do not frighten anyone who has put on a garland. The people of Mecca used to garland with tree bark, and the rest of the Arabs with camel hair and [goat] hair.
His saying: ﴿وَلاۤ آمِّينَ ٱلْبَيْتَ﴾ — He is saying: and do not prevent any of the polytheists who are heading for the Sacred House or intend it. Then this verse was abrogated by the one in [Sūrat] al-Tawba: ﴿فاقْتُلُوا الْمُشْرِكينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدتُّمُوهُمْ﴾ to the end of the verse.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ﴾ — Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read it "wa-lā yujrimannakum", from ajramtu. The speech of the Arabs and the reading of the readers is ﴿يَجرِمنكم﴾ with fatḥa on the yāʾ. The exegesis has come: "and let not hatred of a people drive you." Al-Farrāʾ said: I heard the Arabs say: "So-and-so is the jarīma of his family," meaning: the earner for his family; and "he went out to yajrimuhum," i.e. to earn for them. The meaning in it is close: "let not hatred of a people earn you [i.e. lead you to] doing evil." So (أن) is in the position of the accusative. [Translator's note: «فى وضع تصب» in the text is evidently a misprint for «فى موضع نصب».]
If you place (على) before (أن), you take it in the sense of: "let not their hatred drive you to such-and-such — to not being just"; so it is fine to drop (على), just as you say: "It drove me to ask (an asʾala)" and "to asking (ʿalā an asʾala)."
﴿وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ﴾ — some read «الشنآن» heavy [i.e. shanaʾān, with a vowel on the nūn], and most of the readers read it light [shanʾān].
Both the light and the heavy form have been transmitted from al-Aʿmash. It means: "let not hatred of a people drive you." The proper way, when it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), is to make it heavy; and if you mean by it "one who is hated by a people", you say: shanʾān.
And ﴿أَن صَدُّوكُمْ﴾ is in the position of the accusative because a preposition is fit [to be supplied] before it. Had it been read with kasra in the sense of a condition (jazāʾ), it would have been correct. In the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbdallāh it is (إِن يَصدُّوكم). If you read it with kasra, you make the verb future; if with fatḥa, you make it past. If you make it a condition with kasra, that is fine, as in His saying ﴿أفَنَضْرِبُ عَنْكُمُ الذِّكْرَ صَفْحاً إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾, where [it is read] «أن» with fatḥa and with kasra. Likewise ﴿أَوْلِيَاءَ إِن اسْتَحَبُّوا الكُفْرَ عَلَى الإيمَانِ﴾ is read with kasra, and had it been with fatḥa it would have been correct. And His saying ﴿باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ أَلاَّ يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [admits] both fatḥa and kasra. As for His saying ﴿بَلِ اللّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُم أَنْ هَدَاكُمْ لِلإيمانِ﴾, (أَنْ) has fatḥa because its meaning is past, as though you said: "He has favoured you in that He guided you." Had you intended the future, kasra would be permissible in it; but fatḥa is the proper way because the first of the two verbs is past. If you say "I honoured you because you came to me (an ataytanī)," kasra of «أن» is not permissible, because the verb is past.
His saying: ﴿وَتَعَاوَنُواْ﴾ — it is in the position of the jussive, because it is a command, and it is not conjoined to ﴿تَعْتَدُواْ﴾.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِ﴾ — ﴿وَمَآ﴾ is in the position of the nominative by the verb whose agent is not named [i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive «حُرِّمت»].
﴿وَٱلْمُنْخَنِقَةُ﴾: that which was strangled and died and was not reached [in time to be slaughtered].
﴿وَٱلْمَوْقُوذَةُ﴾: that which was beaten until it died and was not ritually slaughtered.
﴿وَٱلْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ﴾: that which fell from the top of a mountain or into a well, and was not reached in time for its ritual slaughter.
﴿وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ﴾: that which was gored to death. All of that is forbidden if its ritual slaughter was not reached in time.
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ﴾ — accusative and nominative [are both possible].
﴿وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ﴾: what was slaughtered for the idols. (ما ذبح) is in the position of the nominative and nothing else.
﴿وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُواْ﴾ — nominative by the verb whose agent is not named. Al-istiqsām: there used to be arrows in the Kaʿba; on some of them [was written] "My Lord has commanded me", (and in its place: "My Lord has forbidden me"). When one of them wanted to travel, he would take out two arrows and shuffle them; if the one on which was "My Lord has commanded me" came out, he went out; and if the one on which was "My Lord has forbidden me" came out, he stayed and refrained from going out.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾ — the statement breaks off at «الفسق», and ﴿ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾ is accusative by (يئِس), not by «الفسق».
﴿اليومَ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطّيِّباتُ﴾ — (اليوم) is accusative by (أُحِلّ).
His saying: ﴿غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٍ لإِثْمٍ ﴾ is like His saying ﴿غير محلّى الصيد﴾ — He is saying: not deliberately inclining to sin. (غير) is accusative because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (مَنْ), and it comes out of the noun [the pronoun] that is in (اضطرّ).

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا عَلَّمْتُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْجَوَارِحِ﴾ — He means the dogs. And ﴿مُكَلِّبِينَ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) coming out of (لكم); by «مكلِّبين» He means the men who own the hunting dogs. One of them is called mukallib and kallāb. The position of (ما) is nominative.
His saying: ﴿تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ﴾: you train them not to eat their catch.
Then He, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿فَكُلُواْ مِمَّآ أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ — of what they have not eaten from. If it [the dog] has eaten, it is not lawful, because it held it only for itself.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾ — it is referred back to «الوجوه» [i.e. accusative, conjoined to the faces to be washed]. Al-Farrāʾ said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ related to me from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd, that he read (وأرجلكم) [as being] placed out of order [i.e. belonging, in meaning, with the washed limbs]. Al-Farrāʾ said: Muḥammad ibn Abān al-Qurashī related to me from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī, from a man, from ʿAlī, that he said: "The Book came down with wiping, and the Sunna is washing." Al-Farrāʾ said: Abū Shihāb related to me from a man, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: "Gabriel ﷺ came down to Muhammad — may Allah bless them both and all the prophets — with wiping." Al-Farrāʾ said: The Sunna is washing.
His saying: ﴿أَوْ جَآءَ أَحَدٌ مِّنْكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْغَائِطِ﴾ — an allusion to a man's going off alone when he wants to relieve himself.

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿ٱعْدِلُواْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾ — had (هو) not been in the utterance, (أقرب) would have been accusative. In this position the action is referred to by «هو» and by «ذلك»; both are fit. He said in another place: ﴿إِذَا نَاجَيْتُمُ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَىْ نَجْواكُم صَدَقَةً ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ﴾, and in [Sūrat] al-Ṣaff ﴿ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾. Had neither (هو) nor (ذلك) been in the utterance, it would have been accusative, as in His saying ﴿انْتَهُوا خَيْراً لَكُمْ﴾.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ أَنْبِيَآءَ﴾ — He means the seventy whom Moses chose to go with him to the mountain; He called them prophets for this reason.
﴿وَجَعَلَكُمْ مُّلُوكاً﴾ — He is saying: each of you is a king in his own house; no one enters upon him except with permission.
﴿وَآتَاكُمْ مَّا لَمْ يُؤْتِ أَحَداً مِّن ٱلْعَٱلَمِينَ﴾ — He shaded you with the white clouds and sent down to you manna and quails.

farraa:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الأَرْضَ المُقَدَّسَةَ﴾ — it is mentioned that the Holy Land is Damascus, Palestine (Filasṭūn) and part of al-Urdunn (with a doubled nūn).

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱذْهَبْ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَاتِلاۤ﴾ — He said (أنت); had (أنت) been dropped, so that it were said "idhhab wa-rabbuka fa-qātilā", it would have been correct, because in one of the two readings it is (إِنه يراكم وقبِيلُه) without (هو), while [the other] has «هو». But (اذهب أنت وربك) is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs. That is because conjoining [a noun] to a nominative noun that is only implied is disliked, for the nominative is hidden in the verb; it is not like the accusative, because the accusative appears: you say "ḍarabtuhu" and "ḍarabtuka", while for the nominative you say "qāma" and "qāmā", so that you do not see a noun separate from the verb in its basic form. That is why expressing it is preferred. Yet Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿أَئِذَا كُنّا تُرَاباً وَآبَاؤُنَا﴾ and did not say (نحن); and all of it is correct.
When you separate [the verb] from the conjoined noun by something on which the verb has fallen, it becomes fairly acceptable.
Of that is your saying: "I struck Zayd, and you [did too] (wa-anta)." Were there no "Zayd", you would say "qumtu anā wa-anta"; "qumtu wa-anta" is rare. Had it been (إِنا ها هنا قاعدين) [in the accusative], it would have been correct.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً﴾ — it is accusative by «التحريم» [i.e. by «مُحَرَّمة»]. Had you cut off the statement [after «عليهم»] and put it in the accusative by His saying (يَتِيهُونَ), it would have been correct.
Similar to it in speech is your saying: "la-uʿṭiyannaka thawban tarḍā" ("I will surely give you a garment you will be pleased with"): you put «ثوب» in the accusative by the giving; and had you put it in the accusative by «الرضا», cutting it off from (لأعطينك), it would have been correct. [Translator's note: «صوبا» in the text is evidently a misprint for «صوابا».]

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿فَتُقُبِّلَ مِن أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ ٱلآخَرِ قَالَ لأَقْتُلَنَّكَ﴾ — He did not say "the one from whom it was not accepted said (لأقتلنَّك)", because the meaning shows that the one from whom it was not accepted is the one who said, out of envy of his brother, "I will surely kill you." Similar to it in speech is your saying: "When the fool and the forbearing man come together, he is praised," meaning by the praise the forbearing one; and "When you see the wrongdoer and the wronged, you help," meaning "you help the wronged," because the meaning is unambiguous. But if you said "A man and a woman passed by me, and I helped," meaning one of them, it would not be permissible until you made it clear, because there is no sign in them by which one can infer where the help went — unless you mean: "and I helped them both."

farraa:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ﴾ — He means: it went along with him.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿مِنْ أَجْلِ ذٰلِكَ﴾ — it is the answer to [i.e. follows from] the son of Adam's killing his companion.
His saying: ﴿وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا﴾ — He is saying: whoever pardons it; "giving life" here is pardoning.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا جَزَآءُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ فَسَاداً أَن يُقَتَّلُوۤاْ أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوۤاْ أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ﴾ — (أن) is in the position of the nominative [as the khabar (predicate)].
When a man has shed blood, taken property and made the road unsafe, he is crucified. When he has killed but not taken property, he is killed. When he has taken property but not killed, his right hand and left foot are cut off "on opposite sides". In place of (مِن) [in «مِن خلاف»], «على», the bāʾ and the lām are also fit.
His banishment (nafy) is that it be proclaimed: "Whoever kills him, his blood may be shed with impunity." This is the banishment.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقْطَعُوۤاْ أَيْدِيَهُمَا﴾ — both are nominative by the pronoun that refers back to them. The accusative is permissible in them, just as "a-Zaydun ḍarabtahu?" and "a-Zaydan ḍarabtahu?" are permissible. The Arabs prefer the nominative in "the male thief and the female thief" only because they are [not] specific; so they were treated like a conditional, as in your saying: "Whoever steals, cut off his hand," where (من) can only be nominative. Had you meant a particular male thief or a particular female thief, the accusative would be the proper form of speech. Similar to it is ﴿واللذانِ يأتيانها مِنكم فآذوهما﴾. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "والسارقون والسارقات فاقطعوا أيمانهما".
He said (أيدِيهما) [plural] only because every single member of the human body, when mentioned as annexed to two or more, is put in the plural. Thus it is said: "I smashed their [two] heads (ruʾūsahumā)," and "I filled their [two] backs and bellies (ẓuhūrahumā wa-buṭūnahumā) with blows."
Similar to it is ﴿إِن تَتُوبَا إِلى الله فقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما﴾.
The plural was preferred over the dual only because most of the limbs in a human being come in twos: the two hands, the two feet and the two eyes. Since most of them follow this pattern, a single member, when annexed to two [persons], was treated in the manner of the dual. The dual is also permissible; Abū Dhuʾayb said:
فتخالسا نَفْسَيهِما بنوافذ * كنوافِذِ العُبُط التى لا ترقَع
(So the two snatched each other's lives with piercing thrusts, like the rents in [garments] torn fresh that cannot be patched.)
This is also permissible in what is not a part of the human body: you say to two men "khallaytumā nisāʾakumā" ("you have let your wives go"), meaning two women, and "kharaqtumā qumuṣakumā" ("you have torn your shirts").
I have mentioned that only because some grammarians used to permit it only for parts of the human body, whereas all are the same. It is also permissible to say in speech: "As for the male and female thief, cut off their right hand (yamīnahumā)," because the meaning is: the right hand of each of them; as the poet said:
كُلُوا فى نصف بطنِكم تعِيشوا * فإنَّ زمانكم زمن خمِيص
(Eat to half [the capacity] of your belly [singular] and you will live, for your time is a time of hunger.)
And another said:
الواردون وتَيْم فى ذرى سبأٍ * قد عضَّ أعناقهم جِلدُ الجوامِيس
(Those who come down to water, and Taym, in the shelter of Sabaʾ — the hide of the buffaloes [i.e. the yokes] has bitten their necks.)
Whoever says (ذَرَى) [darā] takes Sabaʾ as a people, and whoever says (ذُرَى) [durā] means a place.
It is permissible in speech to say: "Bring me the head of two sheep (raʾsa shātayni)" and "the head of a sheep". When you say "the head of a sheep", you mean two heads of this kind; and when you say "the head of two sheep", you mean by it the head of each sheep. The poet said, on another matter:
كأنه وَجْه تركِيَّينِ قد غضِبا * مستهدف لِطعانٍ غيرِ تذبيب
(As though it were the face [singular] of two Turks who have become angry, exposed to thrusts that do not falter.)

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ﴾ — if you wish, you can make His saying "سمَّاعون للكذب" nominative by «مِن» [i.e. as the mubtadaʾ (subject) with the prepositional phrase as its khabar (predicate)], without making (مِن) connected in meaning to what precedes it, as Allah said: ﴿فمِنهم ظالِم لِنفسِهِ ومِنهم مقتصِد﴾. And if you wish, the meaning is: "Let not those who hasten into unbelief grieve you — of these, and ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ﴾"; you then make (سمَّاعون) nominative as a fresh start (istiʾnāf). It is then like His saying ﴿لِيستأذِنكم الذِين ملكت أيمانُكُمْ والذِين لم يبلغوا الحُلُم مِنكم﴾, after which He, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿طوَّافون عليكم﴾. Had "sammāʿīna" and "ṭawwāfīna" been said, it would have been correct, as He said ﴿ملعونِين أينما ثُقِفوا﴾, and as He said ﴿إن المتَّقِين في جَنَّاتٍ وعُيونٍ﴾ and then said ﴿آخِذين، وفاكِهِين، ومتكئِين﴾. The accusative is more frequent. He also said, with the nominative: ﴿ كلاَّ إِنها لظى نزَّاعة لِلشوى﴾, putting (نزَّاعة) in the nominative as a fresh start, although it is an indefinite describing a definite. Likewise His saying ﴿لا تبقِى ولا تذر لَوَّاحَة﴾. And in the reading of Ubayy: "إِنها لإِحدا الكُبَر نِذير لِلبشرِ" without alif [i.e. nominative «نذير»]. So whatever of this kind comes to you in speech, you may put in the accusative or the nominative. Its accusative is by qaṭʿ (cutting off) or as a ḥāl (circumstantial). When praise or blame fits it, that is a third way; and when you put it in the accusative for blame or praise, it is fine to put its definite form in the accusative just as you did its indefinite. Likewise His saying ﴿سمَّاعون لِلكذبِ أكَّالون لِلسُّحتِ﴾ follows what I have mentioned to you.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَتَبْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيهَآ أَنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ بِٱلنَّفْسِ﴾ — (النفس) is put in the accusative because (أَنّ) falls on it. In His saying ﴿وَٱلْعَيْنَ بِٱلْعَيْنِ وَٱلأَنْفَ بِٱلأَنْفِ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَٱلْجُرُوحَ قِصَاصٌ﴾ you have the choice: if you wish, you use the nominative, and if you wish, the accusative. Ḥamza used the accusative and al-Kisāʾī the nominative. Al-Farrāʾ said: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Yaḥyā related to me from Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ read: (والعين بِالعين) in the nominative. Al-Farrāʾ said: If you put «العين» in the nominative, the rest of the statement follows «العين»; and if you put it in the accusative, that is permissible. Some used to put all of it in the accusative, and when they reached ﴿وَٱلْجُرُوحَ قِصَاصٌ﴾ they used the nominative. All is correct; except that the nominative and accusative in what is conjoined to inna and anna are easy only when there are verbs [i.e. predicates] with the nouns, as in His saying ﴿وإذا قيل إن وعد اللّهِ حق والساعة لا ريب فِيها﴾: the accusative was easy because after «الساعة» comes its khabar. Similar is ﴿إن الأرض لِلّهِ يورِثها من يشاء مِن عبادِهِ والعاقِبة لِلمتقِين﴾, and similar is ﴿وإِن الظالِمِين بعضُهم أولياءُ بعضٍ والله وَلِىُّ المتقِين﴾. But when there is no khabar after the second noun, you put it in the nominative, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿أنَّ الله برئ مِن المشرِكِين ورسوله﴾ and His saying ﴿فإن الله هو مولاه وجِبرِيل وصالِح المؤمِنين﴾. Likewise you say: "inna akhāka qāʾimun wa-Zaydun" — you put (زيد) in the nominative by making it follow the implied pronoun in «قائم». Build on this. [Translator's note: «نصبنه» in the text is evidently for «نصبته».]
His saying: ﴿فَمَن تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَّهُ﴾ — He referred (to [the act] with «هو»); this is [done] with an act from which faʿala and yafʿalu are formed, as you say: "The caravan has arrived, and I was glad of it," meaning: of its arrival.
His saying ﴿كَفَّارَةٌ لَّهُ﴾ — He means: [an expiation] for the one who inflicted the wound and committed the offence, and a reward for the wounded one.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ ٱلإِنجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدًى﴾, then He said ﴿وَمُصَدِّقاً﴾ — if you wish, you can make ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ a description of Jesus, and if you wish, a description of the Gospel.
His saying ﴿وَهُدًى وَمَوْعِظَةً لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ follows «المصدّق» in its accusative; had you put it in the nominative, making it follow His saying ﴿فِيهِ هُدًى وَنُورٌ﴾, it would have been correct.

farraa:47-47.t: His saying: ﴿وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ ٱلإِنْجِيلِ﴾ — Ḥamza and others read it with the accusative, the lām being taken in the sense of «كى» (in order that). And ﴿وَلْيَحْكُمْ﴾ has been read with the jussive, as a lām of command.

farraa:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنِ ٱحْكُم بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ — this is evidence that His saying (وليحكم) is jussive, because it is speech in which one part is conjoined to another.

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾ — it is a fresh start, in the nominative. Had it been put in the accusative, referring it back to His saying ﴿فعسى الله أَن يأْتِى بِالفتحِ أَو أَمرٍ مِن عِندِهِ﴾, it would have been correct. In the codices of the people of Medina it is (يقول الذين آمنوا) without the wāw.

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — genitive: you make it a naʿt (adjective) for (لقوم). Had you put it in the accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off) from their pronouns in ﴿يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ﴾, it would have been a valid way. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (أَذلَّة على المؤمنين غلظاء على الكافرين). "Adhilla" means: merciful to them.

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلْكُفَّارَ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾ — in the reading of Ubayy: (ومن الكفار). Whoever puts it in the accusative refers it back to ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ﴾.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فَاسِقُونَ﴾ — (أنّ) is in the position of the accusative, on the basis of His saying ﴿هَلْ تَنقِمُونَ مِنَّآ﴾ [anything] except our faith and your iniquity. (أن) is in the position of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Had you begun afresh, (وإن اكثركم فاسقون), with kasra, it would have been correct.

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذٰلِكَ مَثُوبَةً﴾ — (مثوبة) is accusative because it is explanatory [i.e. tamyīz (specification)], as in His saying ﴿أَنا أَكثر مِنك مالا وأَعزُّ نَفَرا﴾.
His saying: ﴿مَن لَّعَنَهُ ٱللَّهُ ﴾ — (من) is in the position of the genitive, referring it back to (بِشرّ). If you wish, you can begin afresh with it and put it in the nominative, as He said: ﴿قل أَفَأُنبئكم بِشر مِن ذلِكم النار وعدها الله الذِين كفروا﴾. You could also put (من) in the accusative according to your saying "I will inform you of (من)", as you say "I informed you of good" and "I informed you that Zayd was standing (Zaydan qāʾiman)". But the proper way is the genitive.
His saying ﴿وَعَبَدَ ٱلطَّاغُوتَ﴾ is on the basis of His saying: "and He made of them apes [and swine] and whoever worshipped the ṭāghūt". In the reading of Ubayy and ʿAbdallāh it is (وعبدوا), in the plural. The companions of ʿAbdallāh used to read "وعَبَد الطاغوتِ" on the pattern faʿal, annexing it to «الطاغوت», and explaining it as: the servants of the ṭāghūt. Some people intended this meaning and gave the ʿayn a ḍamma, saying "ʿubudu al-ṭāghūti", like thimār and thumur — a plural of a plural.
Had a reader read (وعَبَد الطاغوتِ), it would be correct and good: he would mean "ʿabadat al-ṭāghūt" ("worshippers of the ṭāghūt"), dropping the hāʾ [i.e. the tāʾ marbūṭa] because of the annexation; as the poet said:
* قام وُلاَها فسقَوها صَرْخدا *
(Her keepers rose and gave her Ṣarkhad wine to drink.)
He means: wulātuhā. As for His saying (وعَبُد الطاغوت): if there is a dialect form in it like ḥadhir and ḥadhur and ʿajul, then it is a valid way; otherwise he meant — and Allah knows best — [what is in] the poet's saying:
أَبَنِى لُبَيْنَى إِنّ أمَّكُمُ * أَمَةٌ وإِن أباكم عَبُد
(O sons of Lubaynā, your mother is a slave-woman and your father is a slave.)
This is permissible in poetry by the necessity of rhymes; but in Quranic reading it is not.

farraa:64-64.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ يَدُ ٱللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ﴾ — they meant: withheld from spending and from bestowing abundantly upon us. It is like His saying ﴿ولا تجعلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلى عُنُقك ولا تَبْسُطْها كلَّ البَسْطِ﴾, concerning spending.
﴿بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ﴾ — in the text of ʿAbdallāh: (بل يداه بُِسْطَانِ). The Arabs say: "Meet your brother with an open (mabsūṭ) face," and "with an open (busṭ / basṭ) face."

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿لأَكَلُواْ مِن فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِم﴾ — He is saying: from the rain of the sky and the growth of the earth, its fruits and other things. It is also said that this is by way of [expressing] abundance, as you say: "He is in good from his head to his foot."

farraa:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ وَٱلصَّابِئُونَ وَٱلنَّصَارَىٰ﴾ — (الصابِئين) is put in the nominative as being conjoined to (الذين). (الذين) is a word with one form in its nominative, accusative and genitive; so since its case-form is one, and since the accusative of (إنّ) is a weak accusative — its weakness being that it falls on (the noun and does not fall on) its khabar (predicate) — the nominative of «الصابئين» became permissible.
I do not like to say "inna ʿAbdallāhi wa-Zaydun qāʾimāni", because the case is visible in «عبدالله». Al-Kisāʾī used to permit it, because of the weakness of inna. They have recited this verse to us both with the nominative and with the accusative:
فمن يك أمسى بالمدينةِ رحلُهُ * فإنِى وقَيَّارا بها لغرِيب
(Whoever has his lodging in Medina [is at home], but I and Qayyār are strangers there.)
— and «وقَيَّارٌ». This is not evidence for al-Kisāʾī in his permitting "inna ʿAmran wa-Zaydun qāʾimāni", because «قيار» has been conjoined to a pronoun, and the pronoun has no [visible] case-ending; so that was made easy (in it, just as it was made easy) in (الذين) when (الصابئون) is conjoined to it. Indeed this is stronger in permissibility than (الصابئون), because the nominative is never visible in the pronoun, whereas with (الذين) one sometimes says «اللذون», so that it is nominative in one case.
Someone recited to me:
وإلاَّ فاعلموا أَنَّا وأَنتم * بُغَاة ما حيِينا فى شِقاقِ
(Otherwise know that we and you [nominative] are rebels, as long as we live, in discord.)
And another said:
يا ليتنى وأَنتِ يا لَمِيسُ * ببلدٍ ليس به أنِيس
(Would that I and you, O Lamīs, were in a land where there is no one.)
And someone recited to me:
يا ليتنى وهما نخلو بمنزِلةٍ * حتى يرى بعضُنا بعضا ونأتلِف
(Would that I and they [two] were alone in some place, until we could see one another and be reconciled.)
Al-Kisāʾī said: I put (الصابِئون) in the nominative by making it follow the noun [the pronoun] in «هادوا», taking it from His saying (إنا هدنا إليك) ("we have turned back to You"), not from Judaism. But the exegesis came otherwise, because He described those who believed with their mouths while their hearts did not believe, then mentioned the Jews and the Christians and said: whoever of them believes shall have such-and-such; so He made them Jews and Christians. [Translator's note: «يأفواههم» in the text is evidently a misprint for «بأفواههم».]

farraa:71-71.t:
His saying: ﴿فَعَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ ثُمَّ تَابَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ﴾ — the nominative of «الكثير» can be from two directions. One is that you repeat the verb upon it, meaning: "many of them became blind and deaf." And if you wish, you make ﴿عَمُوا وصَمُّوا﴾ the verb of «الكثير», as the poet said:
يلوموننى فى اشترائى النخيـ * لَ أَهلِى فكلُّهم أَلْوَمُ
(They blame me for buying the palm trees — my family — and all of them are most blameworthy.)
This is for one who says "qāmū qawmuka" ("your people stood", with the plural verb before the agent). And if you wish, you make «الكثير» a maṣdar (verbal noun) and say: i.e. that is much [found] among them; this is a third way. Had it been put in the accusative in this sense, it would have been correct. Similar to it is the poet's saying:
وسوَّد ماءُ المَرْدِ فاها فلونه * كَلَون النَؤُور وهى أدماء سارُها
(The juice of the unripe fruit has blackened her mouth, so that its colour is like the colour of kohl-soot, while she is tawny — most of her.)
Similar to it is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وأَسَرّوا النَّجْوَى الذِين ظلموا﴾ — if you wish, you make (وأسَرّوا) a verb for His saying ﴿لاهِيةً قلوبُهم وأسَرّوا النجوى﴾ and then begin (الذين) afresh in the nominative. If you wish, you make it genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «الناس» in His saying "اقترب لِلناسِ حِسابهم". And if you wish, it is nominative, just as "dhahabū qawmuka" is permissible.

farraa:101-101.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ تَسْأَلُواْ عَنْ أَشْيَآءَ إِن تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ﴾ — the Prophet ﷺ addressed the people and told them that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, had made the Hajj obligatory for them. A man stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, (is it) every year?" He turned away from him.
Then he repeated (and said: "Is it every year?" He turned away from him; then he repeated it), and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "What makes you safe from my saying (yes), so that it becomes obligatory for you, and then you do not do it and so disbelieve? Leave me alone as long as I leave you alone."
(أشياء) is in the position of the genitive and is diptote (lā tujrā). Some grammarians have said of it: it became frequent in speech while being [on the pattern] (afʿāl), and so it resembled faʿlāʾ and was not declined, just as ḥamrāʾ is not declined; and its plural is ashāwā — as they made the plural of ʿadhrāʾ ʿadhārā and of ṣaḥrāʾ ṣaḥārā — and ashyāwāt, as one says ḥamrāwāt. But if it were by mere fancied analogy (tawahhum), the stronger of the two ways would be to decline it, because when a word is frequently used it becomes light; just as naming people Yazīd became frequent and so they declined it, although it has an augment yāʾ that prevents declension. Rather, we hold that ashyāʾ was formed as a plural on the pattern afʿilāʾ, as layyin has the plural alyināʾ; a hamza was dropped from the middle of ashyāʾ, which should have been ashyiʾāʾ, and the hamza was dropped because of its frequency. The Arabs have said: "This is of the abnāwāt of Saʿd," and "I commend you to the protection of the asmāwāt of Allah," whose singulars asmāʾ and abnāʾ are declined. So if I denied ashyāʾ declension because they made its plural ashyāwāt, I would have to decline neither asmāʾ nor abnāʾ, since they were made plural as asmāwāt and abnāwāt.

farraa:103-103.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن بَحِيرَةٍ وَلاَ سَآئِبَةٍ وَلاَ وَصِيلَةٍ وَلاَ حَامٍ﴾ — there has been disagreement about the sāʾiba. It was said: a man would set loose (yusayyib) whatever he wished of his property and take it to those who attended to the service of their gods. Some said: the sāʾiba is when a she-camel has borne ten litters, all of them female; she was set loose, not ridden, her hair not shorn, and none drank her milk except her offspring or a guest, until she died. When she died, men and women ate her, and the ear of her daughter's daughter was slit (buḥirat) — he means: pierced. So the baḥīra is the daughter of the sāʾiba, and she has the same status as her mother. As for the waṣīla, it is from sheep: when a ewe had borne seven litters of female kids in pairs, and in her seventh bore a female kid and a male kid, it was said: "She has joined (waṣalat) her brother"; so women did not drink her milk, which was for the men, and she was treated like the sāʾiba.
As for the ḥāmī, it is the stallion camel: when the offspring of his offspring had conceived, his back was protected (ḥamā); he was not ridden, his hair was not shorn, he was not kept from any pasture, and whatever camels he covered, he was not kept away from them.
So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿مَا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن بَحِيرَةٍ﴾ — it is you who made it so.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ لاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.

farraa:105-105.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ — this is a command from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as in your saying: "Look after yourselves." The Arabs give commands using prepositions (ṣifāt) such as ʿalayka, ʿindaka, dūnaka and ilayka. They say "ilayka ilayka," meaning "Get back," as you say "warāʾaka warāʾaka". These particles are many. Al-Kisāʾī claimed that he heard "baynakumā al-baʿīra fa-khudhāhu" ("Between you two is the camel — take it"); so he permitted it with all the prepositions that can stand alone, but did not permit it with the lām, the bāʾ or the kāf.
