The clause ﴿قال الله﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause ﴿يا عيسى ابن مريم﴾ is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿أأنت قلت للناس اتخذوني وأمي إلهين من دون الله﴾: The hamza is interrogative; «أنت» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «قلت للناس» is the khabar (predicate); the interrogative clause is the object of the saying. The clause «اتخذوني», made up of the imperative verb, the fāʿil (agent) and the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying. ﴿وأمي﴾: the wāw is for accompaniment or conjunction, and «أمي» is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment) or conjoined to the yāʾ; «إلهين» is the second direct object of «اتخذوني»; and «من دون الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «إلهين», i.e. «كائنين من دونه تعالى» ("being apart from Him, Exalted is He"), or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of «اتخذوني», i.e. «متجاوزين» ("going beyond [Him]").
﴿قال سبحانك﴾: «قال» is a past verb; «سبحانك»: it stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative by an omitted verb, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; together with its omitted verb it is a parenthetical clause with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿قال سبحانك...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق﴾: «ما» is negating; «يكون» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; «لي» is a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the omitted khabar of «يكون», placed first; and ﴿أن﴾ with what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) that is the noun of «يكون», placed later. The clause ﴿ما يكون لي...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿ليس﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the noun of «ليس» is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «هو» ("it"); ﴿بحق﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition, and «حق» is the khabar of «ليس»; «لي» is a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it has been placed before what it qualifies. «ما» is a relative noun, the object of ﴿أقول﴾, because it comprises the meaning of a sentence.
﴿إن كنت قلته فقد علمته﴾: The clause is resumptive with no grammatical position. «إن» is conditional; «كنت» is an incomplete past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and the incomplete verb is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause ﴿قلته﴾ is the khabar of «كنت»; the fāʾ is linking; the clause «قد علمته» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the jussive-governing condition; and «علمته» is a verb, its fāʿil and a direct object.
﴿تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك﴾: The clause is resumptive with no grammatical position. «ما» is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a direct object; «في نفسي» is a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted [verb that is the] ṣila of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿لا أعلم ما في نفسك﴾ is conjoined to what preceded.
﴿إنك أنت علام الغيوب﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and the kāf is its noun; «أنت» is a mubtadaʾ and «علام الغيوب» is the khabar, and the clause is the khabar of ﴿إن﴾; or ﴿أنت﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and «علام» is the khabar of ﴿إن﴾. The clause «إنك» with what follows it has no grammatical position because it is causal (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:117-117.t:
﴿ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به﴾: «ما» is negating; «قلت» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «لهم» is attached to «قلت»; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «ما» is a relative noun, the object of «قلت»; and the clause «أمرتني به» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿أن اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم﴾: ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar from «أن اعبدوا» is a badal (substitute) from ﴿ما﴾, or from the hāʾ in ﴿به﴾, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) whose implied form is «هو» ("it is"); the clause ﴿اعبدوا الله﴾ is the ṣila of the maṣdar-forming ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿أن﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause after it is explicative with no grammatical position. ﴿ربي﴾ is a badal from ﴿الله﴾ or a naʿt (adjective).
﴿وكنت عليهم شهيدا ما دمت فيهم﴾: The wāw is a conjunction; «كنت» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb (kāna and its sisters), the tāʾ is its noun and «شهيدًا» is its khabar; ﴿عليهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to ﴿شهيدًا﴾. ﴿ما دمت﴾ is an incomplete past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and «فيهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to its omitted khabar; the adverb formed from ﴿ما دمت﴾ is attached to ﴿شهيدًا﴾, i.e. «مدة دوامي مستقرًّا فيهم» ("for the duration of my remaining among them").
﴿فلما توفيتني كنت أنت الرقيب عليهم﴾: The fāʾ is resumptive. «لما» is temporal (ḥīniyya), or linking [Translator's note: so in the source, «أو رابطة»], in which case it is an adverb; or it is a particle comprising the sense of condition. The clause «توفيتني» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), or has no grammatical position; «توفيتني» is a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. You took me fully by raising me to heaven. The clause ﴿كنت﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. «كنت» is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; «أنت» is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun in «كنت», or a detached pronoun with no grammatical position [Translator's note: i.e. a separating pronoun, ḍamīr faṣl]; «الرقيب»: the khabar of «كنت»; «عليهم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to «الرقيب».
﴿وأنت على كل شيء شهيد﴾: The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «أنت» is a mubtadaʾ and «شهيد» is the khabar; «على كل شيء» is a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to «شهيد»; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position, or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: (يا) is for the vocative. According to Sībawayh the vocative particles are five: يا, أيا, هيّا, أي and the alif [hamza]. «ها» is for alerting (tanbīh), and (أيّ) is a singular one addressed (munādā mufrad), and the naʿt (adjective) is necessary to it in order to make it clear. الَّذِينَ is a naʿt of أيّ; one also says «الّذون». آمَنُوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; its original form is «أأمنوا», and the second hamza was lightened; it is not permitted to combine the two in one word except in [the pattern] faʿʿāl. أَوْفُوا is jussive (majzūm) according to the Kufans, who imply the lām [of command], and not declinable (ghayr muʿrab) according to the Basrans, because it does not resemble [the noun as the imperfect does]. بِالْعُقُودِ is genitive by the bāʾ; it is the plural of ʿaqd. One says: ʿaqadtu the rope and the covenant, and aʿqadtu the honey. By this it became obligatory to fulfil every oath, guarantee of safety, sale and hire, so long as it is not unlawful. أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ الْأَنْعامِ: the noun of that whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), i.e. eating them and benefiting from them has been made lawful for you. The Banū Tamīm say «بهيمة». [Translator's note: the source does not show how the Tamīmī pronunciation differs; it is reproduced as written.]
إِلَّا ما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ: in the position of an accusative by exception; according to Sībawayh it is like the object, and according to Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] it has the sense of "I excepted". Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: nothing is permissible except what Sībawayh said, and what Abū al-ʿAbbās said is not sound. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the nominative is permissible by making it the conjunctive «إلا», and the accusative, in his view, is by إنّ. غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what is in أوفوا. Al-Akhfash said:
i.e. "O you who believe, fulfil the contracts, not making game lawful". Others said: a ḥāl from the kāf and mīm, the implied form being "the beasts of livestock have been made lawful for you, you not making game lawful". The original form is محلّين; the nūn was omitted for lightness, and the yāʾ is omitted in continuous speech because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
إِنَّ اللَّهَ: the noun of «إنّ»; يَحْكُمُ is in the position of the khabar, i.e. among His servants.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ: these are the marks; it has been said they are the sacrificial camels that are marked (mushʿara), i.e. given a sign, i.e. do not treat them as lawful before their due place; and it has been said they are the marks between the area outside the sanctuary and the sanctuary — do not pass beyond them without being in iḥrām. وَلَا الشَّهْرَ الْحَرامَ: conjoined, and likewise وَلَا الْهَدْيَ وَلَا الْقَلائِدَ وَلَا آمِّينَ. It has been said: all of this is abrogated; and it has been said: it was forbidden to them to touch the offerings and the garlands before the offering reached its place. It is reported from al-Aʿmash: ولا آمّي البيت الحرام, with the nūn omitted and the construct (iḍāfa).
يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ: in the position of an accusative, i.e. "seeking (مبتغين)". Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read وَلا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ with a ḍamma on the yāʾ. Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialectal forms; the Basrans do not know the ḍamma in this sense — that is said only of committing crime (ijrām). أَنْ صَدُّوكُمْ: in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "because they barred you". Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read it as أَنْ صَدُّوكُمْ with a kasra on إن [i.e. إن صدّوكم], and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. It is reported from al-Aʿmash: إن يصدّوكم; this reading is not permissible by the consensus of the grammarians except in poetry, according to some of them, because when «إن» governs [the jussive], its apodosis must have the fāʾ and the verb — even though Sībawayh recited: [al-Rajaz metre] 116-
إنّك إن يصرع أخوك تصرع
(If your brother is thrown down, you will be thrown down.)
— he only permitted it in poetry, and his statement has been rejected. As for «إن صدّوكم» with a kasra on «إن», the eminent scholars of grammar, hadith and reasoning forbid reading with it for several reasons. Among them: this verse was revealed in the year of the Conquest, the year eight, while the idolaters had barred the believers in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya, the year six; so the barring was before the verse, and if it is read with a kasra it can only be after it, just as you say: "Do not give so-and-so anything if he fights you" — this can only be for the future, whereas if you use the fatḥa it is for the past. On this basis only أن صدّوكم is permissible. Further, even if this report were not sound, the fatḥa would be obligatory, because His words, the Exalted, لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ to the end of the verse show that Mecca was in their hands, and that they are not forbidden this except when they are able to bar [others] from the Sacred House; so from this it is necessary to read «أن» with a fatḥa, because it is for what is past. Further, if it were for the future it would be unlikely linguistically, because if you said to a man who fears from another insult, beating and killing: "Do not be angry if so-and-so beats you", that would be unlikely, because you would be implying that he is angered by beating alone. أَنْ تَعْتَدُوا: in the position of an accusative because it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "let not the hatred of a people earn you transgression". Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd rejected «شنان» with a sukūn on the nūn, because maṣdars (verbal nouns) in a case like this come only with a vowelled [middle letter]; others disagreed with them and said: this is not a maṣdar but an active participle on the pattern of كسلان and غضبان. Al-Akhfash said: then He said عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوى, cutting it off from the beginning of the speech.
إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ: the noun of إنّ and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ: the noun of that whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), and what follows it is conjoined to it; in what follows, the accusative is also permissible, in the sense of "and Allah has forbidden to you the blood". The original pattern of دم is faʿal; evidence for this is the poet's words: [al-Wāfir metre] 117-
جرى الدميان بالخبر اليقين
(The two bloods flowed with the certain news.)
It is from دمي يدمى, like حذر يحذر. It has been said: its pattern is faʿl, with a sukūn on the middle radical.
وَالنَّطِيحَةُ has the [feminine] hāʾ, even though it is turned from mafʿūla, because no noun precedes it. Likewise one says:
خضيبة; but if you mention a feminine [noun] you say: "I saw a dyed hand (كفّا خضيبا)". This is al-Farrāʾ's view. The Basrans say:
it was made a noun, so the hāʾ was omitted from it, like الذبيحة. [Translator's note: so in the source; النطيحة in fact keeps the hāʾ, so "omitted" is probably a slip for "kept".] It has also been said: it is in the sense of ناطحة (goring). Al-Farrāʾ said: the people of Najd say «السبع», dropping the ḍamma. إِلَّا ما ذَكَّيْتُمْ: in the position of an accusative by exception. وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُوا بِالْأَزْلامِ: its literal meaning in the language is "that you seek a portion (division) by means of arrows". Al-Akhfash and Abū ʿUbayda said:
the singular of الأزلام is زلم and زلم. ذلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). الْيَوْمَ: an adverb, governed by يئس; the implied form is: "Today those who disbelieve have despaired of changing your religion and turning you away from it", because of what they saw of your clear insight into its soundness and your delight in it. الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ: by this He indicated that faith and Islam are many things; this is contrary to the view of the Murjiʾa. فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ: (من) is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; the implied form is "then Allah is, to him, Forgiving, Merciful"; then له was omitted. Sībawayh recited: [al-Rajaz metre] 118-
قد أصبحت أمّ الخيار تدّعى ... عليّ ذنبا كلّه لم أصنع
(Umm al-Khiyār has come to accuse me of a sin, all of which I did not commit.)
اضْطُرَّ is in the position of a jussive by the condition, except that it is a past verb on which no governor acts [overtly]. The kasra and the ḍamma of the nūn are both permissible. Ibn Muḥayṣin read فمن اطّرّ, and this is a solecism (laḥn), because the ḍād has spreading (tafashshī) and is not assimilated into anything. غَيْرَ مُتَجانِفٍ: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). And if you wish, a kasra on the nūn in «فمن», according to the basic rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: يَسْئَلُونَكَ ماذا أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ: ما is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is الْمَيْتَةُ وَالدَّمُ, ذا being redundant (zāʾida). [Translator's note: so in the source; the khabar would ordinarily be أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ.] If you wish, it [ذا] is in the sense of الذي, and the khabar is قُلْ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّباتُ. [Translator's note: the text here appears disordered in the source (one would expect the khabar to be أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ); it is translated as written.] الطيبات: i.e. the lawful; nothing unlawful is good. It has been said: the good is what its eater and drinker enjoy and from which no harm comes to him in this world or the Hereafter. وَما عَلَّمْتُمْ مِنَ الْجَوارِحِ: al-Akhfash said: its singular is jāriḥa. مُكَلِّبِينَ: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). فَكُلُوا مِمَّا أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ: the original form is أمسكنه; the hāʾ was omitted because of the length of the noun. In this and in what precedes it there is evidence that if the hunting animal eats [of the game], it is not to be eaten. وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ: mentioning is with the tongue; and it has been said: with the heart. What the language requires is that it be with the tongue literally and with the heart figuratively.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
مُحْصِنِينَ.
accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). غَيْرَ مُسافِحِينَ: likewise; and if you wish, it is a naʿt (adjective). وَلا مُتَّخِذِي أَخْدانٍ: conjoined to مسافحين; it may not be conjoined to محصنين. وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالْإِيمانِ: a condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَقَدْ حَبِطَ عَمَلُهُ. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: i.e. whoever changes anything that Allah has made lawful and makes it unlawful, or makes unlawful anything that Allah has made lawful, his deeds have come to nothing, i.e. he is not rewarded for them.
وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ: the adverbial phrase may not be attached to (mutaʿalliq) الخاسرين, for it would then enter into the ṣila (relative clause); rather it is attached to the maṣdar, and we have mentioned its like earlier. As for the statement of Mujāhid, reported from him by Ibn Jurayj, on the words of Allah the Exalted وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالْإِيمانِ — he said "in Allah" — its meaning is: whoever disbelieves in faith disbelieves in Allah, and his deeds come to nothing. The evidence for that is that Sufyān reported from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād from Mujāhid, who said: "Faith is word and deed; it increases and decreases."

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلاةِ: Zayd ibn Aslam said: i.e. when you rise from sleep to the prayer. Others said: there is an omission in the speech, i.e. when you rise to the prayer having broken your ablution. It has been said: it was obligatory for everyone who rose to the prayer to prepare [i.e. purify himself] for it, then that was abrogated. وَامْسَحُوا بِرُؤُسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ: whoever reads it in the accusative makes it conjoined to the first, i.e. "and wash your feet". We have [already] mentioned the genitive,
except that al-Akhfash and Abū ʿUbayda hold that the genitive is by proximity (ʿalā al-jiwār), the meaning being washing.
Al-Akhfash said: and like it is «هذا جحر ضب خرب» (this is the hole of a lizard, ruined). This view is a great mistake, because proximity [attraction] may not be used as a basis for analogy in speech; it is only an error, and its counterpart is iqwāʾ [a fault in the rhyme vowel]. Among the best of what has been said is that wiping and washing are both obligatory: wiping is obligatory according to the reading of whoever reads with the genitive, and washing is obligatory according to the reading of whoever reads with the accusative, the two readings being like two verses. According to some of them there is a fronting and postponing in the verse; he said: the implied order is: "When you rise to the prayer, or one of you comes from the privy, or you have touched women, then wash your faces and your hands to the elbows and wipe your heads and your feet to the ankles." وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ جُنُباً: i.e. possessors of janāba, because جنب is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it is singular; if you pluralise it you say جنوب, أجناب and جناب. Thaʿlab and Muḥammad ibn Jarīr reported: أجنب الرجل, جنب and اجتنب, and the maṣdar is الجنابة and الإجناب. فَاطَّهَّرُوا: the original form is فتطهّروا; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ because they are both from the roots of the upper front teeth and the tip of the tongue, and the connecting alif was brought to reach the quiescent letter. Al-Zuhrī read أو جاء أحد منكم من الغيط. وَلكِنْ يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ: the lām of purpose (lām kay), i.e. His will is to purify you from sins. وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ: with the reward.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمِيثاقَهُ الَّذِي واثَقَكُمْ بِهِ: it has been said: this is the covenant in His words, Mighty and Majestic, وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ [al-Aʿrāf: 172]; and it has been said: this is the covenant that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took from them at the Pledge of Riḍwān.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: شُهَداءَ: i.e. making [the truth] clear. It is accusative as a second khabar (predicate) of كونوا; it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of قوامين, or a badal (substitute). It is diptote because it has the feminine alif. عَلى أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا: accusative by أن; «لا» does not come between the governor and what it governs [so as to block it], because it may occur as redundant (zāʾida). اعْدِلُوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوى: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ: when you say وعد it is only for good, and أوعد is for evil, unless it is specified. لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ: nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject). وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ: conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: وَلَقَدْ: a lām of emphasis. أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ: it is the one that Moses ﷺ had taken from them. وَبَعَثْنا مِنْهُمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ نَقِيباً: accusative by بعثنا, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ. اثنا عشر is declined, alone among its sisters [the compound numbers], because the dual is not made indeclinable (mabnī). وَقالَ اللَّهُ إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ: «إن» has a kasra because it begins [a new clause]; معكم is accusative because it is an adverb (ẓarf). لَئِنْ أَقَمْتُمُ الصَّلاةَ: a lām of emphasis whose meaning is the oath; likewise لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْكُمْ, and likewise وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ: «ما» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and نَقْضِهِمْ is genitive by the bāʾ; outside the Quran its nominative is permissible, i.e. "for that which is their breaking". يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ عَنْ مَواضِعِهِ: i.e. they interpret it according to their [own] interpretation. يُحَرِّفُونَ is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "We made their hearts hard, [they] distorting". It has been said: the meaning of "We made their hearts hard" is "We described them thus"; there is much like this, reported by Sībawayh and others, and we have mentioned it.
وَلا تَزالُ تَطَّلِعُ عَلى خائِنَةٍ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا: an exception from the hāʾ and mīm in خائنة منهم. Qatāda said: خائنة means treachery (خيانة). فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاصْفَحْ: a command, with two views on its meaning. One: pardon them and overlook as long as there is a covenant between you and them — and they are the protected people (ahl al-dhimma). The other view is that it is abrogated by His words, the Exalted: وَإِمَّا تَخافَنَّ مِنْ قَوْمٍ خِيانَةً فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلى سَواءٍ [al-Anfāl: 58].

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا إِنَّا نَصارى أَخَذْنا مِيثاقَهُمْ: Saʿīd al-Akhfash said: this is as you say: "From Zayd I took his dirham". Abū Jaʿfar said: the grammarians do not permit "أخذنا ميثاقهم من الذين قالوا إنا نصارى" (We took their covenant from those who said "We are Christians"), nor "ألينها لبست من الثياب", lest a pronoun precede the overt noun [it refers to]. [Translator's note: the second example appears to be garbled in the source; it is reproduced as written.]
فَنَسُوا حَظًّا مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ: i.e. they abandoned a portion of the Book with which they were admonished and reminded, and they made that abandonment and distortion a cause for disbelieving in Muhammad ﷺ. The plural of حظ is حظوظ; it has been heard from the Arabs: أحظ with a sukūn on the ḥāʾ, the original form being أحظظ, and a yāʾ was substituted for the ḍād; and أحاظ has been heard from them. [Translator's note: the source says "ḍād", but the letter in حظ is ẓāʾ.] فَأَغْرَيْنا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَداوَةَ وَالْبَغْضاءَ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ: it has been said: the Christians are meant by it; and it has been said:
the Jews and the Christians, because both have been mentioned before. It is more fitting that it be the Christians, because they are nearer [in the text].
The best of what has been said about the meaning of فَأَغْرَيْنا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَداوَةَ وَالْبَغْضاءَ is that Allah the Exalted commanded enmity towards the disbelievers and hating them, so each sect is commanded to have enmity towards the other and to hate it, because they are disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
Al-Ḥasan read قَدْ جاءَكُمْ رَسُولُنا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ.
He assimilated the nūn into the lām because of its closeness to it. يُبَيِّنُ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَيَعْفُوا عَنْ كَثِيرٍ is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: يَهْدِي بِهِ اللَّهُ: with a ḍamma on the hāʾ according to the original form; whoever uses a kasra substitutes a kasra for the ḍamma so as not to combine a ḍamma and a kasra. سُبُلَ السَّلامِ: a second object; the original form is إلى سبل السلام.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصارى نَحْنُ أَبْناءُ اللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّاؤُهُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Allah the Exalted refuted this against them, saying: قُلْ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُمْ بِذُنُوبِكُمْ. So they could not escape one of two positions: either they say "He punishes us", and it is said to them: "Then you are not His sons and His beloved"; or they say "He does not punish us", and so they give the lie to what is in their scriptures and what their messengers brought, and they make acts of disobedience permissible. بَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ: mubtadaʾ and khabar.
يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made known whom He forgives — that it is whoever repents and believes — and has made known whom He punishes — whoever disbelieves and persists. Since its meaning was known, it came in general terms, and He, Mighty and Majestic, did not say:
"He forgives whom He wills of you."

nahhas-irab:19-20.t:
أَنْ تَقُولُوا: in the position of an accusative, i.e. "out of aversion (كراهة) that you say". مِنْ بَشِيرٍ وَلا نَذِيرٍ is [also] permissible [in the nominative] according to the position [of the noun].
ʿUbayd ibn ʿAqīl reported from Shibl ibn ʿAbbād from ʿAbdullāh ibn Kathīr that he read يا قوم اذكروا with a ḍamma on the mīm (يا قومُ), and likewise whatever resembles it; its implied form is "O you people (يا أيّها القوم)", as [the poet] said: [al-Basīṭ metre] 119-
ويلا عليك وويلا منك يا رجل
(Woe upon you, and woe from you, O man!)
إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ أَنْبِياءَ: diptote because it has the feminine alif. وَجَعَلَكُمْ مُلُوكاً: it has been said: you own your affairs and no overpowerer overpowers you in them; and it has been said: He made you possessors of dwellings into which no one enters upon you except with permission. Anas ibn ʿIyāḍ reported from Zayd ibn Aslam from Anas ibn Mālik — I know him only to have said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever has a dwelling — or he said: a house — in which he takes shelter, and a wife, and a servant who serves him, is a king." ما لَمْ يُؤْتِ أَحَداً مِنَ الْعالَمِينَ: the yāʾ was omitted for the jussive; keeping it is permissible in poetry.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: يا قَوْمِ ادْخُلُوا الْأَرْضَ الْمُقَدَّسَةَ: meaning Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). الْمُقَدَّسَةَ is a naʿt (adjective) of الأرض, i.e. purified of many sins through the great number of prophets in it. الَّتِي كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ: a naʿt, i.e. He decreed for you dwelling in it. وَلا تَرْتَدُّوا عَلى أَدْبارِكُمْ: i.e. do not turn back from obeying Me. فَتَنْقَلِبُوا خاسِرِينَ: the answer to the prohibition.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: قالُوا يا مُوسى إِنَّ فِيها قَوْماً: the noun of «إن». جَبَّارِينَ: a naʿt (adjective), and the khabar (predicate) is in the adverbial phrase. حَتَّى يَخْرُجُوا: accusative by حتى; its nominative is not permissible because it is future.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: قالَ رَجُلانِ: assimilation — assimilating the lām into the rāʾ — is permissible, and a sukūn on the jīm of رجلين is permissible because of the heaviness of the ḍamma. مِنَ الَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ: whoever reads يَخافُونَ [Translator's note: so in the source; the context indicates the passive reading يُخافون is meant] says: they were two of the giants (jabbārūn) on whom Allah bestowed Islam; and whoever reads with a fatḥa on the yāʾ says: they were two of the companions of Moses who feared the giants. On this reading it is also possible that they were of the giants.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: أَبَداً: an adverb of time. فَاذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَرَبُّكَ: conjoined to the pronoun latent in فَاذْهَبْ, because you have emphasised it [with أنت]. According to the Basrans it is ugly to conjoin to a nominative pronoun when you have not emphasised it, because it is like one of the letters of the verb, though it is permissible for them in poetry; according to al-Farrāʾ it is permissible everywhere. إِنَّا هاهُنا قاعِدُونَ: the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; outside the Quran قاعدين is permissible as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the sentence is already complete.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
قالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لا أَمْلِكُ إِلَّا نَفْسِي وَأَخِي: the original form is إنّني; the nūn was omitted because of the cluster of nūns.
وَأَخِي is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to نفسي; or, if you wish, conjoined to the noun of إن. Its position may also be nominative, conjoined to the position [of the noun of إن], or, if you wish, to the latent pronoun. Ibn ʿUyayna reported from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr that he read فَافْرُقْ with a kasra on the rāʾ. The meaning of فَافْرُقْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ الْفاسِقِينَ is: make our abode Paradise, so that there may be a separation between us and them.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: قالَ فَإِنَّها مُحَرَّمَةٌ: the noun of «إن» and its khabar (predicate). The meaning of محرمة is that they are barred from entering it, as one says: "May Allah make your face forbidden to the Fire." أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً: an adverb of time.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: وَاتْلُ: a command, and therefore the wāw has been dropped from it. Allah the Exalted commanded the Prophet ﷺ to recite to the Jews the story of the two sons of Adam when they offered a sacrifice — even though it was with them in the Torah — to teach them that their way in disobeying Allah the Exalted and disbelieving in His Prophet ﷺ is the way of the son of Adam, peace be upon him, and that they are no more honoured before Allah than Adam's own son. In that there was a proof of his prophethood ﷺ, since he had not read the scriptures. As for the statement of ʿAmr Mujāhid [Translator's note: so in the source; probably "the statement of Mujāhid"] that the two who offered a sacrifice were of the Children of Israel, it is a mistake; evidence of that is His words, Mighty and Majestic: لِيُرِيَهُ كَيْفَ يُوارِي سَوْأَةَ أَخِيهِ. قالَ إِنَّما يَتَقَبَّلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ: i.e. from those who guard themselves against acts of disobedience.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ: it may be asked: how can a believer want this? There are two views on this.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad]: this is figurative; since the believer wants the reward and does not stretch out his hand to kill, he is like one who wants this. The other answer is that it is literal: when he said to him "I will surely kill you", he deserved the Fire by this, and Allah the Exalted willed that he be among the people of the Fire, so the believers must want that. As for the meaning of بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ, among the best of what has been said about it — and it is Sībawayh's position — is that the meaning is "with our sin", because the maṣdar (verbal noun) is put in construct with both the agent and the object. Sībawayh reported: "The wealth is between me and between you", i.e. between us, and he recited: [al-Wāfir metre] 120-
فأيّي ما وأيّك كان شرّا
(Whichever of me and whichever of you was the worse …)
i.e. whichever of us. It is also possible that بإثمي means "with the sin of your saying to me: I will surely kill you", and it is possible that the meaning is "with the sin of killing me, if you kill me". فَتَكُونَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ النَّارِ: conjoined. وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:30-31.t:
Abū Wāqid read فطاوعت له نفسه.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is unlikely, because one only says طاوعته نفسه (his soul complied with him).
فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ غُراباً يَبْحَثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ: i.e. He created in it a desire for this. لِيُرِيَهُ: a lām of purpose (lām kay); since its affair ended in this, it was as though it did it in order to show him; it is also possible that the meaning is "so that Allah might show him". If you lighten the hamza [of سوأة] you say سوّة. يا وَيْلَتى: the original form is يا ويلتي; then an alif was substituted for the yāʾ. Al-Ḥasan read يا ويلتي with the yāʾ. The first is more eloquent, because dropping the yāʾ in the vocative is more frequent. Sībawayh's position is that the vocative in these things occurs only for intensification: when you say يا عجبا it is as if you said "O wonder, come, for this is your time", and this is more intense than your saying "this is the time for wonder". يا ويلتا is a word with which the Arabs cry out at destruction; this is Sībawayh's view. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: ويل is remoteness (بعد). [Translator's note: the wording «ويل بعد» is terse in the source; this is one reading of it.] Al-Ḥasan read أَعَجَزْتُ with a kasra on the jīm (أعجِزت); this is an anomalous form, for one only says عجزت [with kasra] of a woman when her buttocks (عجيزة) become large, whereas [the verb of incapacity is] عجزت عن الشيء أعجز عجزا ومعجزة ومعجزة. فَأُوارِيَ: conjoined to أكون; it may also be the answer to the question.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t:
Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read مِنْ أَجْلِ ذلِكَ
with a kasra on the nūn and the hamza dropped; this follows the dialect of those who say إجل, and then the hamza was lightened.
One says: أجلت الشيء آجله أجلا وإجلا when you commit (bring about) it. أَنَّهُ: in the position of an accusative, i.e. "that (بأنّه)", the hāʾ being a pronoun standing for the matter (al-ḥadīth); إنه with a kasra is also permissible, as quotation (ḥikāya), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «انّ». Al-Ḥasan read أو فسادا, i.e. "or did corruption"; it may also be in the sense of a maṣdar, i.e. "or caused corruption (أفسد فسادا)".

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
جَزاءُ: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is أَنْ يُقَتَّلُوا. The implied form [of يحاربون الله ورسوله] is: "those who wage war on the friends of Allah and the followers of His messengers". Al-Ḥasan read أَنْ يُقَتَّلُوا أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوا أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ [Translator's note: the source does not show how al-Ḥasan's reading differs; it is presumably the lightened forms يُقْتَلوا… يُصْلَبوا… تُقْطَع]. The original form is أيديُهم; the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness. ذلِكَ لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ فِي الدُّنْيا: mubtadaʾ and khabar.
وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ: this indicates that the prescribed penalty (ḥadd) does not remove the punishment of the Hereafter from whoever has not repented.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا: in the position of an accusative by exception; it may also be in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being: "except those who repent before you overpower them — فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ [is], to them, غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ."

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَابْتَغُوا إِلَيْهِ الْوَسِيلَةَ.
i.e. by abandoning acts of disobedience, and by jihad.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t:
وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُما. According to Sībawayh the khabar is omitted, the implied form in his view being: "And among what has been prescribed for you: the male thief and the female thief — so cut off their hands." According to the Kufans the nominative is by the returning pronoun. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ in the accusative, and this is Sībawayh's preference. He said: "except that the ʿāmma refused anything but the nominative" — by al-ʿāmma he means the majority. Its accusative is by an implied verb, i.e. "cut off the male thief and the female thief"; he preferred the accusative only because the command is more appropriate with a verb. Sībawayh has been opposed in this: al-Farrāʾ claimed that the nominative is better, because a particular thief is not intended so as to put it in the accusative; rather the meaning is "whoever steals, cut off his hand". This is a good, unrefuted view; evidence for it is that they agreed on reading وَالَّذانِ يَأْتِيانِها مِنْكُمْ فَآذُوهُما [al-Nisāʾ: 16]. This is the position of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad]. As for فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُما, where He did not say يديهما, the grammarians have discussed it. Al-Khalīl said: they wanted to distinguish between that of which a person has one and that of which he has two, so he said: أشبعت بطونها, and إِنْ تَتُوبا إِلَى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما [al-Taḥrīm: 4]. Al-Farrāʾ said: since most of a person's limbs come in pairs, they treated the fewer according to the more numerous. Others said: this was done because the dual is a plural; and it has been said: because it causes no ambiguity. The grammarians permitted the dual, according to the original form, and the singular, because it is understood. Sībawayh permitted the plural in other than this, and reported: وصغار حالهما, meaning the saddles (rahl) of two riding-camels. [Translator's note: the quoted example appears corrupted in the source; it is reproduced as written.]
جَزاءً بِما كَسَبا: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); or, if you wish, a maṣdar (verbal noun); and likewise نَكالًا مِنَ اللَّهِ.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: فَمَنْ تابَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ظُلْمِهِ وَأَصْلَحَ: a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِ.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
لا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ: one also says يحزنك [i.e. يُحزِنك], and the first is more eloquent. مِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا آمَنَّا بِأَفْواهِهِمْ وَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ قُلُوبُهُمْ: i.e. they did not hold faith in their hearts as their tongues spoke it. وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا: this may be the end of the sentence; then He, Mighty and Majestic, said سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ, i.e. "they are listeners"; like it is طَوَّافُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ [al-Nūr: 58]. Al-Farrāʾ said: سمّاعين and طوّافين are permissible, as He said: مَلْعُونِينَ أَيْنَما ثُقِفُوا [al-Aḥzāb: 61], and as He said: إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَعِيمٍ [al-Ṭūr: 17], then said فاكِهِينَ [al-Ṭūr: 18] and آخِذِينَ [al-Dhāriyāt: 26]. It is also possible that the meaning is: "and of those who are Jews are people who listen to falsehood".
سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ: then He said: يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَواضِعِهِ, i.e. they interpret it other than its [true] interpretation after they had understood it from you and known its places which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended. يَقُولُونَ إِنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هذا فَخُذُوهُ: i.e. if you are given this which we told you, accept it. وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ: i.e. if you are forbidden it, فَاحْذَرُوا to accept it from the one who told you, for he is not a prophet — they wanted to show their weak ones that they were advising them sincerely. أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمْ: i.e. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not will to purify their hearts of the stamping and sealing upon them, as He purified the hearts of the believers as a reward for them.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t:
أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ.
[An intensive form] expressing multiplicity. In the language, al-suḥt is everything unlawful that wipes out (yasḥatu) acts of obedience, i.e. removes them. Al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Faḍl reported from Khārija ibn Muṣʿab from Nāfiʿ: أكّالون للسّحت with a fatḥa on the sīn (al-saḥt); this is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of سحته. One says سحت and أسحت with one meaning. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said:
سحته means he removed it little by little.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا التَّوْراةَ فِيها هُدىً وَنُورٌ: «هدى» is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and نور is conjoined to it. وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبارُ: conjoined to النبيين. وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: nominative as mubtadaʾ, and its khabar (predicate) is فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْكافِرُونَ. We have already mentioned its meaning. Among the best of what has been said about it is the statement of al-Shaʿbī, who said: this concerns the Jews specifically. Three things indicate [the correctness of] what he said. First, the Jews were mentioned before this, in His words لِلَّذِينَ هادُوا, so the pronoun refers back to them. Second, the context of the speech indicates that — do you not see that after it comes وَكَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيها, and this pronoun refers to the Jews by consensus? Further, it was the Jews who denied stoning and retaliation. If someone says: «من», when it is conditional, is general unless some evidence for its specification occurs — it is said to him: «من» here is in the sense of الذي, together with the evidences we have mentioned, and the implied form is: "And the Jews who did not judge by what Allah revealed — those are the disbelievers." This is the best of what has been said on this. It has also been said: whoever does not judge by what Allah revealed, considering that lawful. And it has been said: whoever abandons judging by all of what Allah revealed is a disbeliever.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: The verse has [several] aspects: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read all of it in the accusative, and this is clear, by conjunction. It is also permissible to lighten أن and put all of it in the nominative, by the mubtadaʾ (subject) and conjunction. Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū ʿAmr and Abū Jaʿfar read all of it in the accusative except الجروح. Abū Jaʿfar said: Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd related to us from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz from Abū ʿUbayd, who said: Ḥajjāj related to us from Hārūn from ʿAbbād ibn Kathīr from ʿUqayl from al-Zuhrī from Anas that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ read وَكَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيها أَنَّ النَّفْسَ بِالنَّفْسِ وَالْعَيْنَ بِالْعَيْنِ وَالْأَنْفَ بِالْأَنْفِ وَالْأُذُنَ بِالْأُذُنِ وَالسِّنَّ بِالسِّنِّ وَالْجُرُوحَ قِصاصٌ. The nominative is from three aspects: by mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate); according to the meaning, because the meaning is "We said to them: the life for the life"; and the third aspect, stated by Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj]: it is conjoined to the latent pronoun. فَمَنْ تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَهُ: a condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); outside the Quran فمن اصّدّق به is permissible.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: وَقَفَّيْنا عَلى آثارِهِمْ بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ مُصَدِّقاً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). فِيهِ هُدىً: in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). وَنُورٌ: conjoined to it. وَمُصَدِّقاً: there are two aspects to it. It may refer to ʿĪsā ﷺ, and we conjoin it to the first مصدّق; or it may refer to the Gospel, the implied form being: "and We gave him the Gospel, there being in it guidance and light, and confirming". وَهُدىً وَمَوْعِظَةً: conjoined to مصدّق.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ الْإِنْجِيلِ: a command; a kasra on the lām with the jussive is also permissible, because the lām is originally with kasra. There is an omission in the speech, the meaning being: "and We commanded its people to judge بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ", and this was omitted. Al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ الْإِنْجِيلِ [i.e. ولِيَحكمَ] taking it as the lām of purpose (lām kay); the command is more fitting, and the context of the speech indicates it. Abū Jaʿfar said: the correct view in my opinion is that they are two good readings, because Allah the Exalted did not reveal a book except for what is in it to be acted upon, and He commanded acting upon what is in it, so both are sound. If it is the lām kay, there is an omission in the speech, i.e. "and so that the people of the Gospel may judge by what Allah revealed in it, We revealed it to them".

nahhas-irab:48-48.t:
وَأَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ بِالْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقاً: a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَمُهَيْمِناً: conjoined to it. لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنا مِنْكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهاجاً: it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: al-shirʿa and al-minhāj are Islam and the Sunna. It has been said:
al-shirʿa is the beginning of the thing, which is saying "There is no god but Allah", and al-minhāj is the totality of the obligations. And it has been said: they are one thing. Among the best of what has been said about it is that al-sharīʿa and al-shirʿa are one, and it is what is manifest of the religion, taken by hearing [revelation], such as prayer, zakat and what resembles them. From it comes "I opened (ashraʿtu) a door onto the road"; from it شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا; from it إِذْ تَأْتِيهِمْ حِيتانُهُمْ يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ شُرَّعاً [al-Aʿrāf: 163]; from it "a thoroughfare (ṭarīq shāriʿ)"; and from it al-shirāʿ (the sail). Al-minhāj is the clear, evident, straight road. So He made a law and a clear road, i.e. a clear proof. By this He indicated that the law of Muhammad ﷺ differs from the law of Moses ﷺ. لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً: i.e. He would have made your law one.
وَلكِنْ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي ما: there is an omission in the speech to which the lām kay is attached, i.e. "but He made your laws different in order to test you", i.e. to make you worship Him. آتاكُمْ فَاسْتَبِقُوا: i.e. race to the good deeds before you become incapable of them, or die, or their time passes.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t:
وَأَنِ احْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: He had given him a choice before this, and the choice was abrogated by the obligation. The evidence that this abrogates, and that the imam must judge the People of the Book by the truth, is His words: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَداءَ لِلَّهِ [al-Nisāʾ: 35]. [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Nisāʾ 135.] وَأَنِ احْكُمْ: «أن» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to الكتاب, i.e. "and We revealed to you that you judge between them by what Allah revealed", i.e. by the ruling of Allah which He revealed to you in His Book. وَاحْذَرْهُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنُوكَ: the hāʾ and mīm are in the position of an accusative. This must be according to the view of those who say حاذر; it may also be according to the view of those who say
حذر, in Sībawayh's view, and he recited: [al-Kāmil metre] 121-
حذر أمورا لا تضير وآمن ... ما ليس منجيه من الأقدار
(Wary of things that do no harm, and feeling safe from what will not save him from the decrees of fate.)
أَنْ يَفْتِنُوكَ: a badal (substitute); or, if you wish, in the sense of "lest (من أن) they tempt you away".

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: أَفَحُكْمَ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ: accusative by يبغون. The meaning is that the people of the Jāhiliyya used to make the ruling for the noble different from the ruling for the lowly, and the Jews used to apply the prescribed penalties to the weak and poor and not apply them to the strong and rich, so they resembled the Jāhiliyya by this practice. وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). مِنَ اللَّهِ حُكْماً: as explanation (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)].

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: لا تَتَّخِذُوا الْيَهُودَ وَالنَّصارى أَوْلِياءَ: two objects. Taking them as allies means supporting them against the Muslims and favouring them to the exclusion of [the Muslims]. بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ مِنْكُمْ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْهُمْ: i.e. because he has opposed Allah the Exalted and His Messenger as they opposed [them], and enmity towards him has become obligatory as enmity towards them is obligatory, and the Fire has become due for him as it is due for them; so he has become one of them, i.e. one of their fellows.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: فَتَرَى الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ يُسارِعُونَ فِيهِمْ: i.e. in befriending them. فَعَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِالْفَتْحِ: i.e. with victory; it is accusative by أن. فَيُصْبِحُوا: conjoined, i.e. they become regretful of having befriended the disbelievers, when they see Allah's, Mighty and Majestic, victory for the believers, and when they see with their own eyes at death and are given the tidings of punishment.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
The people of Medina and the people of Syria read «يا أيها الذين آمنوا» [Translator's note: so in the source; what is meant is يقول الذين آمنوا] without a wāw, in the nominative because it is an imperfect (future) verb. Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا with the wāw and the accusative, conjoined to «أن يأتي» according to most grammarians. If it is on this basis, the accusative is unlikely, because it is like your saying: "Perhaps Zayd will come and ʿAmr will stand" (عسى زيد أن يأتي ويقوم عمرو). This is very unlikely; the meaning "perhaps Zayd that ʿAmr stands" is not sound. But if you said: "Perhaps Zayd will stand and ʿAmr come" (عسى أن يقوم زيد ويأتي عمرو), it would be good. Had the verse been "عسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح", the accusative would have been fine; its permissibility is by construing it according to this meaning, like his words: [Majzūʾ al-Kāmil metre] 122-
ورأيت زوجك في الوغا ... متقلّدا سيفا ورمحا
(And I saw your husband in the fray, girded with a sword and a spear.)
There is another view: you conjoin it to الفتح, as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir metre] 123-
للبس عباءة وتقرّ عيني ... أحبّ إليّ من لبس الشّفوف
(Wearing a coarse cloak, with my eye content, is dearer to me than wearing fine sheer garments.)
The Kufans read وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا in the nominative, cut off (resumed) from what precedes. أَهؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ لَمَعَكُمْ: i.e. they said "they are…"; أنّهم is permissible by أقسموا; إنّهم … and أنّهم is permissible by أقسموا. [Translator's note: the source repeats the phrase «إنّهم ويجوز أنّهم بأقسموا» twice, apparently a copying error.] فَأَصْبَحُوا خاسِرِينَ: i.e. losers of the reward.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: يا أيّها الذين آمنوا من يرتدد منك عن دينه: this is the reading of the people of Medina and the people of Syria. [Translator's note: «منك» is so in the source, for منكم.] The people of Kufa and the people of Basra read مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ with a fatḥa on the dāl because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; a kasra on it is also permissible, but the fatḥa was chosen because it is lighter. The Kufans said: it has a fatḥa because it was built by analogy with your saying ردّا; and for this reason, according to al-Farrāʾ, the past verb has a fatḥa. يرتدد is better, because the second letter is quiescent. فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ: in the position of a naʿt (adjective). أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: a naʿt, i.e. they are gentle with them and show them mercy. أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ: they are harsh with them and show them enmity. «أذلّة» in the accusative is also permissible, as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He loves them and they love Him in this state. يُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلا يَخافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لائِمٍ: by this He indicated the confirmation of the imamate of Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them, because they are the ones who strove for Allah during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and after his death. ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَاللَّهُ واسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ: i.e. vast in bounty, knowing of what is good for His creation.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: إِنَّما وَلِيُّكُمُ اللَّهُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَرَسُولُهُ: conjoined. وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: likewise; then He described them, saying: الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned that Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī Abū Jaʿfar was asked about the meaning of إِنَّما وَلِيُّكُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا — is it ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him? He said: "ʿAlī is among the believers", holding that this is for all the believers. This is a clear view, because الذين is for the body of the believers, and this concerns the believers' befriending one another; it has nothing to do with the imamate. Evidence of that is that this befriending was during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The meaning of يقيمون الصلاة is that they perform it at its times with all its rights, as one says: "so-and-so is upholding (qāʾim bi-) his work".

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject). It has been said that the khabar (predicate) is omitted, the implied form being: "and whoever takes Allah, His Messenger and those who believe as allies is of the party of Allah"; and it has been said: هُمُ is the khabar and الْغالِبُونَ is a second khabar.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَكُمْ هُزُواً وَلَعِباً مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَالْكُفَّارَ أَوْلِياءَ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (57) يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَكُمْ هُزُواً وَلَعِباً: this is the reading of the people of Medina. The people of Kufa read
هزؤا, dropping the ḍamma because of its heaviness. If you lighten the hamza according to the reading of the people of Medina, you change it into a wāw and say «هزوا»; and if you lighten it according to the reading of the people of Kufa, you say «هزا», like «هدى». مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَالْكُفَّارَ أَوْلِياءَ: this is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and the people of Kufa, i.e. "and do not take the disbelievers as allies". Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read وَالْكُفَّارَ أَوْلِياءَ [Translator's note: their reading is the genitive والكفارِ, though the source prints the same vowelling] in the sense of "and of the disbelievers"; مِنَ here is for clarifying the genus. The accusative is clearer and more evident.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: هَلْ تَنْقِمُونَ مِنَّا: the lām may be assimilated into the tāʾ because of its closeness to it. إِلَّا أَنْ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ: in the position of an accusative, i.e. "do you resent anything in us except our believing in Him", when you know that we are upon the truth, and [you know] your own transgression in abandoning faith.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: قُلْ هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذلِكَ: i.e. of something worse than your resentment against us; and it has been said: than the worst of the harm you wish for us. مَثُوبَةً: as explanation (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)]. Its original form is mafʿūla; the vowel of the wāw was cast onto the thāʾ, so the wāw became quiescent, followed by a quiescent wāw, and one of them was omitted. مَنْ لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ: in the position of a nominative, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذلِكُمُ النَّارُ [al-Ḥajj: 72], the implied form being: "it is the curse of whom Allah cursed". It may be in the position of an accusative, in the sense of "Say: shall I inform you of whom Allah cursed"; and it may be in the position of a genitive, as a badal (substitute) for شرّ. We have [already] mentioned وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ and the readings of it. On the reading of al-Aʿmash, وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ is permissible with the ḍamma dropped because of its heaviness; and on the reading of Ḥamza, وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ is permissible, also with the ḍamma dropped, and with its accusative as censure (ʿalā al-dhamm); or, if you wish, it is accusative in the sense of "and He made of them", i.e. described them thus. The nominative is permissible in the sense of "and they are", and the genitive is permissible, conjoined to مِنْ when it is in the position of a genitive. أُولئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكاناً: it may be said: there is no evil in the believers, so how does أولئك شرّ مكانا come? There are [several] answers to this. The Kufans reported: "Honey is sweeter than vinegar", though this is rejected. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is "those are worse in position according to your claim". Among the best of what has been said about it: "those whom Allah has cursed are worse in position in the Hereafter than your position in this world, because of the evil that has befallen you". It has been said: "those whom Allah has forgotten are worse than those who resented you"; and it has been said: "those who resented you are worse than those whom Allah has cursed".

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: وَقَدْ دَخَلُوا: i.e. with hatred for the Prophet ﷺ and the believers and wishing for their destruction, and they went out still harbouring it. وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما كانُوا يَكْتُمُونَ: of disbelief.

nahhas-irab:64-64.t:
غُلَّتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ: the noun of that whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent); the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness; i.e. they will be fettered in the Hereafter. It may also be an imprecation against them; likewise وَلُعِنُوا بِما قالُوا. بَلْ يَداهُ مَبْسُوطَتانِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
Al-Akhfash said: in the reading of ʿAbdullāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is بل يداه بسطان. Al-Akhfash said: one says يد بسطة, i.e. free and outstretched. وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ: a lām of oath. كُلَّما أَوْقَدُوا ناراً: an adverb, i.e. whenever they gathered and prepared.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ: «أن» is in the position of a nominative; likewise وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ.

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: يا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ: i.e. all that has been revealed from your Lord. وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ: a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) [follows]. فَما بَلَّغْتَ رِسالَتَهُ: this is the reading of the people of Medina [Translator's note: their reading is the plural رسالاته, as the following words show]; Abū ʿAmr, the people of Kufa and al-Kisāʾī read (رسالته) in the singular. Both readings are good, except that the plural is clearer, because revelation used to come down to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ piece by piece, and then he would make it clear. وَاللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النَّاسِ: a proof of the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed that he is protected. In this verse there is a proof refuting the view of whoever said that the Prophet ﷺ concealed something of the religion out of precaution (taqiyya), and a proof that he did not confide anything of the religion secretly to anyone, because the meaning is "convey openly all that has been revealed to you"; were it not for this, there would be no benefit in His words, Mighty and Majestic: وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَما بَلَّغْتَ رِسالَتَهُ.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: the noun of إن. وَالَّذِينَ هادُوا: conjoined to it. وَالصَّابِئُونَ: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read والصابئين in the accusative. The implied form is: "Those who believe and those who are Jews — whoever of them believes in Allah and does good, they have their reward — and the Sabians and the Christians likewise." Sībawayh recited — and it is a parallel to this: [al-Wāfir metre] 124-
وإلّا فاعلموا أنّا وأنتم ... بغاة ما بقينا في شقاق
(Otherwise, know that we and you are transgressors as long as we remain in discord.)
Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash — he mentioned it in «al-Masāʾil al-Kabīr» — said: «الصابئون» is conjoined to the pronoun latent in هادوا. Al-Farrāʾ said: the nominative is permissible only because the case inflection does not show in الذين. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] say, when the view of al-Akhfash and al-Kisāʾī was mentioned to him: this is wrong in two respects. First, it is ugly to conjoin to a nominative pronoun until it is emphasised. The other respect is that the conjoined shares in [the ruling of] what it is conjoined to, so the meaning would become: "the Sabians have entered Judaism", which is absurd. And the course of what does not show its inflection and what does show it is one and the same.

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: فَرِيقاً كَذَّبُوا: i.e. they called a party liars; and likewise وَفَرِيقاً يَقْتُلُونَ.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t:
وَحَسِبُوا أَلَّا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ: this is the reading of the Kufans, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī [Translator's note: i.e. with the nominative تكونُ; the source prints the same vowelling for both readings]; the people of the two Sanctuaries read it in the accusative. Sībawayh said: "حسبت أن لا تقول ذاك (I reckoned that you would not say that), i.e. I reckoned that it [is so]." He said: "And if you wish, you may use the accusative." Abū Jaʿfar said: according to the grammarians the nominative with حسبت and its sisters is better, as Imruʾ al-Qays said: [al-Ṭawīl metre] 125-
ألا زعمت بسباسة اليوم أنّني ... كبرت وأن لا يشهد اللهو أمثالي
(Lo, Basbāsa claimed today that I have grown old, and that the likes of me do not attend amusement.)
The nominative became better only because حسبت and its sisters are like knowledge in that [their object] is something established; the accusative is permissible only if you treat them like خشيت and خفت. This is Sībawayh's view on the accusative.
فِتْنَةٌ: the noun of تكون. Fitna is testing; if it is used for anything else, that is figurative. The meaning is: "and they reckoned there would be no punishment". فَعَمُوا وَصَمُّوا ثُمَّ تابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ: He did not say
عمي وصمّ (in the singular), though the verb comes first. There are [several] answers to this. Among them: كثير منهم is a badal (substitute) for the wāw.
Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: as you say "I saw your people, two thirds of them". Or, if you wish, it is with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the blind and deaf among them are many". A fourth answer: it is according to the dialect of those who say أكلوني البراغيث ("the fleas ate me", with the plural marker on the verb).
Al-Akhfash said: this may be of that [kind], and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl metre] 126-
ولكن ديافيّ أبوه وأمّه ... بحوران يعصرن السليط أقاربه
(But he is a man of Dayāf, his father and mother; in Ḥawrān his kinsfolk press the oil.)
Outside the Quran كثيرا in the accusative is permissible, as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:72-72.t: لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ: this is the view of the Jacobites (al-Yaʿqūbiyya). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refuted it against them with a decisive proof from what they themselves acknowledge, saying: وَقالَ الْمَسِيحُ يا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ, i.e. if the Messiah says "O Lord" and "O Allah", how could he be calling upon himself, or how could he be asking himself? This is absurd.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ ثالِثُ ثَلاثَةٍ وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ إِلاَّ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ (73) لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ ثالِثُ ثَلاثَةٍ: this means "one of three", and tanwīn is not permissible in it; but if you say ثالث اثنين ("the third of two", i.e. making two into three), tanwīn is permissible. وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ إِلَّا إِلهٌ واحِدٌ: (من) is redundant (zāʾida). Outside the Quran إلا إلها واحدا is permissible, by exception. Al-Kisāʾī permitted the genitive as a badal (substitute), and that is an error according to al-Farrāʾ and the Basrans, because «من» does not enter an affirmative statement.

nahhas-irab:75-76.t:
مَا الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. even though the Messiah ﷺ displayed signs, he only brought them as the messengers brought them. وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ: mubtadaʾ and khabar. كانا يَأْكُلانِ الطَّعامَ: i.e. since they ate food, they relieved themselves; Allah the Exalted alluded to that indirectly, and in this there is evidence that they were both human beings. Allah the Exalted said: انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ الْآياتِ ثُمَّ انْظُرْ أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ, i.e. how they are turned away from the truth after this clarification. Then He added to the clarification for them, saying:
قُلْ أَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا نَفْعاً.
i.e. you acknowledge that ʿĪsā was a foetus in his mother's womb, possessing no power to harm or benefit anyone. وَاللَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ: i.e. you have acknowledged that ʿĪsā was, in one of his states, not hearing and not knowing, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has always been Hearing, Knowing.

nahhas-irab:77-77.t: قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لا تَغْلُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ: i.e. do not go to excess as the Jews and the Christians went to excess regarding ʿĪsā. وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا أَهْواءَ قَوْمٍ: the plural of هوى; this is how the defective noun (maqṣūr) is pluralised, on the pattern of its sound counterpart. It has been said: [it is called] هوى because it brings its owner down (yahwī) into falsehood.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t:
لُعِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: the noun of that whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent); some Arabs say الّذون.
عَلى لِسانِ داوُدَ وَعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ: i.e. He commanded that they be cursed, so We cursed them. داود, peace be upon him, is diptote because it is a foreign name to which the alif and lām [the article] are not well suited; if the alif and lām suit such a word, it is fully declined, like طاوس and راقود. ذلِكَ: in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "that curse [was]" بِما عَصَوْا. It may also be with an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is that"; and it may be in the position of an accusative, i.e. "We did that to them because of their disobedience and their transgression".

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: كانُوا لا يَتَناهَوْنَ: nominative because it is an imperfect verb, and it is in the position of an accusative because it is the khabar (predicate) of كان. لَبِئْسَ: a lām of emphasis. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is "evil indeed, as a thing, is their deed".

nahhas-irab:80-80.t: تَرى كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: they are the Jews; they used to ally themselves with the idolaters, though they were not of their religion. لَبِئْسَ ما قَدَّمَتْ لَهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ أَنْ سَخِطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ: (أن) is in the position of a nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); and it has been said: a badal (substitute) for what is in «لبئس ما». It may also be in the position of an accusative in the sense of "because (لأن) Allah was angry". وَفِي الْعَذابِ هُمْ خالِدُونَ: mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:81-81.t: By this He indicated that whoever takes a disbeliever as an ally is not a believer.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t:
لَتَجِدَنَّ: a lām of oath; and the nūn entered, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, to distinguish between the present and the future. أَشَدَّ النَّاسِ عَداوَةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الْيَهُودَ: two objects, and عَداوَةً is as explanation (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)]; likewise وَلَتَجِدَنَّ أَقْرَبَهُمْ مَوَدَّةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الَّذِينَ قالُوا إِنَّا نَصارى. There are two views on this. One is that they were not truly Christians — and it is not possible that Allah the Exalted would praise a disbeliever — but were only a people who believed in ʿĪsā and did not say that he was a god, so they were called Christians before they embraced Islam. The other view is that the meaning is: "those who said 'We are Christians'". ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ مِنْهُمْ قِسِّيسِينَ: the noun of أن. In the broken plural of قسيس one says قساوسة, a wāw having been substituted for one of the two sīns. One also says قسّ in the same sense, its plural being قسوس; and slander is also called قسّ: "he spread (qassa) the talk, qassan". ورهبانا: the plural of راهب; its verb is رهب الله يرهب, i.e. he feared Him, [maṣdar] رهبا, رهبانا and رهبة. Abū ʿUbayd said: رهبان is also said for the singular.
Al-Farrāʾ said: its plural is رهابنة and رهابين. وَأَنَّهُمْ: in the position of a genitive, by conjunction.

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: Sībawayh permitted the jussive with إذا in poetry. تَفِيضُ: in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); likewise (يقولون).

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: وَما لَنا لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ: in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. what [reason] do we have, in this state?

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: in the position of a nominative, a naʿt (adjective) of أي. لا تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّباتِ ما أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ: jussive (majzūm) by the prohibition, and therefore the nūn has been dropped from it; likewise وَلا تَعْتَدُوا.

nahhas-irab:88-88.t: وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ: in the position of an accusative, a naʿt (adjective). [Translator's note: so in the source; what is described as an accusative naʿt is evidently الَّذِي (of Allah) in الَّذِي أَنْتُمْ بِهِ مُؤْمِنُونَ.] أَنْتُمْ: mubtadaʾ (subject); مُؤْمِنُونَ: khabar (predicate); and the two are the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, the hāʾ in (به) referring back to it.

nahhas-irab:89-89.t:
Abū ʿAmr and the people of Medina read وَلكِنْ يُؤاخِذُكُمْ بِما عَقَّدْتُمُ الْأَيْمانَ with the doubled form, and the people of Kufa and al-Kisāʾī read بما عقدتم with the light form. Abū ʿUbayd rejected the doubled form. He said:
because it is for repetition; and he claimed to fear that whoever reads it would be bound to say that expiation is not obligatory until one has sworn several times. He said: and this is outside what people hold. Abū Jaʿfar said: this does not follow. There are two views on the doubled form. Abū ʿAmr said: عقّدتم means وكّدتم (you made firm); just as you say وكّدتم, so you say عقّدتم; and the meaning of "I bound (ʿaqadtu) the oath" and "I made it firm" is that the swearer swears to something neither mistaken nor forgetful. And it has been said: عقّدتم because it is for a group. فَكَفَّارَتُهُ إِطْعامُ عَشَرَةِ مَساكِينَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It is permissible to give إطعام tanwīn and put عشرة in the accusative, without tanwīn and with tanwīn, مَساكِينَ then being in the position of an accusative as a badal (substitute). مِنْ أَوْسَطِ ما تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ: what is clear in this is that what you feed is neither the finest nor the lowest. كِسْوَتُهُمْ is in the position of an accusative, the sign of the accusative in it being the yāʾ, and the nūn was dropped for the construct. [Translator's note: so in the source; this remark belongs to أَهْلِيكُمْ, not to كسوتهم.] أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ: conjoined to إطعام; likewise أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ. «أو تحرير رقبة» is also permissible [Translator's note: the variant vowelling is not shown in the source]; and likewise فَصِيامُ ثَلاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ, the implied form being "then upon him is". ذلِكَ كَفَّارَةُ أَيْمانِكُمْ: mubtadaʾ and khabar; the implied form is "when you swear and break [the oath]", then it was omitted. وَاحْفَظُوا أَيْمانَكُمْ: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded guarding oaths and not treating them lightly to the point that they are forgotten, so that one remembers them and fulfils what is due in them of expiation or otherwise. كَذلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آياتِهِ: the kāf is in the position of an accusative, i.e. He makes His signs clear to you with a clarification like what He made clear to you about the expiation of the oath.

nahhas-irab:90-90.t: إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنْصابُ وَالْأَزْلامُ رِجْسٌ: khamr, for the Arabs, is grape juice when it has become strong. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every intoxicant is khamr", thereby giving it the status of what the Arabs knew as khamr. Al-anṣāb are the idols and al-azlām the divining arrows; the implied form is "and the use of the azlām". رِجْسٌ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject). Rijs, for the Arabs, is every deed that is ugly to do; its verb is رجس يرجس and رجس يرجس. Al-rajs, with a fatḥa on the rāʾ and a sukūn on the jīm, is sound (noise). The verb from al-maysir is يسر ييسر, so he is ياسر and يسر. فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ: it may mean "avoid the rijs", or "avoid this deed", or it may refer to one of these things, the rest being included in what it is included in.

nahhas-irab:93-93.t: لَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جُناحٌ فِيما طَعِمُوا: i.e. of the lawful; إِذا مَا اتَّقَوْا indicates this. As for the repetition in His words إِذا مَا اتَّقَوْا ثُمَّ اتَّقَوْا, there are several views on it. Among them: the meaning is "when they guarded against disbelief, then believed and did good deeds, then guarded against acts of disobedience, then guarded against wronging people"; وَآمَنُوا indicates this. It has been said: "when they were godfearing in the past" — «إذا» being suitable for the past by implying كانوا — "then were godfearing in the present, then godfearing in the future". It has been said: إذا اتقوا is for the present, ثُمَّ اتَّقَوْا for the future, and ثم اتقوا [the third] means they persisted in godfearing. And it has been said: "when they guarded against disbelief, then guarded against the major sins, then guarded against the minor sins".

nahhas-irab:94-94.t: لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ اللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ: a lām of oath. Concerning the entry of «من» there are three answers. It may be for clarifying the genus, as you say: "I will surely test you with something of gold", and as Sībawayh said: "This is the chapter of knowing what words are in Arabic (هذا باب علم ما الكلم من العربيّة)". «من» may also be partitive, because what is forbidden is land game specifically; and it may be partitive because game is forbidden only during iḥrām specifically. The singular of الحرم is حرام, i.e. muḥrim; and muḥrim applies in two ways: one by ḥajj or ʿumra, and the other in that one says أحرم when he enters the Sanctuary (al-Ḥaram). لِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ: a lām of purpose (lām kay).

nahhas-irab:95-95.t:
وَمَنْ قَتَلَهُ مِنْكُمْ مُتَعَمِّداً: a condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَجَزاءٌ مِثْلُ ما قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ. This is the reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr; the people of Kufa read فَجَزاءٌ مِثْلُ ما قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ. [Translator's note: the source prints the same vowelling for both; the Medinan reading is the construct فجزاءُ مثلِ and the Kufan one فجزاءٌ مثلُ.] Hārūn ibn Ḥātim reported from Ibn ʿAyyāsh from ʿĀṣim فَجَزاءٌ مِثْلُ ما قَتَلَ with «مثل» in the accusative.
Al-Kisāʾī said: in the reading (ḥarf) of ʿAbdullāh it is فجزاؤه مثل ما قتل. The reading of the Medinans and Abū ʿAmr is in the sense of "then upon him is a recompense like what he killed". This may also be [the sense] on the reading of the Kufans, «مثل» then being a naʿt (adjective) of جزاء; and «جزاء» may be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being «مثل ما قتل», the meaning being "the recompense of his deed is the like of what he killed". Whoever puts «مثلا» in the accusative, its implied form is "then it is upon him to recompense the like of what he killed".
يَحْكُمُ بِهِ ذَوا عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ: the dual of ذو according to the original form. هَدْياً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «به»; it may also be as explanation (bayān), and it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Aʿraj read هديّا with a doubled yāʾ, and it is an eloquent dialectal form. بالِغَ الْكَعْبَةِ: its original form is بالغا الكعبة, because it is a naʿt of an indefinite noun.
أَوْ كَفَّارَةٌ طَعامُ مَساكِينَ: this is the reading of the people of Medina, with the construct of the genus; and the reading of Abū ʿAmr and the people of Kufa is أَوْ كَفَّارَةٌ طَعامُ مَساكِينَ. [Translator's note: again the source prints the same vowelling; the Medinan reading is كفارةُ طعامِ and the other كفارةٌ طعامُ.] Abū ʿUbayd said: because the food is the expiation; according to the Basrans it is a badal (substitute). أَوْ كَفَّارَةٌ is conjoined to جزاء, i.e. "or upon him is an expiation".
أَوْ عَدْلُ ذلِكَ: we have [already] mentioned it. صِياماً: as explanation (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)]. لِيَذُوقَ: with the lām of purpose (lām kay). وَمَنْ عادَ: in the position of a jussive by the condition, except that it is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. فَيَنْتَقِمُ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ: an imperfect verb, and in it is the apodosis of the condition.

nahhas-irab:96-96.t: أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَحْرِ: the noun of that whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). وَطَعامُهُ: conjoined to it. We have mentioned its meaning; among the best of what has been said about it is that Allah the Exalted made lawful the game of the sea and eating it. It has been said: its food is the water, because it is tasted. Ibn ʿAbbās read وطعمه with a ḍamma on the ṭāʾ and a sukūn on the ʿayn. مَتاعاً: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of "this has been made lawful for you" is "you have been given enjoyment of it, an enjoyment"; its parallel is كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ [al-Nisāʾ: 24]. ما دمتم حرما: one also says «دمتم» [i.e. dimtum], and the ḍamma is more eloquent.

nahhas-irab:97-97.t: جَعَلَ اللَّهُ الْكَعْبَةَ: first object; it was called Kaʿba because of the squareness of its top. الْبَيْتَ الْحَرامَ: a badal (substitute). قيما: second object. Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read قِياماً لِلنَّاسِ. [Translator's note: so in the source; the attribution seems reversed, since Ibn ʿĀmir is known for قيما.] Both are from roots with wāw, and the wāw was changed into yāʾ because of the kasra before it; قوام has also been said. وَالشَّهْرَ الْحَرامَ وَالْهَدْيَ وَالْقَلائِدَ: conjoined. لِتَعْلَمُوا: in the position of a nominative, i.e. "the matter is that"; it may also be in the position of an accusative, i.e. "Allah did that". أَنَّ: a lām of purpose (lām kay). [Translator's note: so in the source; this label belongs to the lām of لِتَعْلَمُوا.] أَنَّ اللَّهَ: in the position of an accusative.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t:
أَشْياءَ: diptote, and the grammarians have [several] views on it. Al-Khalīl, Sībawayh — may Allah have mercy on them — and al-Māzinī said: its original form is faʿlāʾ, شيئاء; two hamzas with an alif between them were felt to be heavy, so the first was shifted [before the root], and it became [the pattern] lafʿāʾ. Al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayd said: it is diptote because it resembles حمراء, since the Arabs say
أشياوات, like حمراوات. Al-Akhfash, al-Farrāʾ
and al-Ziyādī said: it is diptote because it is afʿilāʾ, أشيئاء, on the pattern of أشيعاع, as one says هين and أهوناء. Abū Ḥātim said: أشياء is afʿāl, like أنباء, and it ought to be fully declined, except that it was heard from the Arabs undeclined (ghayr maṣrūfa), so the grammarians devised contrivances for it that are not sound. Abū Jaʿfar said: the soundest of these views is that of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and al-Māzinī. Al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayd are bound not to decline أسماء and أبناء, because one says of them أبناوات and أسماوات. Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭabarī the grammarian, known as Ibn Rustum, related to me from Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī, who said:
I said to al-Akhfash: "How do you form the diminutive of أشياء?" He said: "أشياء [i.e. أُشَيّاء]." I said to him: "According to your view you must form the diminutive of the singular and then pluralise it", and he was silenced. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a clear argument, because if أشياء were afʿilāʾ it could not be made diminutive until it was returned to the singular; furthermore, faʿl is not pluralised as afʿilāʾ. As for its being afʿāl, according to Abū Ḥātim's view, that is impossible, because afʿāl is not barred from full declension, and nothing is barred from full declension without a cause. The implied form is: "Do not ask about things that Allah has pardoned, which if made plain to you would trouble you." The best of what has been said about this is what Abū Hurayra, may Allah have mercy on him, reported: that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ:
"Who is my father?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَسْئَلُوا عَنْ أَشْياءَ إِنْ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ. The meaning on this basis is: do not ask about concealed things which Allah has pardoned through repentance, which if made plain to you would trouble you; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew that what was good for them was that they not ask about them.
