"اَلسّائِبَةُ": when a man made a vow for (his) return from a journey, or recovery from an illness, or the like, he would say: "This she-camel of mine is sāʾiba (let loose)", and she was like the baḥīra in that no benefit was taken from her, she was not driven away from water, and she was not kept from pasture. And when a man freed a slave, he would say: "He is sāʾiba", and then there was no blood-money liability (ʿaql) between them, nor inheritance. As for "اَلْوَصِيلَةُ", it is among sheep: when a ewe bore a female, it was theirs, and when she bore a male and a female, they said: "She has joined (وَصَلَتْ) her brother", so they did not slaughter the male for their gods. As for "اَلْحامِي", it is the male among camels: when ten litters had been born from the stallion's loins, the Arabs would protect (حُمِيَ) his back, so no load was put on him, and he was not kept from water or pasture. So Allah made known that He had not forbidden anything of these things, and that those who disbelieve fabricated (it) against Allah.

zajjaj:105-105.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا عَلَيْكم أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾: its meaning is: Allah has only made you responsible for the affair of your own selves.
﴿لا يَضُرُّكم مَن ضَلَّ إذا اهْتَدَيْتُمْ﴾, that is: Allah will not hold you accountable for the sins of others. The wording of this verse does not require abandoning commanding the right and forbidding the wrong; He made known that the disbelief of the disbeliever does not harm the believer. But if the believer abandons commanding the right while he is able to do so, he is astray and not rightly guided. The i'rab of "لا يَضُرُّكم مَن ضَلَّ": the best is that it be nominative (indicative), as a statement (khabar), the meaning being: "the one who strays does not harm you if you are rightly guided". It may be that its position is jussive (jazm), the original being "لا يَضْرُرْكم", except that the first rāʾ was assimilated into the second, and the second was given ḍamma because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. In Arabic, by way of prohibition, "لا يَضُرَّكم" with fatḥa on the rāʾ and "لا يَضُرِّكم" with kasra are permissible, but the (established) recitation is not to be contradicted, and also because the ḍamma is better, whether the position is nominative or jussive. As for whoever gives ḍamma for the meeting of two quiescents, he makes the ḍamma follow the ḍamma; as for whoever gives kasra, it is because kasra is the basic (vowel) for the meeting of two quiescents; and as for whoever gives fatḥa, he gives fatḥa for the meeting of two quiescents because of the lightness of fatḥa. This prohibition is in the wording of the absent (third person) while those addressed are meant: when you say "لا يَضْرُرْكَ كُفْرُ الكافِرِ" (let not the disbeliever's disbelief harm you), the meaning is: "do not count his disbelief as harm"; just as when you say "لا أرَيَنَّكَ هَهُنا" (let me not see you here), the prohibition in the wording is to yourself, but its meaning is to the one you address; its meaning is: "do not be here".

zajjaj:106-106.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا شَهادَةُ بَيْنِكم إذا حَضَرَ أحَدَكُمُ المَوْتُ حِينَ الوَصِيَّةِ اثْنانِ ذَوا عَدْلٍ مِنكُمْ﴾: its meaning is that the testimony at the time of the bequest is for (the case of) death — not that death is present to him while he makes his bequest — by what the testator says, whether he is healthy or not healthy: "When death comes to me — or when I die — then do (such)... and carry out (such)...". "Testimony" is nominative from two aspects. One of them is that it is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is "اِثْنانِ", the meaning being: "The testimony of this situation is the testimony of two"; then "شَهادَةُ" is omitted and "اِثْنانِ" stands in its place.
And the nominative of "شَهادَةُ بَيْنِكم" may be according to (the sense of) His saying: "and among what Allah has prescribed for you regarding your testimony is that two should testify", so "اِثْنانِ" is made nominative by "شَهادَةُ", the meaning being: "that two upright men from among you should testify". Regarding the meaning of "مِنكم", two views were stated. Some said: "مِنكم" means: from the people of your religion, ﴿أوْ آخَرانِ مِن غَيْرِكُمْ﴾: from other than the people of your religion. Others said: "ذَوا عَدْلٍ مِنكم" means: from the family of the deceased, "أوْ آخَرانِ مِن غَيْرِكم": from other than the family of the deceased. These argued that His saying ﴿فَيُقْسِمانِ بِاللَّهِ إنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ لا نَشْتَرِي بِهِ ثَمَنًا ولَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى﴾ indicates that "مِنكم" means: from those of your kinship. These said: also, when they are upright and of the kin of the deceased, they are more fitting, because they know the circumstances of the family better than strangers do, and know better what is good for them. They also argued that ﴿ذَوا عَدْلٍ﴾ (two upright men) cannot be from other than the people of the religion of Islam, because disbelief has put (one) far from uprightness. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that the two witnesses of a bequest ought to be two upright men from the family of the deceased or from other than his family, if the testator is resident; and likewise if he is on a journey. For His saying ﴿إنْ أنْتُمْ ضَرَبْتُمْ في الأرْضِ فَأصابَتْكم مُصِيبَةُ المَوْتِ﴾ mentions death on a journey after His saying ﴿إذا حَضَرَ أحَدَكُمُ المَوْتُ حِينَ الوَصِيَّةِ﴾; so it is as though there is in the verse — and Allah knows best — an indication regarding testimony both when resident and on a journey. It has come in the tafsīr that two non-Muslims had testified on a journey; and (against this) there is the consensus that witnesses are not required to swear. Some have permitted the testimony of two dhimmīs on a journey. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَأشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنكم وأقِيمُوا الشَّهادَةَ لِلَّهِ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 2], and said: ﴿مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ الشُّهَداءِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 282]. When a witness is known to be a liar, it is not permissible to accept his testimony; and we know that the Christians claimed that Allah is the third of three, and that the Jews said that ʿUzayr is the son of Allah, and we know that they are liars; so how can the testimony of one who persists in lying be accepted? As for the meaning of His saying ﴿تَحْبِسُونَهُما مِن بَعْدِ الصَّلاةِ فَيُقْسِمانِ بِاللَّهِ﴾: people in the Ḥijāz used to swear (oaths) after the ʿAṣr prayer, because it is the time when people gather.
His saying: ﴿إنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ﴾: if doubt about them occurs in your souls, that is: you suspect them of something doubtful.

zajjaj:107-107.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإنْ عُثِرَ عَلى أنَّهُما اسْتَحَقّا إثْمًا﴾, that is: if it is discovered that they have both acted treacherously, ﴿فَآخَرانِ يَقُومانِ مَقامَهُما مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الأوْلَيانِ﴾. It has been read "اَلْأوَّلِينَ", and "مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الأوْلَيانِ" is permissible [Translator's note: so in the text; a different vocalisation, e.g. the passive «اسْتُحِقَّ», is presumably meant]. This is one of the most difficult places in the Quran as regards i'rab. "أوْلَيانِ", according to the view of most of the Basrans, are nominative as a badal (substitute) of what is in "يَقُومانِ" (its pronoun); the meaning is: "Let the two nearest to the deceased stand in the place of these two treacherous ones", and they swear by Allah: our testimony is truer than their testimony.
When "اَلْأوْلَيانِ" is nominative as a badal, then what is in "اِسْتَحَقَّ" of the pronoun has the sense of the bequest; the meaning is: "Let the two nearest stand, from those against whom the bequest has become due, or against whom the bequeathing has become due". Some said: the meaning of "مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الأوْلَيانِ" is: "it has become due among them (فِيهِمْ)", "عَلى" standing in place of "في", just as "في" stood in place of "عَلى" in His saying: ﴿وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكم في جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 71], meaning: on the trunks of the palm trees. And some said: the meaning of "عَلى" in "مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الأوْلَيانِ" is (that of "مِن"), as He said: ﴿الَّذِينَ إذا اكْتالُوا عَلى النّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 2], that is: when they take measure from people. And it was said: in "اِسْتَحَقَّ" there is reference to the sin, because in His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَإنْ عُثِرَ عَلى أنَّهُما اسْتَحَقّا إثْمًا فَآخَرانِ يَقُومانِ مَقامَهُما مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الأوْلَيانِ﴾ the meaning was: "those against whom the sin was committed". And it was said that "اَلْأوْلَيانِ" may be nominative by "اِسْتَحَقَّ", their meaning being: "the two most entitled to the oath", that is: to making those who testify after them swear. If the testimony of the two Christians is permissible, then "اَلْأوْلَيانِ" on this view are "the two Christians", or the other two from outside the household of the deceased. The best of these views is that "اَلْأوْلَيانِ" be a badal, with the meaning: "Let the two nearest stand, from those against whom the bequest has become due". Whoever read "اَلْأوَّلِينَ" referred it back to "اَلَّذِينَ", and the meaning was: "from those first ones against whom the bequeathing has become due". The one who read so argued, saying: what do you think if the two nearest were minors?

zajjaj:108-108.t: His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ أدْنى أنْ يَأْتُوا بِالشَّهادَةِ عَلى وجْهِها﴾, that is: that is nearer to bringing the testimony in its proper form, and nearer to their fearing.

zajjaj:109-109.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ الرُّسُلَ فَيَقُولُ ماذا أُجِبْتُمْ﴾: as for the accusative of "يَوْمَ", it is construed with His saying: ﴿واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ واسْمَعُوا﴾ [al-Māʾida: 108], that is: and fear the Day on which Allah will gather the messengers, as He said: ﴿واتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 48]. The meaning of the questioning of the messengers by Allah the Exalted is by way of rebuke to those to whom they were sent, as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَإذا المَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 8] ﴿بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 9]: she is only asked so that her killers may be rebuked. As for the messengers' answer and their saying "لا عِلْمَ لَنا" (we have no knowledge), people have said more than one thing about this. It has come in some of the tafsīr that their understanding left them because of the terror of the Day of Resurrection, so they said: "We have no knowledge alongside Your knowledge". Some said: had their understanding left them, they would not have said: ﴿إنَّكَ أنْتَ عَلامُ الغُيُوبِ﴾. And some said: the meaning of the messengers' saying "لا عِلْمَ لَنا" is: (we have no knowledge) of what was hidden from us of those to whom we were sent; You, our Lord, know their inner selves, and we do not know what is hidden of them; ﴿إنَّكَ أنْتَ عَلّامُ الغُيُوبِ﴾.

zajjaj:110-110.t:
His saying: ﴿إذْ قالَ اللَّهُ يا عِيسى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ اذْكُرْ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكَ وعَلى والِدَتِكَ﴾: as for His favour upon his mother, it is that He chose her, purified her and chose her above the women of the worlds, and her provision used to come to her from Him while she was in her sanctuary (miḥrāb).
His saying: ﴿إذْ أيَّدْتُكَ بِرُوحِ القُدُسِ﴾, that is: I supported you with Jibrīl. It is possible that He strengthened him with him when the Children of Israel attempted to kill him, and it is possible that He supported him with him in all his circumstances, because there is an indication of that in the speech.
His saying: ﴿تُكَلِّمُ النّاسَ في المَهْدِ﴾, that is: I supported you, (you) speaking to people in the cradle; ﴿وَكَهْلا﴾, that is: I supported you as a man of mature age. And it is possible that "وَكَهْلًا" is construed with "تُكَلِّمُ", the meaning being: I supported you, addressing people in your infancy and addressing people as a man of mature age. Some read "أأْيَدْتُكَ" on the pattern "أفْعَلْتُكَ", from "اَلْأيْدُ" (strength), and some read "آيَدْتُكَ" on the pattern "فاعَلْتُكَ", that is: I aided you.
His saying: ﴿وَتُبْرِئُ الأكْمَهَ والأبْرَصَ بِإذْنِي﴾: "اَلْأكْمَهُ" — some said: the one who is born blind. Al-Khalīl said: it is the one who is born blind, and it is the one who becomes blind after having been sighted.

zajjaj:111-111.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإذْ أوْحَيْتُ إلى الحَوارِيِّينَ أنْ آمِنُوا بِي وبِرَسُولِي﴾: some said: "أوْحَيْتُ إلى الحَوارِيِّينَ" means: I inspired them, as He said: ﴿وَأوْحى رَبُّكَ إلى النَّحْلِ أنِ اتَّخِذِي مِنَ الجِبالِ بُيُوتًا﴾ [al-Naḥl: 68], that is: He inspired it. Some said: "أوْحَيْتُ إلى الحَوارِيِّينَ" means: He commanded them; and they recited the poet's saying:
؎اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي استَهَلَّتْ ∗∗∗ بِإذْنِهِ السَّماءُ واطْمَأنَّتْ
أوْحى لَها القَرارَ فاسْتَقَرَّتْ
(Praise be to Allah, by whose leave the sky poured down rain and then became still; He commanded it to settle, and it settled.)
They said: its meaning is: He commanded it. And some said: the meaning of "وَإذْ أوْحَيْتُ إلى الحَوارِيِّينَ" is: I brought them, in the revelation to you, the proofs and signs by which they inferred (the way) to faith, so they believed in Me.

zajjaj:112-112.t:
His saying: ﴿إذْ قالَ الحَوارِيُّونَ يا عِيسى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ﴾: it is possible that the position of "عِيسى" is accusative, as you say "يا زَيْدَ بْنَ عَمْرٍو", because when "اِبْنٌ" is annexed to a known proper name, or annexed to a known kunya (agnomen), it and what precedes it are treated as a single thing. All the grammarians choose "يا زَيْدَ بْنَ عَمْرٍو", and all of them permit "يا زَيْدُ بْنَ عَمْرٍو"; accordingly, the position of "عِيسى" may be the position of a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma. They all said: if you say "يا زَيْدُ ابْنَ أخِينا" (O Zayd, son of our brother) and "يا زَيْدُ ابْنَ الرَّجُلِ الصّالِحِ" (O Zayd, son of the righteous man), you give "زَيْدًا" ḍamma and nothing else, because the accusative only occurs when "اِبْنٌ" is annexed to a proper name, as we described. It has been read "هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ رَبَّكَ" and ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ﴾. Whoever read "هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ رَبَّكَ", the meaning is: "Can you call for His response and His compliance in sending down to us...?" And whoever read it "هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ", its meaning was: "Is your Lord able?" Abū Isḥāq [Translator's note: al-Zajjāj himself] said: the meaning in my view — and Allah knows best — is not that they were ignorant that Allah is able to send down a table, but the thrust of the question is: "Will you show us that your Lord will show us what we have asked, for your sake, of your signs which indicate your prophethood?" As for "اَلْمائِدَةُ", Abū ʿUbayda said: in meaning it is "مَفْعُولَةٌ" (passive participle) while its wording is "فاعِلَةٌ" (active participle); he said: it is like ﴿عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 21]. And he said: al-māʾida is from giving, and "اَلْمُمْتادُ" is the iftaʿala form, the one from whom giving is sought. The poet said:
؎إنِّي أمِيرُ المُؤْمِنِينَ المُمْتادْ
(I am the Commander of the Faithful, the one from whom bounty is sought.)
And "مادَ زَيْدٌ عَمْرًا" (Zayd gave to ʿAmr) when he gave to him. The origin of "مائِدَةٌ" in my view is that it is "فاعِلَةٌ" from "مادَ، يَمِيدُ" when it moves, as though it sways with what is on it. It was said in the tafsīr that it was sent down upon them on Sunday, and on it were bread and fish; so the Christians make Sunday a feast — according to what was said — because of that. Some said that it was not sent down, because of the tahawwud [Translator's note: so in the text («لِلتَّهَوُّدِ»); perhaps «التَّهْدِيدِ», "the threat", is meant] that occurred regarding disbelief after its sending down. The more likely is that it was (sent down), because its sending down is mentioned in this story; Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿إنِّي مُنَـزِّلُها عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 115]. And non-Muslims said that it was sent down, and the reports (about it) have reached (us), so believing in it is obligatory. As for the reason for the disciples' asking ʿĪsā for the table, it bears two aspects: one of them is that they sought to increase in firmness, as Ibrāhīm said: ﴿رَبِّ أرِنِي كَيْفَ تُحْيِ المَوْتى﴾ [al-Baqara: 260]; and it is possible that their asking for the table was before their knowing that he had healed the one born blind and the leper and that he had brought the dead to life. As for ʿĪsā's saying to the disciples: اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ (fear Allah if you are believers), he only commanded them not to propose signs themselves, and not to put themselves forward before Allah and His Messenger, because Allah had shown them the signs and proofs through the bringing of the dead to life, and that is more conclusive than what they asked for and sought.

zajjaj:114-114.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ عِيسى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنا﴾: Sībawayh mentioned that "اَللَّهُمَّ" is like an interjection (ṣawt), and that it does not take a qualifier, and that "رَبَّنا" is accusative by another vocative. We have explained this before in full. The meaning of His saying ﴿وَآيَةً مِنكَ﴾ is: so that it may be for us a sign from You.

zajjaj:115-115.t: As for His saying: ﴿فَإنِّي أُعَذِّبُهُ عَذابًا لا أُعَذِّبُهُ أحَدًا مِنَ العالَمِينَ﴾, it is possible that He hastens the punishment for them in this world, and it is possible that it is in the Hereafter, because of His saying: ﴿لا أُعَذِّبُهُ أحَدًا مِنَ العالَمِينَ﴾.

zajjaj:116-116.t: His saying: ﴿أأنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وأُمِّيَ إلَهَيْنِ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾: the questioning here is by way of rebuke to those who made claims against him, because they are agreed that he is truthful in what he reports and that he does not lie to them, and he is the truthful one in their view; so that is more conclusive as an argument against them and more effective in rebuking them, and rebuke is a kind of punishment. ﴿قالَ سُبْحانَكَ﴾, that is: You are free of evil. ﴿ما يَكُونُ لِي أنْ أقُولَ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ﴾. As for His saying: ﴿تَعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِي ولا أعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِكَ إنَّكَ أنْتَ عَلامُ الغُيُوبِ﴾: "اَلْغِيُوبِ" (is said) with kasra and with ḍamma. Abū Isḥāq said: this is a place — I mean "تَعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِي ولا أعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِكَ" — with which the heretics confuse those whose knowledge of the language is weak, and the reality of it is known only from the language. The lexicographers said: "اَلنَّفْسُ" in the speech of the Arabs is used in two ways. One of them is your saying: "خَرَجَتْ نَفْسُ فُلانٍ" (so-and-so's soul departed) and "في نَفْسِ فُلانٍ أنْ يَفْعَلَ كَذا وكَذا" (it is in so-and-so's mind to do such-and-such). The other way: the meaning of "اَلنَّفْسُ" in it is the totality of the thing and the reality of the thing: "قَتَلَ فُلانٌ نَفْسَهُ" (so-and-so killed himself) and "أهْلَكَ فُلانٌ نَفْسَهُ" (so-and-so destroyed himself) — its meaning is not that the destruction fell upon part of him; the destruction fell only upon his entire self, and upon his reality. The meaning of "تَعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِي" is: "You know what I conceal", "وَلا أعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِكَ": "I do not know what is in Your reality, and that of which I have no knowledge". So the interpretation is: You know what I know, and I do not know what You know; and indicating this is ﴿إنَّكَ أنْتَ عَلامُ الغُيُوبِ﴾, for it refers back to the point concerning what is known, and to the emphasis that no one knows the unseen except Allah — exalted be His praise.

zajjaj:117-117.t: His saying: ﴿أنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي ورَبَّكُمْ﴾: it is possible that "أنْ" is in the sense of "أيْ" (that is), explicative; the meaning being: "I said to them only what You commanded me, that is: worship...". It is possible that "أنْ" is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ (pronoun), "أنْ" being connected (in a ṣila) with "اُعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ", its meaning being: "except what You commanded me, (namely) that they worship Allah". And it is possible that its position is accusative as a badal of "ما", the meaning being: "I said nothing to them except: worship Allah", that is: "I mentioned to them nothing but the worship of Allah".

zajjaj:118-118.t: His saying: ﴿إنْ تُعَذِّبْهم فَإنَّهم عِبادُكَ وإنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهم فَإنَّكَ أنْتَ العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾: the meaning of the saying of ʿĪsā — upon him be peace — "وَإنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهم": the people of reasoning differed in explaining ʿĪsā's saying "وَإنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهم". Some said: its meaning is: "If You forgive them their lying against me"; and they said: it is not permissible for ʿĪsā — upon him be peace — to say: "Allah may forgive disbelief"; so on this view it is as though (he said): "If You forgive them the report (they made) only". This is the view of Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [Translator's note: al-Mubarrad], and I do not know: is it something he heard, or did he deduce it? What I hold — and Allah knows best — is that ʿĪsā knew that among them were some who believed and some who persisted in disbelief, so ʿĪsā said about them collectively: "If You punish them", that is: "If You punish those of them who disbelieved, they are Your servants and You are just toward them, because You made the truth clear to them and they disbelieved after the argument against them had become binding; and if You forgive those of them who desisted and believed, that is a bounty from You, because it was within Your right not to accept them and not to forgive them after their enormous fabrication; and You, in Your forgiving them, are Mighty — nothing You will is beyond You — and Wise in that". Some people said: it is possible that Allah had not informed ʿĪsā that He does not forgive shirk (associating partners with Him). This is a view not worth attending to, because His saying — Exalted is He —: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 48] does not single out anyone of the community of Muḥammad ﷺ to the exclusion of others, because this is a statement of fact (khabar), and a statement of fact is not abrogated. This view came up in debate, and it is not something that anyone whose knowledge is trusted believes.
